VTj3YBDwJi.one_liner: Recovers both players' incentives in zero-sum stopping games from one continuation-value solve, then certifies equilibrium globally.
VTj3YBDwJi.problem: Given demonstrations of which player stopped and where, the terminal incentives rationalizing both players' decisions are unknown, and local boundary matching ignores that both decisions share one continuation value.
VTj3YBDwJi.method: Solves once for the common continuation value between the observed boundaries, recovers both incentives from its boundary values, and applies a global double-obstacle verification step to rule out profitable deviations; dynamics uncertainty is propagated into admissible transfer and value sets.
VTj3YBDwJi.key_idea: Smooth-fit conditions at the observed boundaries let one continuation-value solve yield both incentives, followed by a global saddle-point check.
VTj3YBDwJi.evidence: Necessity, sufficiency, and uniqueness results within a smooth-fit class, plus 24 synthetic games comparing direct recovery with adaptive calibration and a stopping-action IRL baseline, and volatility-uncertainty propagation experiments.
VTj3YBDwJi.claimed_gains: Direct recovery matches converged adaptive calibration across 24 synthetic games without repeated game solves, and each sixteenfold increase in data reduces mean transfer width by about 75% (abstract cut off).
VTj3YBDwJi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the inverse stopping-game formulation is well motivated and the construction is elegant and computationally efficient, with a verification step that goes beyond local boundary matching.
VTj3YBDwJi.main_concern: Assumptions are restrictive (known base payoffs, scalar diffusion, two separated boundaries, exact first-hit behavior) with limited robustness to misspecification, and the finite-sample certification uses a Gaussian one-step model with discretely observed paths.

zYteQwPojW.one_liner: Trains language models with a label-free RL objective to generate text that maximally activates a given residual-stream direction.
zYteQwPojW.problem: Interpreting a residual-stream direction by scanning a corpus for activating text is limited to what the corpus contains.
zYteQwPojW.method: Maximally-Activating Example Metamodels (MAEMs) map a residual-stream direction of a subject model to text exemplars and are trained with RL to maximize the cosine similarity between the direction and the activations of the generated text.
zYteQwPojW.key_idea: Reward a metamodel with the subject model's own cosine similarity between generated-text activations and the target direction, so every exemplar is verifiable with one forward pass.
zYteQwPojW.evidence: A Qwen3.6-27B MAEM compared with corpus search, a natural-language autoencoder (NLA), GCG and EPO on held-out activations, languages and domains, SAE features, steering vectors and LoRA backdoor payloads.
zYteQwPojW.claimed_gains: A Qwen3.6-27B MAEM beats corpus search (at 10M tokens) on a majority of held-out languages and domains, activates 89% of held-out SAE features, and recovers LoRA backdoor payloads more often than corpus search.
zYteQwPojW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the label-free, verifiable training objective is well motivated, broadly applicable across direction types and domains, and gives strong results over corpus search.
zYteQwPojW.main_concern: Experiments cover mainly one model and layer with unreported training cost, and it is unclear that maximally activating text alone conveys the direction's semantics.

92X16tBT1B.one_liner: LangPatch aligns GenePT gene representations with verbalized electrophysiology profiles via a frozen text encoder and contrastive learning.
92X16tBT1B.problem: Building multimodal neuroscience foundation models requires integrating transcriptomic and electrophysiological data, for which Patch-seq provides paired measurements from the same neuron.
92X16tBT1B.method: Gene descriptions and verbalized electrophysiological profiles are embedded by the same frozen text encoder, and a context adapter and projection modules connect the modalities through paired contrastive learning on Patch-seq data.
92X16tBT1B.key_idea: Use language as a shared interface: embed gene descriptions and verbalized ephys profiles with one frozen text encoder and align them with paired contrastive learning.
92X16tBT1B.evidence: Mouse visual, mouse motor, and human cortical Patch-seq cohorts, compared with foundation-model and representation-learning baselines including JAMIE, on transcriptome-to-electrophysiology prediction, cross-modal alignment, and transfer.
92X16tBT1B.claimed_gains: FOSCTTM is 0.107 in visual cortex and 0.135 in motor cortex versus 0.208 and 0.222 for JAMIE, and LangPatch has the highest mean transcriptome-to-electrophysiology prediction correlation among the evaluated methods.
92X16tBT1B.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evaluation is broad (forward prediction, cell-identity readout, cross-modal alignment, cross-area and cross-species transfer) and the held-out alignment results are promising.
92X16tBT1B.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited and ablations are missing, notably whether verbalization and the shared text embedding matter versus an MLP on quintile-binned features or numeric ephys embeddings.

mffDk4xhj4.one_liner: R-DiT repeats shared Transformer blocks within each denoising step, adding recursion depth as a diffusion compute-scaling axis.
mffDk4xhj4.problem: Scaling diffusion by more sampling steps has diminishing returns, and larger denoisers cost more parameters and memory.
mffDk4xhj4.method: R-DiT refines hidden representations by repeatedly applying shared Transformer blocks, adds recursion modulation that conditions the denoiser on both diffusion time and recursion time, and uses adaptive recursion to allocate recursion across the denoising trajectory under a fixed compute budget.
mffDk4xhj4.key_idea: Reuse shared blocks recursively inside each denoising step, condition on diffusion and recursion time jointly, and allocate recursion depth across timesteps under a fixed budget.
mffDk4xhj4.evidence: Experiments across image, language and molecular diffusion against standard diffusion Transformers, with ablations of the design choices.
mffDk4xhj4.claimed_gains: Reports a significantly better quality-compute-parameter trade-off than standard diffusion Transformers across image, language and molecular diffusion; the abstract gives no numbers.
mffDk4xhj4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clear writing, the three-axis compute-scaling framing, and the breadth across images, text and molecules, with design choices backed by ablations.
mffDk4xhj4.main_concern: Efficiency evidence is incomplete or possibly unfair: no latency or memory analysis despite added recursion cost, unclear CFG tuning (FID worsens as sampling steps increase in Table 1), and no direct comparison with prior recursive-sharing work ELT.

CikiwAduFB.one_liner: CARE learns a consensus predictor, then residual view-specific corrections around it, retaining the consensus as incumbent during model selection.
CikiwAduFB.problem: In incomplete multi-view multi-label classification, coupling consensus learning with view-specific extraction lets complementary updates perturb the shared predictor, which under sparse supervision can compromise reliable consensus.
CikiwAduFB.method: A two-stage framework: stage one builds a consensus predictor through cross-view fusion guided by label semantics, and stage two anchors it and learns residual refinements around it. A theoretical analysis characterizes when residual updates help and relates retained gains to conditional complementary information, approximation error, and selection uncertainty.
CikiwAduFB.key_idea: Anchor a consensus predictor and learn only residual corrections around it, keeping the original consensus as an incumbent candidate during model selection.
CikiwAduFB.evidence: Experiments on six benchmark datasets against competing methods, adaptation of four existing methods on two datasets, paired-stage and component ablations, and a synthetic experiment.
CikiwAduFB.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims superiority over competing methods on six benchmark datasets without numbers).
CikiwAduFB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation clear, the method simple and easy to follow, and the framework reusable, with the highest reported AP and AUC on six benchmarks and gains when adapting four existing methods.
CikiwAduFB.main_concern: Theory and practice diverge and evidence is thin: the theory assumes sample selection independent of candidate construction while experiments select both on the same validation set, hyperparameters are many, and transfer is shown on only two datasets.

f0b2AnYdEE.one_liner: NVWA generates free-topology, riggable 3D humans from one image using native 3D supervision and soft rigging correspondence fields.
f0b2AnYdEE.problem: Single-image 3D human generation faces limited native 3D data, multi-view or video supervision that causes cross-view inconsistency, and parametric templates like SMPL that cannot model loose clothing or accessories.
f0b2AnYdEE.method: NVWA trains on large-scale synthesized explicit 3D human assets for direct native 3D supervision, and uses soft rigging: the model jointly generates free-form volumetric geometry and a spatially aligned semantic correspondence field giving per-vertex correspondence to a standard rigging template.
f0b2AnYdEE.key_idea: Generate free-form geometry together with a semantic correspondence field to a rigging template, decoupling shape from template topology while keeping pose controllability.
f0b2AnYdEE.evidence: Reconstruction comparisons on X-Humans against baselines, trained on the NVWA-100K textured human mesh dataset; the abstract is truncated before the results.
f0b2AnYdEE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the soft-rigging design, which separates generated free-topology geometry from template topology via SMPL-X-referenced semantic UV correspondences, is well motivated and balances geometric expressiveness with animation readiness.
f0b2AnYdEE.main_concern: The native-3D-supervision benefit is weakened because NVWA-100K is built with PSHuman's multi-view pipeline and may inherit its artifacts, and soft rigging lacks quantitative rigging and animation evaluation and comparison with rigging methods.

LItgrMuRr8.one_liner: Aligns hidden states of chemically equivalent molecular serializations along a shared suffix with a margin contrastive objective.
LItgrMuRr8.problem: Autoregressive molecular models score serializations of the same molecule separately, so chemically equivalent histories can induce different internal states along a shared continuation, and randomized strings do not supervise their correspondence.
LItgrMuRr8.method: SIGMA builds chemically certified same-suffix triplets (two equivalent histories, one non-equivalent history, shared suffix) and adds a dense suffix-position objective that aligns corresponding pre-token hidden states and enforces a finite similarity margin over the non-equivalent history. The language-model objective, decoder, and inference procedure are unchanged.
LItgrMuRr8.key_idea: Supervise per-position hidden-state correspondence across chemically equivalent serializations using certified same-suffix triplets with a margin against a non-equivalent history.
LItgrMuRr8.evidence: Comparison with canonical training, randomized-serialization training, and last-token alignment on four datasets under SMILES and SELFIES with three training seeds, plus position-wise analyses and full-corpus ZINC ablations under both representations.
LItgrMuRr8.claimed_gains: Lowers test-reference Frechet ChemNet Distance against every control in all three training seeds on all four SELFIES datasets and on QM9 and ZINC under SMILES.
LItgrMuRr8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the chemically verified triplet construction is a principled way to supervise intermediate states and that experiments over multiple datasets and representations with ablations are informative.
LItgrMuRr8.main_concern: Stronger augmentation baselines (resampled serializations) are missing and the gains are unclear relative to roughly 4x training time, and SIGMA also loses to last-token alignment on SAFE.

PewlqJRkEt.one_liner: Solvable two-layer linear network under SGD shows growing curvature and minibatch noise feedback govern scaling laws and hyperparameter behavior.
PewlqJRkEt.problem: Solvable scaling-law models are mostly linear with fixed curvature, so they cannot capture how growing curvature interacts with minibatch noise and the hyperparameter phenomena that depend on it.
PewlqJRkEt.method: They analyze a two-layer linear network trained with SGD on a power-law task and derive how feature learning ties the kernel scale to the norm of the learned function so curvature grows. The growing kernel amplifies minibatch noise until noise self-stabilizes at a fraction of the stochastic edge of stability.
PewlqJRkEt.key_idea: Kernel scale grows with the norm of the learned function (progressive sharpening), amplifying minibatch noise until it self-stabilizes below the stochastic edge of stability.
PewlqJRkEt.evidence: Analytical derivations on a minimal nonlinear (scalar-gated) model with numerical checks across task spectra, model sizes, and training settings, plus qualitative agreement with observations in real networks.
PewlqJRkEt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that a single feedback mechanism between progressive sharpening and minibatch noise explains several training phenomena, with quantitative predictions that simulations confirm.
PewlqJRkEt.main_concern: The results rest on uncontrolled approximations (a single kernel scale, fast noise-covariance adjustment) and are tested almost only on this simple model, with limited evidence for real networks.

koUcOtZD0e.one_liner: Fine-tunes monitors on one caught collusion behavior, then measures transfer to four unseen behaviors in Llama and Qwen model organisms.
koUcOtZD0e.problem: When a model monitors a copy of itself in AI control it may collude to cover up misbehavior, and it is unknown whether training on caught collusion also removes collusion the control team has not found.
koUcOtZD0e.method: They fine-tune Llama-3.3-70B and Qwen2.5-72B to install five policy-monitor behaviour pairs, correct the monitor on 300 honest reviews of one caught collusion, and measure collusion on the other four behaviors in unseen prompt formats, comparing four correction methods.
koUcOtZD0e.key_idea: Correct the monitor on honest reviews of a single caught collusion behavior and test whether that correction generalizes to other installed collusion behaviors.
koUcOtZD0e.evidence: Three seeds each of Llama-3.3-70B and Qwen2.5-72B model organisms, four correction methods, a control fine-tuned on unrelated examples, and checks of control-item accuracy and capability.
koUcOtZD0e.claimed_gains: Correction reduces held-out collusion from 91% to 14-20% under three of four methods, versus 56-93% for the unrelated-data control, with family-average control-item accuracy changing by at most five points.
koUcOtZD0e.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the study shows a substantial corrective-transfer effect under controlled conditions across two model families on a practically relevant question.
koUcOtZD0e.main_concern: Training on clean reviews or generic honesty data also removes 78-83% of held-out collusion, so how much transfer depends on the specific caught behavior is unclear, and the artificially installed behaviors may limit applicability.

eJ4ECWeHZp.one_liner: Sparse-DETR variant using local feature geometry to correct deformable sampling locations and task-calibrated decoder attention to select encoder tokens.
eJ4ECWeHZp.problem: Sparse detection transformers allocate encoder updates by aggregate attention demand, which can favor already well-represented regions, and queries may read local features and locate boundaries poorly.
eJ4ECWeHZp.method: Local Manifold-Aligned Attention (LMAA) uses a direction-magnitude descriptor and its induced local geometry to correct query-predicted sampling locations, then aggregates by content compatibility. Joint Boundary Refinement predicts four box-side residuals, and TDAM uses matched-instance demand to supervise encoder token selection with restricted reranking.
eJ4ECWeHZp.key_idea: Correct deformable-attention sampling offsets using local feature-space geometry, and supervise encoder token selection with matched-instance decoder demand.
eJ4ECWeHZp.evidence: COCO experiments with ResNet-50 and Swin-T backbones across encoder keeping ratios of 10%-50% after 50 training epochs, compared against Sparse-DETR, plus component ablations.
eJ4ECWeHZp.claimed_gains: Improves over Sparse-DETR by 2.1-2.8 AP with ResNet-50 across keeping ratios of 10%-50%, and at a 10% keeping ratio reaches 48.9 AP with ResNet-50 and 50.8 AP with Swin-T, surpassing Sparse-DETR at 50% while updating one fifth as many encoder tokens.
eJ4ECWeHZp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using local feature geometry to refine sampling locations is a useful idea and that AP gains over Sparse-DETR are reasonably consistent across update ratios.
eJ4ECWeHZp.main_concern: Adding LMAA raises inference latency from 27.18 ms to 58.67 ms for a gain from 46.8 to 47.9 AP, leaving the practical accuracy-latency trade-off unclear.

eNGsbYDNl4.one_liner: Benchmark of 2,000 instruction-based audio editing samples across sound, speech, and music, scored by decomposed rubric criteria.
eNGsbYDNl4.problem: Evaluation infrastructure for instruction-based audio editing is fragmented and limited to specific subdomains or basic operations.
eNGsbYDNl4.method: MMAE spans 7 audio modalities with a taxonomy of 6 task-complexity levels, 2 granularity levels, and 8 operation types, curated through human-agent collaboration into 2,000 samples. Free-form tasks are decomposed into 17,741 verifiable rubric criteria that assess instruction following and context consistency.
eNGsbYDNl4.key_idea: Decompose each free-form editing instruction into verifiable rubric criteria that an automated judge scores for instruction following and context consistency.
eNGsbYDNl4.evidence: Evaluation of leading audio editing models (including MMEdit, Audio-Omni, SmartDJ, Step-Audio-EditX, and Ming-UniAudio) with Identity and Gaussian Noise reference baselines, scored by a Qwen3-Omni judge.
eNGsbYDNl4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a timely, broad benchmark covering multiple audio modalities, operation types, and complexity levels with a thoughtful data curation pipeline.
eNGsbYDNl4.main_concern: The Qwen3-Omni rubric judge is not validated against human listeners, and models are compared on different sample subsets (801 versus 2,000 samples).

0zS4j0rxSb.one_liner: Graph regularizer that smooths second-stage CATE predictions over pairs with similar first-stage plug-in CATE estimates.
0zS4j0rxSb.problem: In two-stage CATE learning, second-stage targets depend on noisy nuisance estimates, and it is unclear how first-stage CATE estimates should select which observations to regularize together.
0zS4j0rxSb.method: NEAR builds a fixed graph (a mutual top-K graph per reviews) from first-stage plug-in CATE estimates and regularizes second-stage CATE predictions over pairs with similar plug-in CATEs, leaving the learner's base loss unchanged. They derive finite-sample CATE risk bounds for squared-loss second-stage regression using a stabilized doubly robust pseudo-outcome.
0zS4j0rxSb.key_idea: Select regularization pairs by similarity of first-stage plug-in CATE estimates rather than covariates, and penalize second-stage prediction differences over that fixed graph.
0zS4j0rxSb.evidence: Experiments across six two-stage learners and three benchmarks, graph-support comparisons, perturbation diagnostics, ablations, and finite-sample risk bounds.
0zS4j0rxSb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple and well motivated, using plug-in CATE similarity rather than covariate proximity, and that the experiments, including ablations of graph construction and edge weighting, are well organized.
0zS4j0rxSb.main_concern: Novelty is limited because the method mainly adapts standard graph Laplacian regularization to CATE estimation, and its distinctions from related work such as HERMES and LITE are not clearly articulated.

TPYXWFUIhp.one_liner: Mesh-to-CAD recovery combining learned feature proposals, geometric parameter fitting, and subset dynamic-programming search over operation order.
TPYXWFUIhp.problem: Geometry-driven mesh-to-CAD methods rely on weak design priors and give feature decompositions inconsistent with the original modeling logic, while learned models struggle with precise parameter recovery.
TPYXWFUIhp.method: A learned proposal model identifies feature-level surface evidence and Boolean roles from the mesh, and a geometry-based stage recovers continuous parameters to form executable parametric features. A learned feature prior ranks and filters candidates, and combinatorial search selects and orders them into a modeling history, with unresolved residuals handled recursively.
TPYXWFUIhp.key_idea: Separate discrete feature discovery from continuous parameter fitting, then select and order recovered features by combinatorial (subset dynamic-programming) search, recursing on unexplained residuals.
TPYXWFUIhp.evidence: Per reviews, comparisons against recent baselines including CADENA, CADFit, and cadrille, with ablations of the subset-DP ordering; the visible abstract does not name datasets.
TPYXWFUIhp.claimed_gains: not stated; the visible abstract has no numeric results.
TPYXWFUIhp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the separation of feature discovery, parameter fitting, and joint ordering, the subset-DP formulation, and substantial gains over recent baselines such as CADENA, CADFit, and cadrille.
TPYXWFUIhp.main_concern: The framework supports only extrusion and revolve operations, leaving fillets, chamfers, and lofts unexplored, which limits comparison breadth and industrial applicability.

CByAJ2zQdl.one_liner: Compiles live webpages into addressable information and action objects in a persistent cache, unifying search and browsing for LLM agents.
CByAJ2zQdl.problem: Existing web-access models support either information gathering or browser interaction, and combining them brings substantial cost or performance trade-offs on long-horizon tasks.
CByAJ2zQdl.method: WebCompiler compiles live webpages into addressable information and action objects under a common schema defined by WebContract. The objects are maintained in WebCache and handled through a shared set of operations, giving agents consistent, operable, and persistent web access.
CByAJ2zQdl.key_idea: Compile each page into addressable information and action objects with a shared schema and persistent cache, so one set of operations covers both search and browser actions.
CByAJ2zQdl.evidence: Experiments across web search, web navigation, and further tasks (abstract is cut off), including an ablation linking information and action objects and, per reviews, WebArena and WebWalkerQA evaluations.
CByAJ2zQdl.claimed_gains: not stated; the visible abstract is cut off before results and only claims extensive experiments across web search and web navigation.
CByAJ2zQdl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem practical and the interface design simple and coherent, motivated by a clear quantitative preliminary analysis and evaluated on multiple benchmarks.
CByAJ2zQdl.main_concern: Gains are not cleanly isolated: results are single runs with missing baselines, the compiler extracts extra page-load data that baselines lack, and component ablations are limited.

0imYw5ajm4.one_liner: Sleeper memory poisoning uses adversarial external content to make an assistant store a fabricated memory that later steers conversations
0imYw5ajm4.problem: Persistent memory in LLM assistants creates an attack surface where adversarial content can corrupt what the assistant remembers and influence future interactions after the original context is gone.
0imYw5ajm4.method: An adversary manipulates external context (a document, webpage, or repository) so the assistant stores a fabricated memory about the user. The attack pipeline is evaluated in three stages: whether poisoned memories are written, later retrieved, and used to steer following conversations; reviewers note it builds on actor-critic prompt optimization and embedding-based retrieval.
0imYw5ajm4.key_idea: Inject a fabricated user memory through external content so it stays dormant in persistent memory and re-emerges in later conversations, unlike one-shot prompt injection.
0imYw5ajm4.evidence: Stateful LLM assistants across models and memory frameworks, with attack templates optimized on proxy models and stage-wise measurement of writing, retrieval, and use.
0imYw5ajm4.claimed_gains: Poisoned memories were added up to 99.8% on GPT-5.6 Sol and 95% on Kimi-K2.6, and among successful injections they cause attacker-intended agentic actions in 38-89% of evaluations across models.
0imYw5ajm4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the timely security problem and the end-to-end evaluation that separates memory writing, retrieval, and use, with clearly documented benchmark construction.
0imYw5ajm4.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited since it builds on actor-critic prompt optimization, and experiments lack a no-poison control to isolate the effect of poisoning.

yfkWCScRbj.one_liner: Recursive flow-field distillation and Propose-Resolve align asynchronous VLA action distributions with the original VLA for reactive real-time control
yfkWCScRbj.problem: Asynchronous execution of VLAs avoids pauses between action chunks but, for non-Markovian demonstrations, can produce a different action distribution from the original VLA, limiting reactivity.
yfkWCScRbj.method: Recursive Flow-Field Distillation trains the asynchronous policy using the VLA's action-generation flow. Propose-Resolve prepares multiple action sequences asynchronously and uses the latest observation to select among them with a lightweight approximation of their likelihood under the VLA's action distribution.
yfkWCScRbj.key_idea: Distill the VLA's flow field so the asynchronous policy covers its action distribution, then propose several action sequences early and pick one with the latest observation by approximate VLA likelihood.
yfkWCScRbj.evidence: A theoretical characterization of the learned distribution and a proposition on distribution mismatch, plus robot experiments (SmolVLA per a reviewer) with a support-coverage analysis and a single training seed per configuration.
yfkWCScRbj.claimed_gains: not stated as numbers (the abstract says the asynchronous policy can generate nearly the full range of actions the original VLA would produce, while existing asynchronous methods recover only a fraction)
yfkWCScRbj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the distribution-mismatch argument for non-Markovian demonstrations convincing and the propose-then-resolve design practical, resembling speculative decoding.
yfkWCScRbj.main_concern: Propose-Resolve may not handle multimodal policies and adds inference cost, and higher success rates do not clearly show improved reactivity or an aligned final action distribution.

8PehJKSMDt.one_liner: WellLogBench and WellLog-LLM: an expert-reviewed well-log QA benchmark and a DPO/GRPO-trained model using compact lithology-aware contexts
8PehJKSMDt.problem: Well-log interpretation requires reasoning over long, multivariate, depth-indexed measurements, and how well LLMs handle it is largely unknown.
8PehJKSMDt.method: Builds WellLogBench (1,075 validated QA pairs across six petrophysical categories and three reasoning levels), the Petrophys library that turns million-token LAS logs into compact lithology-aware contexts, and Dynamic Feature Selection. WellLog-LLM is trained with DPO and GRPO and refined at inference by Group Relative Context Optimization.
8PehJKSMDt.key_idea: Convert raw depth-indexed logs into compact, lithology-aware structured contexts with reproducible calculations, prune them by feature selection, and post-train with DPO and GRPO plus inference-time context optimization.
8PehJKSMDt.evidence: 15 evaluated LLMs and VLMs on public and private splits, with stage-wise ablations, judge-agreement analysis, and statistical comparisons per reviewers.
8PehJKSMDt.claimed_gains: Dynamic Feature Selection cuts the supplied context by 73.5%; GPT-5.6 Luna (high) leads at 70.4 and 69.3 Overall, and WellLog-LLM reaches 66.0 and 66.4 Overall, outperforming the 1T-parameter open-weight Kimi-K2.6 (65.0 and 65.2).
8PehJKSMDt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the expert-validated benchmark in an underexplored domain, the broad model comparison, and consistent gains from domain-specific context engineering and post-training.
8PehJKSMDt.main_concern: Performance may reflect engineered Petrophys features rather than independent reasoning, and generalization is untested beyond 40 wells, with scoring that relies on LLM-as-judge.

UjNiMtNgR7.one_liner: Memorization-residual guided sampling extracts other clients' private images from a federated diffusion model.
UjNiMtNgR7.problem: Federated diffusion models can memorize training samples, creating an unexamined client-to-client privacy leak that needs no gradient access or interference with training.
UjNiMtNgR7.method: A malicious client uses two negative references, a model trained only on its own data and the public pretrained model, and uses their prediction residuals against the global model as sampling-time guidance.
UjNiMtNgR7.key_idea: Subtract the attacker-private and public-model predictions from the global model's prediction as guidance, isolating memorization of other clients' data during sampling.
UjNiMtNgR7.evidence: Experiments on federated datasets such as Fed-Fundus, with component ablations, a classifier-free-guidance sweep and five seeds per the reviews.
UjNiMtNgR7.claimed_gains: The attack consistently increases both the frequency of high-similarity reproductions and the coverage of distinct threat images; no numbers stated.
UjNiMtNgR7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the client-to-client threat model is compelling and the residual-guidance idea simple and intuitive, with consistent gains over direct sampling.
UjNiMtNgR7.main_concern: Practical severity is not cleanly established: the baseline global model already memorizes strongly, and experiments do not separate extraction of training images from similarity to the data distribution.

zYOvvFVRHV.one_liner: ERST measures interaction as the change in an aggregation's output when one entity's representation is swapped for a learned reference.
zYOvvFVRHV.problem: Existing spatiotemporal forecasters aggregate entity representations but do not measure how the aggregation function's output changes when one entity's representation is replaced.
zYOvvFVRHV.method: For each entity, ERST builds a learned reference from its history, other entities' information, and time and layer embeddings, replaces only that entity's representation, and takes the output difference of the same aggregation function as its response. The response updates the entity representation, forming a module that plugs into different forecasting architectures.
zYOvvFVRHV.key_idea: Replace one entity's representation with a learned reference and use the before-and-after output difference of the same aggregation function as that entity's interaction response.
zYOvvFVRHV.evidence: 12 datasets across five domains and four additional forecasting architectures, with ablations; a review reports lower MAE in 23 of 24 architecture-dataset combinations.
zYOvvFVRHV.claimed_gains: Lower forecasting errors in most evaluated comparisons; no numbers stated in the abstract.
zYOvvFVRHV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the mechanism is simple and effective, the evaluation is broad across datasets and architectures, and the ablations are well organized.
zYOvvFVRHV.main_concern: The evidence does not establish that the replacement response captures interaction information, and the forecasting limitation it addresses is not clearly identified.

SlQoWP20k9.one_liner: State space model over event-driven temporal simplicial complexes for online higher-order interaction learning, with a Weisfeiler–Lehman expressivity test.
SlQoWP20k9.problem: Clique-expanded graph models miss higher-order dependencies, while hypergraph models are computationally costly and have limited theoretical expressivity for temporal higher-order networks.
SlQoWP20k9.method: The paper introduces the Temporal Simplicial Complex (TSC), an event-driven sequence of simplicial complexes with isomorphism and a Temporal Simplicial Weisfeiler–Lehman (TSWL) test, then TS³M, an online architecture that uses state space models to propagate information over the TSC, with an expressiveness bound.
SlQoWP20k9.key_idea: Represent time-evolving group interactions as event-driven simplicial complexes and propagate information over them with state space models, analyzed through a temporal simplicial WL test.
SlQoWP20k9.evidence: A TSWL-based expressiveness bound and experiments on temporal higher-order link prediction and dynamic closure prediction, with per-epoch training-time comparisons, as described by reviewers.
SlQoWP20k9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the TSC and TSWL formalism extends simplicial WL theory to continuous-time event streams clearly, and the model shows good training efficiency and performance against baselines.
SlQoWP20k9.main_concern: Reviewers say theory and practice diverge (theorems assume an injective encoder and full neighborhoods while experiments sample none, and large simplices create exponentially many faces), efficiency evidence is per-epoch time only, and architecture and experiment details are vague.

JeIuxhCtbA.one_liner: URGE models each modality as a Gaussian with uncertainty, aligning views and fusing tokens by reliability for urban representations.
JeIuxhCtbA.problem: Existing multimodal urban representation methods treat each observed modality as deterministic evidence, so unreliable observations can distort cross-view learning and propagate into the final representation.
JeIuxhCtbA.method: URGE learns probabilistic view-specific semantics with Pairwise Gaussian Agreement, which scores cross-view compatibility relative to uncertainty, and carries uncertainty into token-level fusion. Relative Fusion Robustness uses controlled evidence degradation and counterfactual fusion as a training signal for productive use of the available evidence.
JeIuxhCtbA.key_idea: Represent each modality as a Gaussian (mean plus variance) and use Pairwise Gaussian Agreement and uncertainty-conditioned token fusion so reliability governs cross-modal interaction.
JeIuxhCtbA.evidence: Reported prediction tasks in two cities plus random token masking and replacement robustness tests; a reviewer notes the paper claims 29 tasks but reports 8 city-task combinations.
JeIuxhCtbA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem (variable modality reliability even when all modalities are available) is practical and that URGE beats the tested baselines across tasks and perturbations in both cities.
JeIuxhCtbA.main_concern: Originality and formulation: the PGA loss closely resembles the mutual likelihood score of PFE, may degenerate as variance goes to zero, and UrbanFusion is not compared.

OApbfOYwkl.one_liner: FakeFlow casts AI-generated image detection as flow matching in label space, from Gaussian states to real or fake label vectors.
OApbfOYwkl.problem: AI-generated image detectors trained as direct mappings can rely on salient cues specific to training generators and generalize poorly to unseen generators.
OApbfOYwkl.method: Given features from a frozen visual encoder, FakeFlow learns image-conditioned trajectories from Gaussian initial states to real or fake label vectors. FakeFlow-Drift regresses the velocity field, FakeFlow-Leap predicts the target label vector and converts it to a velocity, and classifier-free guidance amplifies the gap between conditional and unconditional predictions.
OApbfOYwkl.key_idea: Predict authenticity as an image-conditioned continuous trajectory in label space, with two parameterizations (velocity regression or target prediction) whose different temporal error weighting generalizes differently.
OApbfOYwkl.evidence: Cross-generator evaluation on unseen generators and real-world images with a frozen DINOv3 ViT-7B/16 backbone, ablations on loss, CFG and time sampling, and a theoretical result on one-step Bayes-optimal decoding.
OApbfOYwkl.claimed_gains: not stated in the available abstract (a review cites average accuracy on AIGI-Now rising from 86.4% for the DINOv3 baseline to 88.7% and 91.6%).
OApbfOYwkl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that studying the classification process in label space is an interesting direction, with a clearly presented formulation, broad evaluation on unseen generators and useful ablations.
OApbfOYwkl.main_concern: The benefit of flow matching over direct label regression is not isolated: Leap is equivalent to time-weighted regression, one-step inference is the default, and gains are confounded with the strong frozen DINOv3 backbone.

Cl5uVuDpSN.one_liner: Feasibility-guided LLM algorithm evolution that prevents known failures, repairs infeasible offspring and reuses failure memory across generations.
Cl5uVuDpSN.problem: LLM-evolved solver programs often fail to run, exceed time limits or violate constraints, wasting limited candidate budgets and blocking evaluation of their algorithmic changes.
Cl5uVuDpSN.method: RevivEvo uses parent-specific search and failure experience to prevent known risks during generation, type-aware bounded repair to recover infeasible offspring, and failure and repair memory to reuse experience across generations.
Cl5uVuDpSN.key_idea: Treat feasibility as evolutionary feedback: condition generation on past failures, repair infeasible offspring with bounded type-aware fixes, and store failures and repairs for later generations.
Cl5uVuDpSN.evidence: 14 tasks from CO-Bench and HeuriGym with a 20-candidate budget, with ablations, case studies and three runs per main experiment per the reviews.
Cl5uVuDpSN.claimed_gains: Final candidate feasibility rises from 35.60% to 92.38% over the strongest feasibility baseline, macro-averaged Test Avg. Score from 0.664 to 0.832 over the strongest performance baseline, and 52.4% of final selected solvers result from repair or descend from a repaired candidate.
Cl5uVuDpSN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that offspring infeasibility is a practical bottleneck in LLM-driven algorithm evolution and that the method improves feasibility and solver quality across diverse tasks.
Cl5uVuDpSN.main_concern: Comparisons are not made at equal total compute because repair attempts do not count toward the candidate budget, and the ablations lack a full without-repair or simple self-repair baseline.

ali4PgRT0U.one_liner: Benchmark evaluating long-horizon LLM agents on RTL and commercial EDA-flow co-optimization with independent post-route verification.
ali4PgRT0U.problem: Long-horizon agents must turn decisions into reliable results under imperfect feedback and a finite budget, which single-turn RTL-generation tests do not measure.
ali4PgRT0U.method: SILICA-BENCH gives agents reference RTL and a reference flow, lets them work within a declared resource budget and nominate a deliverable, and checks it with protected RTL and netlist replay plus artifact-matched post-route measurements.
ali4PgRT0U.key_idea: Score agents on continuously graded PPA improvement of real circuits under hard functional requirements, verified by dual replay of the nominated RTL and its post-route netlist.
ali4PgRT0U.evidence: 36 designs across eight domains, six deployed systems, three permission conditions and three independent submissions, giving 1,944 scheduled runs.
ali4PgRT0U.claimed_gains: Terminal acceptance ranges from 92.28% to 99.07% and failure-inclusive quality from 1.045 to 1.254 relative to the reference.
ali4PgRT0U.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a realistic, carefully protected benchmark using a commercial RTL-to-GDS flow on real designs, and that it shows agents often produce valid outputs yet struggle to improve the reference.
ali4PgRT0U.main_concern: Two of the three claimed long-horizon distinctions (early evidence versus final quality, and a found versus a delivered design) are not measured, since only the final nomination is scored.

n5xqtaBt3j.one_liner: Jointly trains novel-view generation with 3D language understanding on a Mixture-of-Transformers multimodal model to improve view synthesis.
n5xqtaBt3j.problem: Novel-view generation methods use fine-grained geometric cues but do not explicitly model high-level semantic and spatial properties such as object identity, attributes and inter-object relationships.
n5xqtaBt3j.method: Ask4NV builds on a pretrained unified multimodal Mixture-of-Transformers model, incorporates camera geometry into both VAE and ViT representations, and lets generation use understanding features through joint self-attention with modality-aware attention masking.
n5xqtaBt3j.key_idea: Use 3D language understanding objectives (QA and grounding) as auxiliary supervision, with understanding features feeding generation through joint self-attention under modality-aware masks.
n5xqtaBt3j.evidence: Novel-view generation experiments on image quality and geometric consistency, 3D language understanding results, and analyses of cross-view correspondence in VAE representations, with ablations against ViT-conditioned and fine-tuned baselines.
n5xqtaBt3j.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that asking whether 3D language supervision helps novel-view generation is an interesting, well-motivated question and that the controlled ablation ladder and mechanism analysis are useful.
n5xqtaBt3j.main_concern: Reviewers say the gains are not causally attributed to 3D language supervision because Ask4NV also sees extra ScanNet frames and training tokens, with no equal-budget non-language control.

VsfKX3cZm9.one_liner: Aligns lightweight subject-specific adapters to a reference subject on shared calibration images before fine-tuning for few-shot fMRI image reconstruction.
VsfKX3cZm9.problem: Current fMRI visual reconstruction methods fall short when subject-specific data and computation are limited.
VsfKX3cZm9.method: Adapter Alignment is a staged, architecture-agnostic procedure: subject-specific adapters are first explicitly aligned to a pre-trained reference subject on a small set of shared calibration images, then the full pipeline is fine-tuned while preserving this alignment. A coverage-based algorithm selects representative calibration images.
VsfKX3cZm9.key_idea: Explicitly align new-subject adapters to a reference subject on shared calibration images before fine-tuning, rather than letting a shared space emerge implicitly.
VsfKX3cZm9.evidence: Experiments across subjects, datasets, reconstruction architectures (MindEye1 and MindEye2 per reviews), reference subjects and training budgets, with ablations, cross-subject representation analysis and pre-diffusion retrieval.
VsfKX3cZm9.claimed_gains: Reconstruction metrics improve by up to 8% in low-data regimes, and with calibration-image selection the method surpasses baselines fine-tuned with one hour of data using only 24 minutes of subject-specific data.
VsfKX3cZm9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method gives consistent improvements in low-data fMRI transfer across subjects, architectures and budgets on a practical problem.
VsfKX3cZm9.main_concern: Reviewers cite missing comparisons with recent few-shot adaptation methods and limited architecture coverage, plus gains that vanish at full data and an unclear interpretation of the aligned space.

qm6pYMJYA5.one_liner: Multi-turn benchmark built from pediatric inpatient records for evaluating LLMs on medication effectiveness and adverse drug events.
qm6pYMJYA5.problem: Existing medical LLM benchmarks emphasize general or adult medicine, and pediatric care, with age-dependent physiology and medication-safety needs, suffers from data scarcity.
qm6pYMJYA5.method: PedMed-Bench is an event-driven benchmark organized around treatment adjustments in real-world pediatric EHR trajectories, released in Chinese and English with human-verified translation. The authors evaluate representative LLMs on adverse drug event (ADE) extraction, suspected drugs and related tasks.
qm6pYMJYA5.key_idea: Organize real pediatric inpatient trajectories around treatment adjustments so clinical state, efficacy and safety are evaluated together over multiple turns.
qm6pYMJYA5.evidence: Systematic evaluation of numerous representative LLMs, including reasoning models, on tasks such as ADE extraction and suspected-drug prediction.
qm6pYMJYA5.claimed_gains: not stated as gains; the highest ADE extraction F1 among evaluated LLMs is only 12.89%.
qm6pYMJYA5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree pediatric medication safety is clinically important and underexplored, and that a benchmark built from real pediatric records with substantial annotation effort is a valuable resource.
qm6pYMJYA5.main_concern: Reviewers cite inconsistent or unclear metric definitions and cohorts (for example a negative accuracy-based ADE Severity score) and a poorly specified problem formulation and pediatric-specific design.

NNNxGpgVJ3.one_liner: Training-free visual token pruning that keeps query-focused and image-intrinsic fine tokens plus a pooled coarse context for MLLMs.
NNNxGpgVJ3.problem: Training-free visual token pruning methods do well on general benchmarks but collapse on fine-grained tasks such as grounding, because keeping only a subset of native patches breaks the content and position integrity of the visual sequence.
NNNxGpgVJ3.method: Before the LLM, Bifocal keeps query-focused tokens the question refers to, image-intrinsic tokens that maximize representation and coverage of the image, and a pooled coarse context. Inside the LLM, it further keeps the top-K tokens by text-to-image attention.
NNNxGpgVJ3.key_idea: Mix fine tokens from two evidence sources (question and image) with a pooled coarse context so the retained sequence keeps content and positional integrity.
NNNxGpgVJ3.evidence: Four models and several token budgets across general VQA, reasoning, OCR, hallucination and grounding benchmarks, with ablations and visualizations.
NNNxGpgVJ3.claimed_gains: Best general average in every setting and, at the tightest budget, leads the strongest baseline on grounding (the margin is cut off in the provided abstract).
NNNxGpgVJ3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the mixed-granularity design is well motivated by the positional and content integrity analysis and that experiments are broad across models, budgets and tasks.
NNNxGpgVJ3.main_concern: Reviewers question the fairness of the layer-averaged budget (Bifocal keeps more tokens in early layers), thin ablations, preprocessing overhead, and generality beyond single-image settings.

fiqZasrkGp.one_liner: Successive-elimination and doubling-epoch algorithms with matching lower bounds for multi-index contextual bandits with monotone reward functions.
fiqZasrkGp.problem: In multi-index bandits the reward depends on the context through several unknown latent projections composed with an unknown multivariate function, so the learner must recover a latent subspace and learn the reward function at the same time.
fiqZasrkGp.method: CM-MIB is a successive-elimination variant that discretizes coordinate-wise monotone reward functions. For a stronger entire-monotonicity condition the paper gives EM-MIB and EM-MIB+, where EM-MIB+ plugs a least-squares estimator for entirely monotone functions into FALCON+ with refitting at doubling epochs.
fiqZasrkGp.key_idea: Exploit entire monotonicity of the reward in the projected context, reducing the contextual bandit to offline monotone regression via least-squares refits at doubling epochs.
fiqZasrkGp.evidence: Regret upper bounds and a minimax lower bound proven in theory, plus a small synthetic experiment (K=10 arms, r=3) in the appendix.
fiqZasrkGp.claimed_gains: Regret upper bound of O-tilde(T^((r+1)/(r+2))) for coordinate-wise monotone rewards with a matching minimax lower bound; the entire-monotone bound is cut off in the provided abstract.
fiqZasrkGp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the multi-index generalization is well motivated and that matching upper and lower bounds in the horizon exponent, with a clear split between the two monotonicity classes, are a solid theoretical contribution.
fiqZasrkGp.main_concern: Reviewers say the empirical validation is weak (an easy instance with a uniformly optimal arm), the algorithms may not scale in practice, and a related random-design least-squares result (Bibaut and van der Laan, 2019) is missing.

h2pbt1cdOM.one_liner: Test-time learning framework that distills verified solutions into reusable cognitive schemas with applicability conditions, retrieved by tag filtering and reranking.
h2pbt1cdOM.problem: Memory-augmented LLM methods accumulate problem-solving experience, but accumulated experience does not automatically yield a systematic understanding of solution principles that guides later reasoning.
h2pbt1cdOM.method: VCST extracts task-level schemas from verified solutions, abstracts shared solution structures across tasks, and reuses schemas after checking their applicability conditions, with no parameter updates. New tasks retrieve schemas via tag-based filtering and semantic reranking, and a fixed API budget is split adaptively between cognition construction and task solving.
h2pbt1cdOM.key_idea: Admit only verified solutions into memory as abstracted schemas that carry explicit applicability conditions, checked before reuse on new tasks.
h2pbt1cdOM.evidence: Four benchmark suites, 13 benchmarks and nine backbone LLMs (GPT, Qwen2.5-Coder and DeepSeek-R1-Distill families per reviews), with ablations, memory diagnostics and task-order analysis.
h2pbt1cdOM.claimed_gains: Improves accuracy over strong test-time scaling baselines; the abstract's LiveCodeBench margin over S* is cut off, though a review cites 6.1-20.7 percentage points.
h2pbt1cdOM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that accumulating and reusing knowledge at test time is an important problem and that the evaluation is broad across benchmarks and backbones.
h2pbt1cdOM.main_concern: Reviewers say novelty is limited relative to ReasoningBank, ExpeL, Buffer of Thoughts, Agent Workflow Memory and Dynamic Cheatsheet, and that the benefit of cross-task schema abstraction is not clearly isolated.

ptdxxQtsyV.one_liner: Autoresearch framework where coding agents propose LLM watermark schemes screened by statistical validity tests and ranked on three dimensions.
ptdxxQtsyV.problem: Recent LLM watermarking progress comes from human refinement of existing methods, which is limited by the pace of human researchers, while reliability and effectiveness matter for commercial and regulatory use.
ptdxxQtsyV.method: They define strict validity criteria (for example no unexpectedly high false positive rate), build statistical tests that automatically check whether a scheme meets them, and an evaluation suite ranking detectability, quality and robustness. Frontier-model agents (GPT-6 Astra, Opus 5, Gemini-3.8 Flash) then propose and refine schemes within this framework.
ptdxxQtsyV.key_idea: Gate agent-proposed watermark schemes with automated statistical validity tests, then rank the survivors on detectability, quality and robustness.
ptdxxQtsyV.evidence: Runs with three frontier-model agents discovered over 50 watermarking schemes, followed by a manual study that distills schemes into components and measures each component's impact on detectability, quality and robustness.
ptdxxQtsyV.claimed_gains: Discovers over 50 distortion-free watermarking schemes, including several that outperform prior works along all three key dimensions (no further numbers in the provided abstract).
ptdxxQtsyV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that formalizing validity criteria with automated statistical tests and using agents to find watermarks that improve on prior work is an interesting, concrete contribution.
ptdxxQtsyV.main_concern: Reviewers say the autonomous-discovery claim is overstated because humans still decompose and interpret schemes, the search may overfit the evaluator, and the dense main text depends heavily on the appendix.

qHhf4VKPRG.one_liner: Switches unified editors to the text-to-image task for bounded intervals during denoising, timed by decay in source-image attention.
qHhf4VKPRG.problem: Standard instruction-based editing pipelines keep source-image conditioning throughout denoising, even though source attention declines for some edits over the sampling trajectory and unified models are also trained for text-to-image generation.
qHhf4VKPRG.method: Task switching lets a unified editor draw on its T2I capability by swapping from editing conditioning to T2I conditioning for bounded intervals of the denoising trajectory. Switch timing is informed by measured source-attention decay and by agreement between the editing and T2I velocity fields.
qHhf4VKPRG.key_idea: Replace source-image-conditioned editing with text-to-image conditioning during bounded denoising intervals chosen from measured source-attention decay.
qHhf4VKPRG.evidence: Three unified editors and four benchmarks, with controls such as removing the image while keeping the original instruction, one-way versus interval switching, continuous guidance, and an improved-instruction baseline.
qHhf4VKPRG.claimed_gains: not stated as numbers; the abstract says switching improves edit quality while mean perceptual preservation stays close to pure editing across all three models.
qHhf4VKPRG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the diagnosis-to-intervention chain is well built, with informative controls and transfer beyond a single editor.
qHhf4VKPRG.main_concern: Reviewers say the preservation claim is stronger than the analysis supports (nonsignificant differences alongside clear SSIM losses) and that the ranking against the strong alternative E* flips across models and judges.

2XrIHeO9jb.one_liner: Training-free query-cued rehearsal restores forgotten key-value associations in fast weight models via ridge regression applied to the current read.
2XrIHeO9jb.problem: Fast weight models compress history into a bounded state, which degrades individual key-value associations through interference, and naive rehearsal is non-local so it can perturb other associations.
2XrIHeO9jb.method: ReCue keeps a bounded cache of associations along underrepresented key directions, selectively rehearses them using the current query, jointly solves the correction by ridge regression, applies it only to the current read, and then restores the original state.
2XrIHeO9jb.key_idea: Rehearse only query-cued cached associations via ridge regression, apply the correction to the current read, and immediately roll back the state.
2XrIHeO9jb.evidence: Pretrained LaCT and DeltaNet models on RULER and LongBench, compared with the base models and query-independent rehearsal, with cache-selection and query-cueing ablations.
2XrIHeO9jb.claimed_gains: The abstract states improvements on RULER and LongBench without numbers; reviews cite the LaCT 8K single-needle average rising from 70.27 to 94.13.
2XrIHeO9jb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the mechanism is simple and training-free, works on official checkpoints, and gives substantial retrieval gains on LaCT.
2XrIHeO9jb.main_concern: Reviewers say LongBench gains over direct Attention Read are marginal, no latency or memory cost is reported, and the cache-selection criterion and ridge-residual read are not well isolated from a direct attention read.

sTAfiKKFDA.one_liner: Reformulates uncalibrated photometric stereo as joint depth-normal estimation, using CLIP pseudo-lighting cues and depth-derived normals for consistency supervision.
sTAfiKKFDA.problem: Uncalibrated photometric stereo estimates surface normals and integrates them to depth afterwards, which ignores the coupling between local shape and global geometry and causes inconsistent reconstructions and error accumulation.
sTAfiKKFDA.method: CLIP provides pseudo-lighting cues to resolve illumination ambiguity, a plane-sweeping-like module recovers coarse depth that is jointly refined with camera intrinsics, and the refined depth and intrinsics yield geometry-consistent surface normals. This enables consistency-driven supervision for semi-supervised learning with limited synthetic data.
sTAfiKKFDA.key_idea: Derive surface normals from refined depth and intrinsics so depth and normals constrain each other, with CLIP supplying pseudo-lighting cues.
sTAfiKKFDA.evidence: Experiments on DiLiGenT and DiLiGenT-Pi against UPS methods and against calibrated and monocular depth methods, plus ablations on the CLIP cues and a small synthetic N&D dataset (per reviews).
sTAfiKKFDA.claimed_gains: Outperforms state-of-the-art UPS techniques and is competitive with calibrated and monocular depth estimation methods (no numbers in the abstract).
sTAfiKKFDA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the joint depth-normal formulation is sensible and that the method reaches strong normal-estimation accuracy on DiLiGenT and DiLiGenT-Pi.
sTAfiKKFDA.main_concern: Reviewers cite reliance on CLIP for lighting cues that degrades on complex relief and mixed materials, limited novelty relative to common joint depth-normal practice, thin depth evaluation, and an unclear depth-to-normal formula (Eq. 7).

UtWRF3rjc4.one_liner: Diagnoses world-model-driven predictive guardrails for LLM agents along prediction integration, prediction reliability and faithful use of predictions.
UtWRF3rjc4.problem: Evaluations of predictive safety guardrails focus on end-to-end safety outcomes, leaving unclear whether gains come from reliable prediction and faithful use of predicted risks.
UtWRF3rjc4.method: They diagnose the prediction-to-action pipeline along three dimensions: how world-model predictions are integrated into decisions, whether the predictions are reliable, and whether their content is faithfully used, via online evaluation, offline prediction tests and feedback interventions.
UtWRF3rjc4.key_idea: Audit the pipeline by varying prediction involvement, testing prediction accuracy by horizon, and corrupting or locally verifying predictions to test whether decisions depend on their content.
UtWRF3rjc4.evidence: Seven policy models and two safety environments, with online evaluation, offline prediction tests and feedback interventions.
UtWRF3rjc4.claimed_gains: not stated; as an analysis paper it reports that stronger prediction involvement does not give monotonic safety gains and can reduce task completion while raising inference cost.
UtWRF3rjc4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the three-question diagnostic framework is coherent and gives a useful audit view beyond end-to-end safety scores.
UtWRF3rjc4.main_concern: Reviewers say the decision-faithfulness conclusion is not isolated from execution gating (safety gains under corrupted predictions may come from the gate or from executing less) and that several findings overlap prior work.

eyrOkMLFOy.one_liner: Auditable evaluation contract for frozen-feature anomaly detection that records reference-access protocols on four cards and certifies single-factor comparisons.
eyrOkMLFOy.problem: Zero- and few-shot industrial anomaly detectors are compared in the same tables even when their reference access differs (clean training-normal images versus the full test cohort including anomalous queries), and labels such as batched zero-shot do not price that difference.
eyrOkMLFOy.method: BudgetMatch describes each protocol on four cards; its certificate lists every field on which two protocols differ and admits a single-factor comparison only within a predeclared intervention set. A registered study expresses the access difference in units of clean reference images.
eyrOkMLFOy.key_idea: Certify comparisons by listing every differing protocol field and admitting only single-factor differences, pricing access in clean reference images.
eyrOkMLFOy.evidence: A registered study with a fixed global reference-patch 1-nearest-neighbor scorer and the transductive detector MuSc, on MVTec AD, VisA and Real-IAD.
eyrOkMLFOy.claimed_gains: Going from one to sixteen clean images raises macro image AUROC by +5.60 (MVTec AD), +6.31 (VisA) and +6.13 (Real-IAD) points, and a clean bank as large as the test cohort beats the cohort by +3.49 and +7.07 points.
eyrOkMLFOy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree reference-access mismatch is a meaningful benchmarking problem and that the controlled experiments show reference budget and purity materially affect performance.
eyrOkMLFOy.main_concern: Reviewers say novelty over existing evaluation-card and protocol-reporting work is limited, and results depend on the scorer (the cohort advantage shrinks under MuSc) without validating the ranking rule on matched published comparisons.

8vYgwMaqes.one_liner: Training-free guidance steers flow-matching VLA action chunks toward the previous chunk's unexecuted tail to smooth chunk boundaries.
8vYgwMaqes.problem: Consecutive action chunks from VLA policies can disagree on overlapping future actions, producing abrupt changes (jerk and discontinuity) at execution boundaries.
8vYgwMaqes.method: SEAM uses the previous chunk's unexecuted tail as a temporally aligned reference, and Velocity-guided Loss Steering alternates learned velocity-field steps with closed-form corrections toward a time-dependent mean reference. The corrected state feeds later velocity evaluations without backpropagating through the policy network.
8vYgwMaqes.key_idea: Alternate flow-matching velocity steps with closed-form corrections toward a time-dependent mean of the previous chunk's unexecuted tail.
8vYgwMaqes.evidence: A 1,300-episode LIBERO-10 comparison with pi0.5 including matched-state reference controls, and SmolVLA on LIBERO-Spatial against baseline and RTC, all in simulation.
8vYgwMaqes.claimed_gains: Reduces boundary action second differences by 28% and chunk transition discontinuity by 27% on LIBERO-10 with pi0.5; with SmolVLA on LIBERO-Spatial reaches 72.0% success versus 65.6% baseline and 60.0% RTC at about 1% extra execution cost.
8vYgwMaqes.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the training-free method addresses a real problem with low overhead and is supported by well-designed controls on reference content, execution length and delays.
8vYgwMaqes.main_concern: Reviewers say novelty over RTC and related past-action conditioning methods is limited, and evaluation is simulation-only (LIBERO) with smoother motion not always yielding higher success.

pr8jovmOI4.one_liner: Zero-shot 3D instance segmentation that segments cutting-plane mesh renderings with SAM 2 and merges masks by overlap on the mesh.
pr8jovmOI4.problem: Existing zero-shot 3D instance segmentation segments input images and must match partial, noisy masks across viewpoints, which dominates their design.
pr8jovmOI4.method: Tomos3D renders multiple cutting-plane views of a textured mesh, segments each view independently with SAM 2, lifts masks onto the mesh (each pixel maps to a 3D triangle) and stitches them by mask overlap with no cross-view matching. MaskProbe classifies instances by adapting the final attention pooling of a frozen vision-language model using projected instance masks.
pr8jovmOI4.key_idea: Segment renderings of cutting planes through the mesh instead of input frames, so masks merge on the mesh by overlap without cross-view association.
pr8jovmOI4.evidence: Evaluated by the fraction of ground-truth instances recovered (average recall) on ScanNet with transfer to 3RScan and SceneNN, plus a recognition comparison of MaskProbe against OM3D+ on shared proposals.
pr8jovmOI4.claimed_gains: 51.9 versus 43.1 for prior training-free methods on ScanNet, within 2.4 points of supervised ESAM-E, and 70.9 versus 59.0 for the best prior method on 3RScan and SceneNN.
pr8jovmOI4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that segmenting cutting-plane renderings is a novel, well-motivated way to avoid cross-view matching and that cross-dataset results against training-free baselines are strong.
pr8jovmOI4.main_concern: Reviewers question the fairness of the average-recall comparison (Tomos3D may assign multiple masks per location), the lack of a plane-sampling ablation, and the modest gain of MaskProbe over OM3D+ (about 1.7 points).

3QfV6ILfEa.one_liner: Parameter-efficient bidirectional adaptation of pretrained weather and power models via prefusion alignment, latent memory and postfusion modulation.
3QfV6ILfEa.problem: Power forecasting methods treat weather as exogenous site-level input, which makes it hard to capture how continuous weather processes propagate across space and time and persistently affect power dynamics, and extending weather foundation models to joint weather-power prediction is underexplored.
3QfV6ILfEa.method: ALM adds three steps (prefusion alignment, latent memory, postfusion modulation) that exchange information between weather and power backbones while keeping most backbone parameters frozen.
3QfV6ILfEa.key_idea: Bidirectional exchange between frozen weather and power backbones through alignment before fusion, a latent memory, and modulation after fusion, trained with few parameters.
3QfV6ILfEa.evidence: A gridded weather-power benchmark for the contiguous United States (CONUS) with comparisons against full fine-tuning, zero-shot backbones and nine PEFT methods, ablations, and downstream power applications.
3QfV6ILfEa.claimed_gains: Versus full fine-tuning, ALM reduces mean 72-hour RMSE by 19.9% across 12 reported variables while using only 9.7% trainable parameters.
3QfV6ILfEa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree bidirectional weather-power exchange is a worthwhile direction and that comparisons against full fine-tuning and many PEFT methods show strong results.
3QfV6ILfEa.main_concern: Reviewers say the gridded wind and PV targets are derived from meteorological data without validation against measured generation, and gains are not isolated between the extra power information and the ALM mechanism.

b8bWNMjMbx.one_liner: Counterexample showing bounded omnidirectional noise cannot guarantee avoidance of sharply repulsive points, plus a Gaussian-noise avoidance result.
b8bWNMjMbx.problem: It was open (Bianchi, Hachem and Schechtman, 2024, Remark 4) whether omnidirectional noise with conditional fourth-moment control suffices for almost-sure avoidance of sharply repulsive critical points in the non-weakly-convex definable setting.
b8bWNMjMbx.method: They construct a globally Lipschitz, coercive, definable, non-weakly-convex objective in R^2 where SGD with ball-uniform noise converges with probability 1 to a nonminimal sharply repulsive point, using a two-cycle argument that bounds rescaled iterates. They also prove that Gaussian noise avoids any finite collection of sharply repulsive points for locally Lipschitz definable objectives.
b8bWNMjMbx.key_idea: A two-cycle argument bounds rescaled iterates to force convergence; for Gaussian noise, difference-quotient functions show convergence would imply a stationary distribution with zero expected descent, contradicting a positive lower bound.
b8bWNMjMbx.evidence: Theoretical proofs only: an explicit counterexample objective and a positive Gaussian-noise avoidance theorem.
b8bWNMjMbx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper resolves an open question with a neat, clearly explained counterexample and adds a complementary positive Gaussian-noise result.
b8bWNMjMbx.main_concern: Reviewers note the main theorems cover only the 1/n step size rather than the full range alpha in (1/2, 1] of the conjecture, the Gaussian result shows avoidance but not convergence, and dropping weak convexity has unclear practical value.

A3GE8kL950.one_liner: Matched-perturbation benchmark testing whether genomic foundation models generalize compositionally to regulatory-element interactions beyond activity prediction.
A3GE8kL950.problem: Genomic foundation models predict regulatory activity, but it is unclear whether they learn transferable rules for how combinations of regulatory elements interact across spacing, sequence background and promoter context.
A3GE8kL950.method: A matched-perturbation evaluation framework measures regulatory effects and interactions through a hierarchy from sequence recognition and local perturbation effects to pairwise interactions, transfer across backgrounds and promoters, and multi-site combinations.
A3GE8kL950.key_idea: Compare matched perturbations so that effects and non-additive interactions are measured instead of sequence-level activity, across a hierarchy of increasing compositional difficulty.
A3GE8kL950.evidence: 14 pretrained model configurations, 65,116 enhancer-pair quartets and 6,181 multi-site records, with native likelihoods, supervised readouts on frozen embeddings, and identity-only and simple reference controls.
A3GE8kL950.claimed_gains: not stated; as a benchmark paper it reports that supervised readouts recover interactions between familiar enhancers no better than an identity-only control.
A3GE8kL950.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is important and that a benchmark built on experimentally measured non-additive interactions across many models is a meaningful addition to DNA foundation-model evaluation.
A3GE8kL950.main_concern: Reviewers say measurement noise and non-comparable dataset sizes across evaluation levels confound the link between lower performance and rising interaction complexity, and the main text under-states weak replicate reliability.

rb73jOu1mt.one_liner: Consolidates agent skill edits by document hierarchy without generative rewriting, organizing a budgeted core skill and retrievable reference subtrees.
rb73jOu1mt.problem: LLM-generated consolidation in multi-trajectory skill evolution can alter or omit useful details while leaving semantic redundancy unresolved.
rb73jOu1mt.method: Skill Tree groups edits by structural context, removes redundant guidance, and preserves useful content without generative rewriting. It organizes knowledge into a budgeted core skill plus supplementary references, reorders core content under importance and workflow constraints, and retrieves task-relevant reference subtrees at inference time.
rb73jOu1mt.key_idea: Use the skill document's heading hierarchy to group, deduplicate and verbatim-apply edits, then split content into a budgeted core and retrievable reference subtrees.
rb73jOu1mt.evidence: Experiments on skill construction, out-of-distribution generalization and cross-model reuse, including SpreadsheetBench and frozen WikiTQ (per reviews), with component and structural ablations.
rb73jOu1mt.claimed_gains: The abstract reports substantial downstream improvements without numbers; reviews cite +8.8 to +14.5 points on the SpreadsheetBench Hard metric.
rb73jOu1mt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the pipeline is coherent, traceable and largely deterministic, with extensive experiments and ablations supporting the structure-aware design.
rb73jOu1mt.main_concern: Reviewers say headline gains may include the 200 SpreadsheetBench tasks used for skill evolution, the tree adds little beyond Markdown headings, and context and construction costs and fixed priorities are not reported.

ooPc1aQXLJ.one_liner: Set-based formal verification of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks using interval, CROWN-style, MILP and star-set reachability that exploit spline structure.
ooPc1aQXLJ.problem: Mainstream neural network verifiers have no spline operator, and converting a KAN with a grid of G cells to a ReLU network inflates the network by a factor of G.
ooPc1aQXLJ.method: They develop set-based reachability for KANs that works directly on the architecture, with exact verification for degree-1 KANs without the base branch and sound verification for degree 2 or higher or with the base branch, instantiated with interval bound propagation, CROWN-style bounds, MILPs and star sets.
ooPc1aQXLJ.key_idea: Verify directly on spline edges using knot-aware partitions of shared input coordinates, exact for degree-1 KANs and sound relaxations otherwise.
ooPc1aQXLJ.evidence: Verification of robustness, output ranges, barrier conditions, monotone ordering and one-step reachability on trained KANs (26 networks per a review), compared against converted-network baselines, with a Lean development noted by reviewers.
ooPc1aQXLJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework exploits KAN structure, covers several property classes including barrier conditions on trained controllers, and usefully separates exact from sound regimes.
ooPc1aQXLJ.main_concern: Reviewers say the comparison protocol is inconsistent (timeout handling and a weakened PWA-MILP baseline), scalability is shown only for networks of at most two layers, and methodological novelty over general nonlinear verification is limited.

NzEMaGTbQ8.one_liner: Jointly grows speculative-decoding verification trees across requests under a shared budget using drafter scores, packed for one target forward pass.
NzEMaGTbQ8.problem: Under high concurrency, giving each request a fixed verification window along a single path ignores differences in draft quality across requests, wastes alternative branches, and adds intermediate verification-state overhead in hybrid architectures.
NzEMaGTbQ8.method: Request Forest reuses candidates and predecessor-conditioned scores from a block-parallel drafter and lets eligible nodes across requests compete for a shared budget by path priority, yielding a prefix-closed forest. It packs the forest into a compact, branch-isolated layout, verifies it in one target-model forward pass, and commits only states along accepted paths.
NzEMaGTbQ8.key_idea: A global priority queue over candidate nodes from all requests allocates tree size, depth and branching jointly under one verification budget.
NzEMaGTbQ8.evidence: Four hybrid-architecture models and four benchmarks, component ablations, and a theoretical analysis showing the growth strategy maximizes summed priorities under the stated scoring assumptions and budget.
NzEMaGTbQ8.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off before the results); reviews cite about 7% throughput from budget sharing and about 5% from allowing branches in ablations.
NzEMaGTbQ8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the shared-budget mechanism addresses a practical high-concurrency bottleneck, needs no drafter retraining, and is backed by theory and component ablations.
NzEMaGTbQ8.main_concern: Reviewers question the benefit over existing schedulers such as DSpark and ECHO (discussed but not evaluated), the reliability of top-k-normalized priority scores across requests, and the narrow task coverage.

NYbFznej32.one_liner: Two-stage training (on-policy self-distillation from transformed views, then GRPO) for grounded adversarial OCR, plus the AdvSpot benchmark.
NYbFznej32.problem: Large multimodal models remain vulnerable to adversarial visual text that humans can read but models struggle to localize and recognize, and existing adversarial OCR evaluations are limited in scale, task coverage or region awareness.
NYbFznej32.method: AdvSpot has 383 images with region-level annotations across 5 primary categories and 13 adversarial OCR types. ArmorOCR first learns missing perception from privileged transformed observations through On-Policy Self-Distillation, then refines grounded perception with GRPO using task-conditioned rewards for localization, recognition, full spotting and VQA.
NYbFznej32.key_idea: Self-distill perception from privileged transformed observations into the adversarial view on-policy, then refine with task-conditioned GRPO rewards.
NYbFznej32.evidence: Experiments on AdvSpot, other adversarial OCR benchmarks and general OCR benchmarks, mainly training Qwen3-VL-8B (per reviews).
NYbFznej32.claimed_gains: The abstract gives no numbers (consistent adversarial OCR gains with competitive general OCR); a review cites 46.8% accuracy and 58.7% IoU for full OTSD versus 44.2% and 54.5% for standard distillation.
NYbFznej32.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree AdvSpot's region-level annotations and grounded questions usefully separate localization from recognition failures and that the method gives meaningful empirical improvements.
NYbFznej32.main_concern: Reviewers say novelty is limited (privileged-view distillation builds on existing work and the benchmark overlaps AdvOCR and SmuggleBench), AdvSpot is small at 383 images, and training is mostly on one base model.

XrSLdoaBAk.one_liner: Aligns controller internal states with macaque motor-cortical population geometry during training to transfer neural structure into GRU and Transformer controllers.
XrSLdoaBAk.problem: It is unclear how to directly transfer computationally useful neural population structure from biological brains into artificial controllers.
XrSLdoaBAk.method: Neuro-Dist uses three macaque motor-cortical datasets as teachers and aligns controller internal states with cortical population geometry during training (via regularized CCA per reviews), so deployment needs no neural data. GRU and Transformer controllers drive a simulated arm.
XrSLdoaBAk.key_idea: Align controller hidden states to neural population geometry with a regularized CCA objective during training only.
XrSLdoaBAk.evidence: GRU and Transformer controllers of a simulated arm on trained, student-held-out and new target directions against five methods including kinematic distillation and six controls, with Holm-corrected seed-split statistics, noise-robustness tests, and tangling and rotational-plane analyses.
XrSLdoaBAk.claimed_gains: Lowest median error among five methods in 10 of 18 comparisons, with a significant Holm-corrected (p<0.05) advantage over all six controls on trained and new targets and over five on student-held-out targets.
XrSLdoaBAk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the control design is rigorous, with solid statistics and a tangling analysis that links the result to known motor-cortex structure.
XrSLdoaBAk.main_concern: Reviewers say the advantage over behavioral supervision is not fully isolated, related corticomotor distillation work is under-discussed, and claims are overstated for a simple planar two-joint arm task.

I51UbJS8ql.one_liner: Shows task arrival order shapes memory accumulation in self-evolving agents, and proposes an offline pilot that selects the order.
I51UbJS8ql.problem: Prior work on memory-based self-evolving agents manages what to save, distill or delete, but early tasks determine what is written first, and filters cannot recover experiences that a bad task order never produced.
I51UbJS8ql.method: They permute the same practice tasks and measure held-out accuracy with memory on and off, compare order selection against tuning per-item memory admission and retrieval rules under a matched search budget, and propose an offline pilot protocol (the ordering lever) for recurring workloads.
I51UbJS8ql.key_idea: Treat practice-task order as a tunable lever upstream of memory write rules, selected with a small offline pilot per memory writer.
