I51UbJS8ql.evidence: Fixed-content task permutations with no-memory controls on Python code benchmarks (including MBPP) with Qwen2.5 models from 7B to 72B and several write policies.
I51UbJS8ql.claimed_gains: Reordering the same tasks changes final accuracy by 4-11 percentage points, and choosing the order gives +2.08 net accuracy versus +0.88 for tuning memory admission and retrieval rules under a matched search budget.
I51UbJS8ql.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the order effect is isolated with careful controls (fixed-content permutations, no-memory control, frozen banks) and that the order-writer interaction is informative.
I51UbJS8ql.main_concern: Reviewers say the order-versus-governance comparison is not matched in search budget or information (the pilot is tuned on the held-out pool) and the evidence is narrow (Python code benchmarks, one agent type).

ctyeFfJijY.one_liner: Training-free one-step image editing that treats source-target residuals as noisy control cues and solves a regularized optimal control problem spectrally.
ctyeFfJijY.problem: Training-free editors become unstable with one-step text-to-image models because source-target residuals act as high-energy control signals, causing structural distortion and background inconsistency.
ctyeFfJijY.method: StableCtrl casts one-step editing as a regularized optimal control problem, yielding an elliptic control equation with an explicit spectral solution that constrains control energy, enforces spatial smoothness and preserves temporal reference consistency. It is model-agnostic and inversion-free, acting as a closed-form FFT-domain low-pass filter on the residual.
ctyeFfJijY.key_idea: Solve an elliptic control equation in closed form in the frequency domain, low-pass filtering the source-target residual while keeping its dominant semantic direction.
ctyeFfJijY.evidence: Four one-step backbones and all ten PIE-Bench categories (per reviews), with ablations, matched-CLIP comparisons against scalar shrinkage and smoothing, and a comparison to ChordEdit.
ctyeFfJijY.claimed_gains: The abstract is cut off before any numbers; reviews cite PSNR rising from 23.80 to 27.46 and scaled LPIPS dropping from 89.20 to 55.55 versus ChordEdit without the proximal step.
ctyeFfJijY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is a simple, closed-form, training-free stabilizer that adds negligible latency and improves background preservation across backbones and categories.
ctyeFfJijY.main_concern: Reviewers say preservation gains may come from weaker editing (lowest CLIP semantic alignment), key controls such as plain low-pass filters are missing, and the contribution of the temporal reference is unclear.

lHU8bfDB8c.one_liner: Adaptive labeling that prioritizes items informative for the hardest pairwise judge comparisons, with valid inference under the learned allocation.
lHU8bfDB8c.problem: Identifying the best LLM judge needs human labels, and unlike classical best-arm identification each label reveals the correctness of all candidate judges, so an item's value depends on how well it separates the hardest-to-distinguish judges.
lHU8bfDB8c.method: Weighted Pairwise Discrepancies (WPD) assigns higher sampling priority to items informative for the most consequential pairwise comparisons, and the paper develops valid inference for judge accuracies and their differences under the adaptively learned allocation (a two-stage estimator with a pilot, per reviews).
lHU8bfDB8c.key_idea: Weight each item's pairwise judge disagreement by how consequential that pair is for identifying the winner, and sample items by that weighted score.
lHU8bfDB8c.evidence: Simulations and five real-data evaluation panels, with asymptotic theory (marginal and pairwise Wald inference) under the learned allocation.
lHU8bfDB8c.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off before the results)
lHU8bfDB8c.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated and that the acquisition criterion plus asymptotic inference for shared labels is a theoretically grounded contribution.
lHU8bfDB8c.main_concern: Reviewers say finite-pilot robustness in near-tie regimes and ablations are thin, judge-prediction costs are ignored, uncertainty quantification does not cover the adaptively selected winner, and novelty over active learning is unclear.

RUygi0fhiT.one_liner: Training-free cross-modal nearest-neighbor retrieval metric (RAVEL) for predicting how well vision encoders perform inside MLLMs.
RUygi0fhiT.problem: Unimodal metrics still dominate vision encoder evaluation even though cross-modal metrics better predict downstream MLLM performance, and prior cross-modal approaches have limitations in experimental design and formulation.
RUygi0fhiT.method: RAVEL scores vision encoders by cross-modal nearest-neighbor retrieval, after fixing limitations in prior experimental design and adding simple improvements (whitening and local set matching of patch-level scores, per reviews).
RUygi0fhiT.key_idea: Measure encoder-language compatibility by cross-modal nearest-neighbor retrieval with whitening and patch-level set matching, without any training.
RUygi0fhiT.evidence: Large-scale ground truth of 210 MLLMs trained with 70 vision encoders and three language backbones of 1.5B to 1.7B parameters under one LLaVA-style pipeline (per reviews), compared against prior metrics.
RUygi0fhiT.claimed_gains: States state-of-the-art performance that outperforms prior methods by a substantial margin, without numbers in the abstract.
RUygi0fhiT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evaluation is large-scale and well controlled and that the simple training-free method gives consistent gains over prior metrics.
RUygi0fhiT.main_concern: Reviewers say correlations over a heterogeneous encoder pool may reflect encoder family or resolution differences, there is little evidence on choosing among similarly strong encoders, and novelty over existing cross-modal metrics is incremental.

CMfu7lDk2j.one_liner: Shows temporary weight decay in Muon pretraining raises loss when removed yet lowers final loss, explained by persistent weight-norm deficits.
CMfu7lDk2j.problem: Evaluating a temporary optimization intervention at the moment it ends can mislead, since its effect on loss can reverse sign by the final training budget.
CMfu7lDk2j.method: They apply fixed-duration temporary weight decay windows in Muon-trained decoder-only Transformers (162M, 405M, 1.4B), vary window timing and duration, and explain the delayed effect with an approximate weight-norm recurrence, fixed-norm replays and norm-reset experiments.
CMfu7lDk2j.key_idea: Early decay leaves a persistent weight-norm deficit that keeps relative update steps larger after the decay ends, producing delayed gains.
CMfu7lDk2j.evidence: Muon-trained decoder-only Transformers at 162M, 405M and 1.4B parameters, with a 3.4B confirmation and a separate Gram intervention.
CMfu7lDk2j.claimed_gains: A schedule selected at 162M and transferred to 1.4B is 0.26 nats worse than no decay when removed, overtakes it after 73% of training, and finishes 0.028 nats better while also beating the best sampled constant-decay baseline.
CMfu7lDk2j.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper gives clear evidence of delayed sign reversal and connects it to weight-norm dynamics with well-separated timing and horizon comparisons.
CMfu7lDk2j.main_concern: Reviewers say the significance is unclear (no demonstrated consistent benefit over constant weight decay or scheduling), the conceptual contribution is incremental, and the explanation is tied to Muon and weight norms.

F0NJFm55ex.one_liner: Hierarchical symbolic music model using rotary time embeddings that restore true musical times despite conditioning-first sequence order.
F0NJFm55ex.problem: Flattened symbolic-music language models place future conditioning information early in the sequence, creating a conflict between autoregressive order and musical time that disrupts temporal relationships.
F0NJFm55ex.method: A hierarchical grouping architecture organizes tokens into timing-aware groups (notes and concurrent onsets), and rotary time embeddings reassign temporal coordinates to the original musical times while leaving the input sequence and causal factorization unchanged. Training uses the standard next-token objective.
F0NJFm55ex.key_idea: Model-level temporal realignment: keep the causal token order but give each token a rotary embedding of its original musical time, on top of an onset-grouped hierarchy.
F0NJFm55ex.evidence: Same-architecture ablations across parameter allocations on timing perplexity and a coherence score under symbolic and audio conditioning, plus a listening study on infilling.
F0NJFm55ex.claimed_gains: Realignment substantially improves timing prediction, raises coherence scores under symbolic and audio conditioning, and a realigned model is rated significantly higher in a listening study; the abstract gives no numbers, while a review cites time-token perplexity falling from 2.57 to 1.80.
F0NJFm55ex.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the hierarchical token-note-onset formulation is well motivated for music and that same-architecture ablations show large, consistent effects.
F0NJFm55ex.main_concern: Reviewers say prior work already studies musical timing and conditioning order, the gain from realignment is not isolated because a flat baseline matches the realigned timing perplexity, and the writing and evaluation are underdeveloped.

q27c1fw7O9.one_liner: Alternates adversarial attack and repair rounds to evolve LLM-generated rubrics that resist reward hacking in rubric-based RL.
q27c1fw7O9.problem: Rubrics generated directly by LLMs omit or underspecify criteria, so a policy can earn high rubric rewards with low-quality responses, and existing generation methods do not proactively guard against this reward hacking.
q27c1fw7O9.method: RubricArmor alternates an attack step, which builds adversarial responses that satisfy the current rubric but fail the task, with a repair step that revises the rubric to catch the exposed defects while preserving other valid criteria, over multiple rounds.
q27c1fw7O9.key_idea: Simulate policy reward hacking with adversarial responses at rubric-generation time and patch each exposed defect, repeating attack and repair.
q27c1fw7O9.evidence: Direct LLM-as-a-judge evaluation with generated rubrics and rubric-based GRPO training, across multiple benchmarks, models and baselines (per reviews).
q27c1fw7O9.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says it outperforms competitive baselines without numbers)
q27c1fw7O9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the attack-then-repair approach is clear, well matched to rubric reward hacking, and supported by consistent gains across benchmarks and RL training.
q27c1fw7O9.main_concern: Reviewers say reward-hacking resistance is not directly verified, a static attacker may miss new hacking behavior as the policy evolves, and baselines are not compute-matched despite multiple rounds of LLM calls.

M38068rlvo.one_liner: Learns a low-dimensional hidden-state intervention space in a frozen language model and searches it with Bayesian optimization for black-box discovery.
M38068rlvo.problem: Iterative prompting and parameter updates give limited control over how completely a language model's search space is explored, and Bayesian optimization needs a suitable continuous domain to operate over.
M38068rlvo.method: BOReFT learns a compact space of hidden-state interventions in a frozen LM and uses it as the search domain for Bayesian optimization with an external scoring function. Theory shows semantic coverage and interpolation control the best reachable score and that decoding yields a stochastic-bandit observation model.
M38068rlvo.key_idea: Make the learned low-dimensional intervention codes the continuous domain for Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization, decoding each code through the frozen LM.
M38068rlvo.evidence: The Semantle word-search task and three de novo molecule property optimization tasks against strong LLM baselines, with 5 seeds (per a review).
M38068rlvo.claimed_gains: Finds a higher number of hidden targets in Semantle and achieves higher property scores on two of three molecular objectives than strong LLM baselines (no numbers in the abstract).
M38068rlvo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that moving discrete proposal generation into a learned continuous intervention space is a promising, controllable approach with a clear theoretical presentation and fair baselines.
M38068rlvo.main_concern: Reviewers say the components are largely from prior work (LoReFT, VAE-style learning, GP-based BO) and resemble LOLBO, the manifold claim is not established, and seeds and training cost are limited or unreported.

tcsQppcisk.one_liner: Trains a differential reward model on paired RTL edits as a fast PPA reward for RL, with periodic real-synthesis audits.
tcsQppcisk.problem: Rewarding power, performance and area (PPA) in RL for RTL generation needs logic synthesis per design, orders of magnitude slower than other checks, and absolute PPA predictors have errors larger than most optimization effects.
tcsQppcisk.method: DiffRTL trains a differential reward model on verified transformation pairs from a paired data engine, uses its fast forward pass as the PPA reward, and corrects it during training with periodic real-synthesis audits. All reported numbers remain grounded in real simulation, formal equivalence checking and synthesis.
tcsQppcisk.key_idea: Predict the relative PPA effect of an edit from paired examples, where systematic errors cancel, instead of absolute PPA.
tcsQppcisk.evidence: Pluto and RTLLMv2 benchmarks, comparing against synthesis-rewarded training at several budgets and an absolute predictor trained on identical data, with reward over-optimization measured by audits.
tcsQppcisk.claimed_gains: With 640 synthesis calls spent on audits alone, DiffRTL beats synthesis-rewarded training at six times the budget by 6.8 eff@1 points on Pluto, with matching gains on RTLLMv2.
tcsQppcisk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree expensive synthesis feedback is a real bottleneck for RL on RTL and that updating a proxy reward model with real synthesis results reduces the proxy-versus-real gap.
tcsQppcisk.main_concern: Reviewers say results depend on the Yosys plus OpenSTA flow (gains may not hold under commercial synthesis), baselines get far fewer updates than DiffRTL, and corpus and reward-model construction costs are not amortized.

YWBTOdJMVO.one_liner: Benchmark and shift-adaptive framework for estimating average treatment effects from text under covariate and posterior shift, with doubly robust aggregation.
YWBTOdJMVO.problem: ATE estimation with open-ended text covariates is hard, especially when source and target populations differ in covariates and causal mechanisms, and LLM abilities alone do not ensure reliable effect estimates.
YWBTOdJMVO.method: TRACE-Bench is an end-to-end benchmark built from social narratives for ATE estimation across shifted domains. TRACE retains transferable source information and adapts the mechanisms that change; TRACE-AGENT learns and adapts natural-language contexts before doubly robust aggregation, and TRACE-NN is an LLM-free, factor-augmented neural realization.
YWBTOdJMVO.key_idea: Decompose ATE estimation into nuisance-function fitting, transfer of source information and adaptation of shifted mechanisms, then aggregate with a doubly robust estimator.
YWBTOdJMVO.evidence: TRACE-Bench built from social narratives (a single Reddit moral-judgment corpus with LLM-generated outcomes per reviews), tested across six LLMs against generic agent and statistical baselines, with a double-robustness proof.
YWBTOdJMVO.claimed_gains: TRACE-AGENT consistently improves ATE estimation over generic agent baselines across foundation models, and TRACE-NN remains competitive with substantially larger LLMs (no numbers in the abstract).
YWBTOdJMVO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree causal estimation from text under covariate and mechanism shift is important and underexplored, and that TRACE-Bench and the decomposed pipeline are valuable.
YWBTOdJMVO.main_concern: Reviewers say the evidence is limited to semi-synthetic tasks from one text corpus and one family of shifts, the benefit of transfer and the statistical baselines (such as pooled-data and CausalBERT) are not convincingly tested, and the theory needs strong identification and nuisance-convergence assumptions.

IKCOkSUj2g.one_liner: Post hoc Bayesian belief tracking fuses generation uncertainty and tool outcomes to score whether an LLM agent trajectory succeeded.
IKCOkSUj2g.problem: Existing uncertainty quantification assesses individual LLM generations, leaving open how to aggregate and propagate uncertainty across different action types (generations, tool calls, revisions) in an agent trajectory.
IKCOkSUj2g.method: They formulate UQ for agents as Bayesian belief tracking over final task correctness, integrating generation-level uncertainty with tool outcomes through Bayesian updates. It needs no change to the harness or LLM and runs post hoc on recorded trajectories without extra agent executions.
IKCOkSUj2g.key_idea: Sum learned log-likelihood-ratio evidence from generation uncertainty and tool results into a posterior over final correctness, with variants modeling trajectory length, history and final step.
IKCOkSUj2g.evidence: Five LLMs, eight agent harnesses and 15 agentic environments spanning coding, retrieval and interactive tasks, with in-domain and transfer tests.
IKCOkSUj2g.claimed_gains: Basic Bayesian fusion achieves the highest average outcome-ranking scores on coding and retrieval, while a variant modeling trajectory length, history and final-step evidence leads on interactive tasks (no numbers in the abstract).
IKCOkSUj2g.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the estimator is practical and low-cost (post hoc, no retraining or new rollouts) and that the evaluation is broad across retrieval, coding and interactive domains.
IKCOkSUj2g.main_concern: Reviewers say novelty is limited (basic fusion is naive Bayes and the belief-tracking framing is overstated), training labels for partial-credit tasks such as DeepSWE are unspecified, and ablations do not isolate the added structure.

bGrcnHxEcc.one_liner: Learns initial-noise and denoising-update corrections so few-step diffusion samplers produce previews that match full-step outputs from the same noise.
bGrcnHxEcc.problem: Users generate and discard many text-to-image candidates, and standard few-step samplers give poor previews of the full-step output even though that output is reproducible by a few-step sampler with optimized noise.
bGrcnHxEcc.method: Observing that optimizing only the initial noise lets frozen 3-4-step samplers closely reproduce full-step outputs, they learn corrections to the initial noise and denoising updates using endpoint supervision. The input correction transfers across sampling budgets without retraining.
bGrcnHxEcc.key_idea: Learn a noise corrector and update corrections trained by endpoint supervision against full-step outputs generated from the same noise and prompt.
bGrcnHxEcc.evidence: SD1.5, SDXL and FLUX.1-dev, measuring reference fidelity, ranking preservation and candidate selection, plus an SDXL human study.
bGrcnHxEcc.claimed_gains: In an SDXL human study, mean ratings of agreement between expectations and the selected full-step images are 4.29/5 versus 3.42/5 for the best baseline.
bGrcnHxEcc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the preview problem is practical and the method is simple and effective, with an interesting motivating experiment on optimizing initial noise.
bGrcnHxEcc.main_concern: Reviewers say positioning against endpoint-matching few-step distillation is unclear, evaluation relies on automatic scorers with few prompts and some unconditional benchmarks, and the corrections have limited theoretical explanation.

6ORcmjnntX.one_liner: Extends all 40 LIBERO tasks with moving objects and model-specific inference latency to benchmark robotic manipulation in dynamic environments.
6ORcmjnntX.problem: Most manipulation benchmarks keep targets static and treat policy inference as instantaneous, hiding how a moving target evolves during computation and how stale an observation is when its action executes.
6ORcmjnntX.method: LIBERO-Dynamic drives objects through contact friction along three trajectory families and three speed tiers while advancing the physical world according to calibrated, model-specific inference latency. The same mechanism produces 9,000 quality-filtered dynamic training trajectories by replaying static demonstrations with online action compensation.
6ORcmjnntX.key_idea: Advance the simulated world during policy inference time, and generate dynamic demonstrations by compensating replayed static actions with the target's displacement.
6ORcmjnntX.evidence: Six pretrained policies on 1,800 dynamic conditions per configuration, comparisons of execution strategies and action horizons with fixed checkpoints, and fine-tuning of three model variants on dynamic and mixed data.
6ORcmjnntX.claimed_gains: not stated as improvements; as a benchmark paper it reports that faster motion degrades every evaluated policy, though not uniformly.
6ORcmjnntX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree dynamic, latency-aware evaluation is practically relevant and that same-checkpoint sweeps and action-queue analysis give useful diagnostics beyond aggregate success rates.
6ORcmjnntX.main_concern: Reviewers question the added value over DOMINO and ReflexBench, the realism of the simulated timing model given limited real-world evidence, and unclear physical-time budgets across execution strategies.

V7HWfIOnRw.one_liner: Unified visual tokenizer adding a magnitude-regularized residual to a frozen VFM, with reconstruction and semantic facets as generative targets.
V7HWfIOnRw.problem: Unified image generation and editing need a visual representation that keeps both semantic structure and fine-grained detail, but existing unified tokenizers fine-tune pretrained vision foundation models under semantic and reconstruction supervision.
V7HWfIOnRw.method: UniFacet keeps the VFM frozen as a semantic anchor and learns a lightweight, magnitude-regularized residual branch to recover image-specific details, compresses the unified representation into a compact reconstruction facet for decoding, and derives a semantic facet from the same representation. UniFacet-1.5B predicts both facets jointly for text-to-image generation and instruction-guided editing.
V7HWfIOnRw.key_idea: Complete a frozen semantic representation with a magnitude-regularized residual, and generate a compact reconstruction facet together with a semantic facet from that same space.
V7HWfIOnRw.evidence: Reconstruction on COCO-512, understanding and alignment experiments, and a controlled same-backbone comparison on generation and editing (GEdit-EN) against UniTok and DualViTok (per reviews).
V7HWfIOnRw.claimed_gains: The abstract is cut off before results; reviews cite 32.95 dB PSNR on COCO-512 versus 26.60 for UniTok, and GEdit-EN improving from 6.29 to 7.35 over a dual-stream baseline.
V7HWfIOnRw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the design separating source-image conditioning from the compact generation target is reasonable and that same-backbone controlled comparisons support the benefit for editing.
V7HWfIOnRw.main_concern: Reviewers say the key design choice (a shared completed space for both facets) is not directly ablated, technical novelty over residual-encoder and joint flow-matching work is limited, and comparisons use different training data and settings.

h2KXDWMd6M.one_liner: Vision-language-action model for mobile manipulation with a two-stream clean-action transformer, near-far attention, and future geometric feature prediction.
h2KXDWMd6M.problem: Mobile manipulation needs perception that stays spatially grounded under continuous ego-motion and coordination of heterogeneous arm and base actions, which fixed-base policies avoid.
h2KXDWMd6M.method: Goku conditions its action expert on sparse multilevel VLM features, supervises the shared representation with a training-only branch that predicts future features of a frozen geometric teacher, and generates manipulation and body actions with MM-APT, a two-stream transformer that predicts clean action chunks. Masked near-far attention lets a longer tail read the near plan without rewriting a short horizon.
h2KXDWMd6M.key_idea: Predict clean action chunks in two coupled streams (arm and base) with asymmetric near-far attention masks, plus training-only future geometric feature prediction.
h2KXDWMd6M.evidence: Pretraining on 5,000+ hours of robot data (400K+ episodes, 12 datasets, 17 embodiments, including the new MM-30 dual-arm mobile manipulation dataset), evaluated on EBench, RoboCasa365, ManiSkill-HAB, LIBERO and real-world tasks, with component ablations.
h2KXDWMd6M.claimed_gains: Goku achieves 44.71% success on EBench, 61.2% on RoboCasa365, the highest mean success on three ManiSkill-HAB suites and 99.1% on LIBERO; replacing clean-action with velocity prediction lowers RoboCasa365 composite-seen success from 32.8% to 29.2%.
h2KXDWMd6M.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the architecture explicitly addresses base-arm coordination, MM-30 is a valuable dataset, and broad simulation results are strong.
h2KXDWMd6M.main_concern: Reviewers say the coordination architecture (two streams, near-far attention) is not directly ablated, component ablations omit large-scale pretraining, and real-world evaluation is limited.

djRYr6c5I9.one_liner: Plug-in patch selector builds spectrally guided multi-scale candidates and keeps a compact subset matching the full-lookback predictive distribution.
djRYr6c5I9.problem: Patch-based time series forecasters treat patching as a fixed tokenization step and pass all patches to the model regardless of predictive utility.
djRYr6c5I9.method: SPS splits patching into candidate generation (multi-scale intervals from dominant temporal periods) and candidate selection, learning a compact subset with an approximate posterior-preservation objective that matches the selected-patch predictive distribution to a full-lookback reference. They also propose the Information Preservation Sufficiency (IPS) metric.
djRYr6c5I9.key_idea: Select patches by matching the predictive distribution of the selected set to a full-lookback teacher distribution, over spectrally generated multi-scale candidates.
djRYr6c5I9.evidence: Standard multivariate forecasting benchmarks (eight datasets per a review) with multiple patch-based backbones including PatchTST, PatchMLP and SRSNet, plus IPS analyses.
djRYr6c5I9.claimed_gains: Improves information preservation and achieves strong forecasting accuracy while retaining fewer patches than existing patching baselines (no numbers in the abstract).
djRYr6c5I9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree separating candidate generation from candidate selection is a useful framing and that results across datasets and backbones are meaningful.
djRYr6c5I9.main_concern: Reviewers say IPS only measures agreement with one trained teacher and so does not establish preserved predictive information, and the spectral generator is not compared with fixed-scale or random multi-scale generators.

YAXalaMD3x.one_liner: Decomposes the rectangularization gap in robust MDPs into reachable defects and picks at most k dependency blocks to recouple.
YAXalaMD3x.problem: Rectangular robust MDPs let an adversary pick the worst transition independently at each time-state-action triple, which is overly pessimistic when transitions share an episode-persistent factor because locally adverse choices may not be jointly realizable.
YAXalaMD3x.method: For a fixed policy and transitions affine in shared scalar factors, they derive an exact decomposition of the rectangularization gap into nonnegative defects at reachable rows, giving computable certificates and a Global-Balance rule that jointly selects dependencies. They add a mixed-integer formulation, approximation and selection guarantees, and finite-data certificates valid after data-dependent selection.
YAXalaMD3x.key_idea: Decompose the rectangularization gap into nonnegative reachable-row defects and choose dependency blocks to recouple jointly, capturing complementarities between groups.
YAXalaMD3x.evidence: Theory (exact decomposition, approximation and finite-data guarantees) plus experiments on six- and eight-factor routing and queue systems and on inventory, crosswind and CliffWalking tasks.
YAXalaMD3x.claimed_gains: Restoring eight of ten blocks reduces held-out candidate-menu regret relative to full release, and in six-factor routing and queue systems retaining two pools recovers 89.5% of the full recoupling gain with four rather than 64 conditional evaluations.
YAXalaMD3x.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem of auditing rectangularization is well motivated and that the exact decomposition and the joint-selection insight (complementarities between blocks) are rigorous and useful.
YAXalaMD3x.main_concern: Reviewers say Global Balance's empirical advantage is inconsistent (on par with Matching in Table 3), the theory largely combines known tools with a loose chi^(H-1) term, and robustness to a misspecified sharing map is unclear.

fIpuldQA06.one_liner: On-policy quantization-aware distillation with reverse KL, layer-wise hidden-state alignment and a gated forward KL to recover capability under KV-cache quantization.
fIpuldQA06.problem: Naive off-policy QAD recovers only 41.5% of the loss for a 1.5B model under TurboQuant K2V3, because quantization flattens output distributions and suppresses key high-confidence tokens while off-policy QAD suffers exposure bias and layer-wise representation drift.
fIpuldQA06.method: OPQAD combines an on-policy backbone, reverse KL divergence, layer-wise hidden-state alignment, and a gated forward KL term that corrects suppressed tokens.
fIpuldQA06.key_idea: Distill on the student's own rollouts with reverse KL and hidden-state alignment, adding a gated forward-KL term on tokens the quantized model underestimates.
fIpuldQA06.evidence: Models from 1.5B to 8B on long chain-of-thought tasks up to 32K length under TurboQuant K2V3 and OSCAR, with out-of-distribution code and instruction-following tests and ablations.
fIpuldQA06.claimed_gains: Improves AIME24 accuracy by 6.0-7.3 percentage points over off-policy QAD under K2V3, raising the 1.5B model's recovery rate to 58.7%, with 9.7% training overhead.
fIpuldQA06.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the diagnosis of quantization-induced degradation is careful and goes beyond aggregate accuracy, and that OPQAD improves math and code capability under K2V3.
fIpuldQA06.main_concern: Reviewers say each component is a known technique so novelty is limited, the evaluation concentrates on K2V3, and ablations and overhead breakdowns are restricted to one model and setting.

7kqZOZecen.one_liner: Eliminates actions using Gaussian-width-guided linear constraints to reach near-optimal regret in contextual linear bandits with polylog oracle calls per round.
7kqZOZecen.problem: Achieving near-optimal O-tilde(d sqrt(T)) regret with efficient optimization over large convex action sets was open, since the efficient algorithm of Dani, Hayes and Kakade has O-tilde(d^(3/2) sqrt(T)) regret and oracle-efficient Thompson-sampling and spanner methods incur an extra sqrt(d) factor.
7kqZOZecen.method: The algorithm progressively removes suboptimal actions by adding linear constraints and measures remaining uncertainty by the Gaussian width of a rescaled feasible set, with the rescaling reflecting previously sampled actions. When the width is small it shrinks the set while preserving an optimal action with high probability; when it is large it samples a random direction to explore (the abstract is cut off).
7kqZOZecen.key_idea: Use the Gaussian width of a rescaled feasible set as the shared uncertainty measure that decides between eliminating actions with linear constraints and exploring a random direction.
7kqZOZecen.evidence: A theoretical regret proof for oblivious-adversary compact convex action sets under boundedness and sub-Gaussian noise assumptions; no experiments.
7kqZOZecen.claimed_gains: O-tilde(d sqrt(T)) regret with high probability using polylogarithmically many calls per round to a linear-optimization oracle for the action sets.
7kqZOZecen.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper addresses a long-standing open problem with an elegant Gaussian-width mechanism that achieves near-optimal regret without enumerating the action set.
7kqZOZecen.main_concern: Reviewers say the main oracle (optimizing over the action set intersected with extra halfspaces) is stronger than an ordinary linear-optimization oracle, which complicates comparison, and that no empirical evaluation is provided.

gPmuNR8nOW.one_liner: Benchmark over a 1.62M-triple biomedical knowledge graph that varies structure and relation-level context independently on the same QA instances.
gPmuNR8nOW.problem: Context-free triples can make distinct candidate hypotheses observationally equivalent, since they share the same topology while the distinguishing observation is absent, which is an identifiability problem at the reasoning interface.
gPmuNR8nOW.method: They build structurally underdetermined questions where relation-level context breaks the symmetry, over a biomedical KG of 1.62M triples (75% with textual evidence or structured metadata), and vary structure and context independently, with controls such as random-context replacement, context swapping and evidence-count debiasing.
gPmuNR8nOW.key_idea: Make candidate hypotheses structurally indistinguishable so that only relation-level context (conditions, evidence, measurements) identifies the answer, then toggle context independently of structure.
gPmuNR8nOW.evidence: Seven LLMs on the benchmark with controls for relation-matched content, evidence-count debiasing and missing structural support, plus a manual audit of 300 records (per a review).
gPmuNR8nOW.claimed_gains: Adding context to explicit candidate paths raises Medium-level accuracy from 61.35% to 89.56% (+28.20 pp), and the gain persists (+14.83 pp) when the graph is retrieved from the question alone.
gPmuNR8nOW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled comparisons cleanly isolate the effect of relation-level context and that the large knowledge graph with a seven-model evaluation gives useful empirical evidence.
gPmuNR8nOW.main_concern: Reviewers say the gold answers are not shown to be scientifically supported or uniquely warranted (limited human audit), the findings largely confirm the expected benefit of restoring omitted information, and the title overstates the scope.

Z5cwKjUXtQ.one_liner: Two-pass latent visual reasoning that constructs a visual-semantic latent block from sampled seeds, then replays it for answer generation.
Z5cwKjUXtQ.problem: Latent Visual Reasoning aligns hidden-state latents directly with visual tokens, which overlooks their distinct roles, and uses ground-truth RoI visual tokens in training but self-generated latents at inference, creating a training-inference gap.
Z5cwKjUXtQ.method: CR^2 first samples latent seeds from a distribution matched to the visual-token norm distribution and transforms them with a latent head into a multi-token latent block, supervised by RoI visual features and answer-related content. Pass-II replays this block as the reasoning state for answer generation, with the same procedure in training and inference.
Z5cwKjUXtQ.key_idea: Construct the latent block from norm-matched seeds in one pass and replay it in a second pass, using the same procedure in training and inference to remove the mismatch.
Z5cwKjUXtQ.evidence: 3B and 7B backbones on ten multi-modal benchmarks against SFT and LVR baselines, with latent replacement experiments, representation probing and ablations.
Z5cwKjUXtQ.claimed_gains: At the 7B scale, CR^2 improves OCRBench and BLINK Spatial Relation by 2.5% and further figures that are cut off in the provided abstract.
Z5cwKjUXtQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper identifies a real training-inference mismatch in latent visual reasoning and that gains over SFT on the same data are consistent, with analyses supporting the constructed latents.
Z5cwKjUXtQ.main_concern: Reviewers say the gains may come from the two-pass structure rather than the visual-semantic supervision, the training-inference gap comparison is not matched, and baselines and benchmark coverage (especially at 7B) are limited.

tZaHwMrvq2.one_liner: Causal activation patching localizes prompt-injection compliance to a low-rank late-layer bottleneck, which is also the best site for detection.
tZaHwMrvq2.problem: Prior work quantified how often prompt injections succeed but not where inside the network the model decides to abandon its system role.
tZaHwMrvq2.method: Layer-by-layer causal activation patching across five models (4B to 32B) measures each layer's causal leverage over compliance, while linear probes test where attack information is decodable. Patching the identified bottleneck reverses compliance, and probes at that layer are used for attack detection.
tZaHwMrvq2.key_idea: Attack information is decodable from layer one but causally effective only in a low-rank late-layer subspace, which is also the best layer for detection probes.
tZaHwMrvq2.evidence: Causal activation patching on five models from 4B to 32B parameters with control baselines, and a detection comparison against early-layer classifiers under leetspeak obfuscation.
tZaHwMrvq2.claimed_gains: Patching the bottleneck reverses compliance in 77-92% of cases; the compliance subspace is rank-8 in 4B and 14B models and rank-64 at 32B.
tZaHwMrvq2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the dissociation between decodability and causal leverage is interesting and the causal patching experiments with controls are well designed and clearly written.
tZaHwMrvq2.main_concern: Generalization across models is weakly shown: most analysis is on Qwen3-4B, the peak layer shifts across model families, and the paper offers no new attack or defense beyond the observation.

JpAWLxt7Xe.one_liner: ZoomSIB-UCB estimates the projection direction with a normalized Stein estimator, then runs UCB over adaptively discretized one-dimensional bins.
JpAWLxt7Xe.problem: For single-index bandits with non-monotone unknown reward functions, the best known regret was O-tilde(T^(3/4)), leaving a gap to the optimal rate.
JpAWLxt7Xe.method: A two-phase algorithm first estimates the projection direction via a normalized Stein estimator, then uses adaptive exploration and discretization to run UCB over the resulting one-dimensional bins. It does not need to know mu* or a lower bound on its magnitude.
JpAWLxt7Xe.key_idea: Estimate the index direction once with a normalized Stein estimator, then treat the problem as a one-dimensional bandit solved by UCB over adaptively zoomed bins.
JpAWLxt7Xe.evidence: A regret upper bound, a matching minimax lower bound, and experiments under different reward functions f.
JpAWLxt7Xe.claimed_gains: Regret of O-tilde(T^(2/3)) versus the prior best O-tilde(T^(3/4)), with a matching minimax lower bound of Omega-tilde(T^(2/3)).
JpAWLxt7Xe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theoretical contribution is clear: a simple algorithm with an improved regret upper bound and a matching lower bound, with rigorous proofs.
JpAWLxt7Xe.main_concern: The dependence on mu* (including mu* near zero) and the exact assumptions are unclear, the algorithm acts like explore-then-commit with a frozen estimate, and parts of the paper are hard to read.

EvigzD2Hze.one_liner: Participant-level contrastive pretraining of a foundation model on 2.75M hours of in-bed ballistocardiography from 145,857 people.
EvigzD2Hze.problem: Biosignal foundation models rely on wearables or sleep labs that require deliberate user action, leaving ambient, effortless modalities such as in-bed BCG without a foundation model.
EvigzD2Hze.method: BCG-FM is pretrained with participant-level contrastive learning on nightly piezoelectric bed-sensor recordings. A second pretraining stage has each minute predict how the embeddings of neighboring minutes differ from its own.
EvigzD2Hze.key_idea: Pretrain with participant-level contrastive learning, then add a stage where each minute predicts how neighboring-minute embeddings differ from its own.
EvigzD2Hze.evidence: Frozen-embedding evaluation on biological-age estimation, 15 self-reported health conditions, and two external clinical cohorts, plus label-efficiency and batch-size scaling analyses.
EvigzD2Hze.claimed_gains: 3.26-year MAE on biological-age estimation (lowest reported for any ambient, contactless modality); representations from only 500 labeled participants outperform a supervised baseline trained on 3,372.
EvigzD2Hze.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree bed-based BCG is an under-explored, practical modality and the pretraining corpus is far larger than prior BCG studies, with frozen-probe and label-efficiency evaluations.
EvigzD2Hze.main_concern: Comparisons are weak: baselines are demographic-only or simple supervised models without validated BCG features or other biosignal foundation models, and data come from one sensor with self-reported labels.

vTCwPX06pU.one_liner: Retrieval-augmented agent skill optimization that retrieves existing skills and adapts them across harnesses for initialization and iterative updates.
vTCwPX06pU.problem: Existing skill optimization relies on expensive agent rollouts and ignores millions of publicly shared skills, which differ from the target task in domain and harness.
vTCwPX06pU.method: RASO retrieves relevant knowledge from an external skill corpus and adapts it to the target task and harness through Cross-Harness Adaptation. RASI builds a knowledge-grounded initial skill without rollouts, and RASU iteratively refines the skill by retrieving external knowledge guided by execution feedback.
vTCwPX06pU.key_idea: Retrieve section-level knowledge from existing skills with BM25 and rewrite it for the target harness, both to initialize skills without rollouts and to update them from feedback.
vTCwPX06pU.evidence: Four agent benchmarks (including ALFWorld, WebShop, SpreadsheetBench and OfficeQA) and two models, with matched-rollout-budget comparisons and init/update ablations.
vTCwPX06pU.claimed_gains: RASO consistently outperforms baselines without retrieval-augmented skill optimization across four agent benchmarks and two models; no numbers are stated in the abstract.
vTCwPX06pU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, broadly applicable and well controlled, with rollout-free initialization giving real gains at matched or lower rollout cost.
vTCwPX06pU.main_concern: The benefit of the retrieved content is not isolated from the extra generation step and the LLM's own knowledge, since the retrieval-free control is constrained and no random-retrieval control exists.

W2qWeMOXr5.one_liner: Trains LLMs to resolve source authority from explicit policy declarations using randomized pointers, shuffled order, and authority-flip augmentation with RLVR.
W2qWeMOXr5.problem: Role-based instruction-hierarchy training ties authority to fixed source roles, so models learn role-authority priors that attackers exploit through role imitation or authoritative framing.
W2qWeMOXr5.method: RAB assigns randomized pointers to sources, shuffles their presentation order, and states each source's executability and precedence in a separate authority policy, with authority-flip augmentation that changes authority assignments while preserving content. Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards reinforces policy lookup and binding.
W2qWeMOXr5.key_idea: Randomizing source identifiers and flipping authority assignments forces the model to look up authority in the policy declaration instead of relying on role-authority associations.
W2qWeMOXr5.evidence: Comparison with a role-based baseline trained on the same data on IHEval, BIPIA, semantic attacks, and adaptive PIArena attacks, across models including Qwen3-14B.
W2qWeMOXr5.claimed_gains: Improves IHEval conflict adherence by up to 20.4%p over a role-based baseline trained on the same data; the adaptive-attack results are cut off in the provided abstract.
W2qWeMOXr5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find separating source authority from fixed roles valuable and credit the thorough robustness testing and ablations.
W2qWeMOXr5.main_concern: Mixed external results: on Qwen3-14B RAB does worse than role-based training on BIPIA and adaptive PIArena, and the authority-flip augmentation is not ablated in isolation.

zDd2Hm1Xzs.one_liner: Proves score-only probabilities lose calibration as best-of-N budget grows, while rank-aware probabilities stay calibrated at every budget.
zDd2Hm1Xzs.problem: A probability calibrated for a typical candidate need not stay calibrated for the selected best-of-N answer as N grows, so calibration at small budgets may not carry to larger ones.
zDd2Hm1Xzs.method: Theoretical analysis of how calibration at budgets 1 to K constrains calibration at larger N, for probabilities depending only on the verifier score and for probabilities that also depend on the score's rank among candidates for the same prompt, including finite-sample estimation error.
zDd2Hm1Xzs.key_idea: Let the reported correctness probability depend on the score's rank among the prompt's candidates, not only the score, so calibration can hold at every budget.
zDd2Hm1Xzs.evidence: Theorems with explicit bounds (trivial for score-only probabilities once N is much larger than K squared; error growing at most like sqrt(N) times estimation error for rank-based ones) and experiments comparing a rank-based probability fitted once with score recalibration at each budget.
zDd2Hm1Xzs.claimed_gains: In experiments, rank-using probabilities fitted only once stay nearly as well calibrated as a score recalibrated at each budget; no numbers stated.
zDd2Hm1Xzs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theory gives a clear, precise explanation of why calibration fails after selection, including the K-squared threshold and a matching raw-score construction, with the rank identified as the key quantity.
zDd2Hm1Xzs.main_concern: Practical benefit is unproven: the quadratic extrapolation range requires exact calibration at budgets 1 to K, seven of eight endpoint improvements have intervals including zero, and a fixed-N score-only recalibration baseline is missing.

YJ8Ar8qmTF.one_liner: Asynchronous hierarchical imitation learning with a slow Option Transformer for vector-quantized skills and a fast Decision Transformer for actions.
YJ8Ar8qmTF.problem: Joint training of discrete skill hierarchies in language-conditioned imitation learning can produce concentrated codebook usage and unstable skill representations.
YJ8Ar8qmTF.method: DASL independently sets the semantic update interval and low-level trajectory horizon, supervises each shared skill with actions across its interval, and regularizes skill-conditioned latent trajectories with a diffusion module used only during training. A slow Option Transformer predicts vector-quantized skills and a Decision Transformer generates actions from full-rate observations without diffusion sampling at inference.
YJ8Ar8qmTF.key_idea: Decouple the skill update interval from the control horizon, supervise each skill with all actions in its interval, and use a diffusion regularizer only at training time.
YJ8Ar8qmTF.evidence: LOReL, Franka Kitchen, a six-task CALVIN-D state-based protocol, BabyAI, and a real robot, with codebook diagnostics and an interval-supervision ablation.
YJ8Ar8qmTF.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says skill acquisition and compositional performance improve in these settings, without numbers)
YJ8Ar8qmTF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the comprehensive ablations and direct codebook diagnostics (active codes, usage entropy) and the efficient inference path enabled by training-only diffusion.
YJ8Ar8qmTF.main_concern: Contributions overlap existing mechanisms (interval supervision resembles gradients already present in straight-through training), the LISA comparison uses mismatched temporal settings, and compositional generalization evidence is limited.

pUj6uDM1SK.one_liner: Fine-tunes LLMs on user-turn messages only to implant beliefs, preferences, and propensities in the assistant.
pUj6uDM1SK.problem: The user turn is an important but understudied lever for shaping an LLM's traits.
pUj6uDM1SK.method: User Message Fine-tuning trains on corpora of user messages that reference a false fact, a made-up fact about the user, praise or criticism of answers, or positive reactions to misaligned responses, tested on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Qwen3-8B.
pUj6uDM1SK.key_idea: Compute the fine-tuning loss only on user turns, so reactions and statements in user messages shift the assistant's own beliefs and preferences.
pUj6uDM1SK.evidence: Four case studies on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Qwen3-8B: false-fact belief compared with synthetic document fine-tuning, made-up user facts, preference steering via praised answers, and reduced emergent misalignment, with appendix replications of three settings.
pUj6uDM1SK.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract says the model believes a false fact about as strongly as after synthetic document fine-tuning and shows less emergent misalignment after later fine-tuning.
pUj6uDM1SK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea of shaping assistant behavior through user turns interesting and surprising, with a broad set of case studies and good presentation.
pUj6uDM1SK.main_concern: Evidence is a few single-example case studies on Qwen models, and the claimed advantage over synthetic document fine-tuning is not isolated from the extra warm-up adapter or shown across several facts.

78YLfEclO6.one_liner: Trains VLA policies with RL using task-wise progress-potential reward shaping and phase-conditioned hidden-state alignment to compose atomic skills.
78YLfEclO6.problem: VLA models succeed on single skills but drop sharply on sequential composite tasks, where sparse binary rewards give little signal and composite instructions leave subtask transitions ambiguous.
78YLfEclO6.method: Learns reusable progress potentials from successful and failed atomic rollouts and composes them across stages into dense phase-aware rewards, and aligns hidden states across phases (cut off in the abstract) so composite conditioning invokes the policy's atomic competence.
78YLfEclO6.key_idea: Reuse the policy's own atomic-task competence by shaping rewards with composed per-task progress potentials and aligning composite-instruction representations with atomic ones.
78YLfEclO6.evidence: Composite tasks of two subtasks with ablations (Table 4) and preliminary physical-robot results per reviews; the abstract is cut off before experiments.
78YLfEclO6.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract.
78YLfEclO6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the combination of potential-based shaping and hidden-state alignment addresses sparse feedback and subtask ambiguity without an extra planner or inference-time prompt switching, with substantial improvements and a clear presentation.
78YLfEclO6.main_concern: Ablations do not separate shaping and alignment from joint atomic-plus-composite training, and evaluation is mostly limited to two-subtask composites.

FfasnoEYRB.one_liner: Nemotron-Cascade 2 is a 30B MoE (3B active) post-trained with scaled Cascade RL and multi-domain on-policy distillation.
FfasnoEYRB.problem: Scaling RL across many reasoning and agentic domains risks benchmark regressions from cross-domain interference as training proceeds.
FfasnoEYRB.method: After SFT on a curated dataset, Cascade RL is scaled to a broader set of reasoning and agentic domains, grouping compatible domains with similar response lengths and verification costs. Multi-domain on-policy distillation from the strongest intermediate checkpoint in each domain recovers regressions and sustains gains.
FfasnoEYRB.key_idea: Group compatible domains for staged Cascade RL, and distill on-policy from each domain's strongest intermediate checkpoint to recover regressions.
FfasnoEYRB.evidence: Stage-wise benchmark analysis including IMO 2025, IOI, ICPC World Finals, LiveCodeBench v6, AIME25 and IFBench; model checkpoint and training data are released.
FfasnoEYRB.claimed_gains: Gold Medal-level performance on the 2025 IMO, IOI and ICPC World Finals with 20x fewer parameters than DeepSeek-V3.2-Speciale-671B-A37B, making it the second open-weight LLM to do so.
FfasnoEYRB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the 3B-active model delivers strong math and coding results and that the open release with stage-wise analysis is valuable.
FfasnoEYRB.main_concern: Methodological novelty is incremental, combining established techniques, and the gains from domain grouping and MOPD are not isolated by ablations or compute-matched comparisons.

lDH9P2ZZ4i.one_liner: Graph in-context learning through sparse message passing, pretrained on synthetic structural-causal-model graph tasks.
lDH9P2ZZ4i.problem: Existing graph in-context learning models use dense attention across nodes, limiting inference efficiency and scalability.
lDH9P2ZZ4i.method: Ephris predicts missing node labels from observed labels as context using sparse message passing that scales linearly with node-feature entries and graph edges. It is pretrained entirely on synthetic tasks from structural causal models extended with diverse graph structures and relational dynamics.
lDH9P2ZZ4i.key_idea: Context and query nodes interact through sparse message passing on the observed graph instead of all-to-all cross-node attention, with pretraining on synthetic graph-structured causal-model tasks.
lDH9P2ZZ4i.evidence: 51 node-classification datasets against 15 tuned GNNs and prior graph ICL models under high-label (50/25/25) and low-label (10/10/80) splits, plus an architecture-prior factorial study per reviews.
lDH9P2ZZ4i.claimed_gains: Ranks 1st on all four aggregate metrics (Elo, improvability, average rank, accuracy) in both label regimes, with inference cost comparable to a single GNN training run.
lDH9P2ZZ4i.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the scalability limit of dense-attention graph ICL is an important problem and that the evaluation is extensive, with 51 datasets and many tuned baselines.
lDH9P2ZZ4i.main_concern: Limited methodological novelty (a composition of existing modules), plus fairness questions over label propagation and an evaluation on classic datasets with narrow coverage.

PBocXiFDHT.one_liner: Black-box fingerprint ranks candidate words for an ambiguous word under growing context to identify an LLM's source family.
PBocXiFDHT.problem: Watermarking needs proactive deployment and white-box fingerprinting needs parameter access, so family-level provenance of derivative LLMs from black-box responses remains hard under fine-tuning, distillation, or merging.
PBocXiFDHT.method: FamilyTrace asks a model to rank candidate words by their relation to an ambiguous word, first with little context and then with progressively more context, and compares the rankings with family profiles. It supports closed-set attribution among known families and open-set rejection of unknown families using 24 text queries per model.
PBocXiFDHT.key_idea: Models in the same family share word-association rankings, because pre-training knowledge in feed-forward layers survives small post-training changes, so rank agreement on ambiguous anchor words fingerprints the family.
PBocXiFDHT.evidence: Comparison with seven baselines over model modifications, leave-one-out reference libraries, and 100 query-list variations; Proposition 1 interprets profile similarity as normalized rank agreement.
PBocXiFDHT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the design is simple, efficient, and practical for API auditing, needing only 24 text queries and supporting both known-family attribution and unknown-family rejection, with comprehensive experiments.
PBocXiFDHT.main_concern: Leave-one-out evaluation keeps near-duplicate variants of the target in the reference library, and closed-set attribution drops from 96.3% to 55.6% when models fine-tuned on the same dataset are removed.

TMULQtRGoc.one_liner: A verifier predicts future representations in a VLA's own space to score action-chunk prefixes and set the execution horizon.
TMULQtRGoc.problem: Adaptive action-chunk methods pick the execution horizon from generation stability or prediction agreement, which does not show whether executing a prefix preserves the ability to complete the task.
TMULQtRGoc.method: PAV evaluates existing candidate action prefixes in the VLA's internal task-conditioned representation space rather than generating actions. It is trained with trajectory-level survival supervision plus a localization prior that preserves useful behavior within failed rollouts, and its validity scores select the execution horizon.
TMULQtRGoc.key_idea: Train a verifier from terminal task outcomes with survival supervision and a localization prior, then use its validity scores on predicted future representations to pick how far to execute.
TMULQtRGoc.evidence: pi_0 and pi_0.5 on LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and real-world manipulation, with ablations and comparisons against adaptive baselines such as AutoHorizon.
TMULQtRGoc.claimed_gains: Improved success-query trade-offs across LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and real-world manipulation; no numbers stated.
TMULQtRGoc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that balancing efficiency and responsiveness in action-chunk VLA execution is important and that evaluating the consequences of candidate prefixes is a reasonable alternative to stability-based horizon selection.
TMULQtRGoc.main_concern: The verifier is trained only from terminal outcomes and is not shown to estimate true continuation validity, and real-world evaluation details are left as TBD.

bqvm1nrPHF.one_liner: An LLM edits an ASCII-art state over turns; an image editor then renders RGB from it and the original image.
bqvm1nrPHF.problem: Sequential multi-turn image editing with image editors drifts from the source image across turns, costs inference time and energy, and offers no discrete, inspectable edit state.
bqvm1nrPHF.method: At each turn an LLM updates the ASCII art and a scene prompt from the user instruction. After the final turn, an image editing model synthesizes an RGB image from the updated state, the aggregated edit instruction, and the original image; reviewers mention a trained ControlNet.
bqvm1nrPHF.key_idea: Use ASCII art as a discrete visual bottleneck that an LLM edits each turn, deferring RGB synthesis to the last turn with the original image as reference.
bqvm1nrPHF.evidence: Four-turn editing sequences compared against six editors with CLIP-I, AugCLIP, MANIQA, and MUSIQ plus a prompt-only baseline; reviewers note only 25 source images and training on human, human-object, and human-animal scenes.
bqvm1nrPHF.claimed_gains: Smallest decline in CLIP-I and AugCLIP among six editors over four turns, highest fourth-turn AugCLIP, MANIQA, and MUSIQ, and 60.2% less inference time and 90.9% less GPU energy than sequential Qwen-Edit.
bqvm1nrPHF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using ASCII art as an inspectable intermediate editing state is a new idea and that separating it from the original appearance reference is a sound design, with promising efficiency results.
bqvm1nrPHF.main_concern: The ASCII state's independent benefit is not established (a prompt-only baseline scores about the same on CLIP-I and AugCLIP), and the evaluation uses only 25 sequences with global metrics that do not measure edit correctness.

ntTTitzD1q.one_liner: Learns an orthonormal latent basis jointly with state-action-conditioned gains to modulate latent world-model predictions across subspaces.
ntTTitzD1q.problem: Latent world models organize prediction along latent directions whose basis and relative weighting are usually predefined rather than learned.
ntTTitzD1q.method: Orthogonal subspace modulation jointly learns an orthonormal basis and adaptive gains conditioned on the current state and action; the basis sets where modulation acts and the gains set how strongly each direction is used. Gain-Basis Coupling formalizes when the latent perspective becomes functionally consequential.
ntTTitzD1q.key_idea: Learn an orthonormal basis plus state-action-conditioned gains, so different subspaces receive different gains and the choice of basis changes the modulation operator.
ntTTitzD1q.evidence: Four visual-control tasks against latent world-model baselines, with ablations (Uniform Gain, Frozen Haar basis) and analyses of Gain-Basis Coupling, subspace coordination, and physical-dynamics accessibility.
ntTTitzD1q.claimed_gains: Improves control performance over strong latent world-model baselines across four visual-control tasks; no numbers stated.
ntTTitzD1q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is clearly structured and the targeted ablations and analyses (uniform gain, frozen basis, interventions) go beyond control scores to show where gains come from.
ntTTitzD1q.main_concern: It is unclear that learning an explicit orthogonal basis beats simpler conditional modulation such as FiLM or coordinate-aligned gating, and one reviewer finds improvements within baseline confidence intervals.

JkWvfI5c7X.one_liner: Object-centric spatial graphs consolidate multi-room video observations for static relations and changing object states.
JkWvfI5c7X.problem: VLMs struggle to maintain and update spatial knowledge across partial observations and room-boundary transitions.
JkWvfI5c7X.method: MUSHROOM evaluates static spatial relations and dynamic state changes during repeated multi-room traversal. SPORE organizes a single video's observations into an object-centric spatial graph without training.
JkWvfI5c7X.key_idea: Connect temporally distant video observations through an object-centric spatial graph to support geometric estimation and state updating.
JkWvfI5c7X.evidence: The benchmark contains 230 egocentric multi-room videos with static and dynamic tasks, and SPORE also receives evaluation on real-world indoor benchmarks.
JkWvfI5c7X.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value testing persistent spatial memory through repeated multi-room traversal before and after object relocations.
JkWvfI5c7X.main_concern: SPORE processes more video observations than the video-only baselines, confounding the reported benefit of its spatial representation.

6sny47o05l.one_liner: Rollout-reference overlap controls privileged solution exposure, while entropy ratios select sparse prefixes for target interpolation.
6sny47o05l.problem: On-policy reasoning supervision needs richer feedback than final rewards without exposing excessive privileged information or miscalibrating token targets.
6sny47o05l.method: PAINT uses overlap between student rollouts and verified solution anchors to choose how much solution context a privileged scorer sees. A teacher-student entropy ratio then selects sparse prefixes for small energy-space interpolations of token targets.
6sny47o05l.key_idea: Adapt solution-context masking using rollout-reference overlap and interpolate teacher-student token targets at sparse entropy-ratio-selected prefixes.
6sny47o05l.evidence: Experiments cover three competition-level math benchmarks and three Qwen3 scales, with masking and interpolation ablations and information-theoretic motivation.
6sny47o05l.claimed_gains: On Qwen3-8B, PAINT raises macro Avg@12 by 2.1 points over full-solution on-policy self-distillation and 2.9 points over GRPO.
6sny47o05l.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize a simple training modification with consistent reported improvements across model-benchmark combinations and no added inference operations.
6sny47o05l.main_concern: Unclear baseline provenance and uncertainty estimates leave the fairness and statistical reliability of the reported gains unresolved.

xsYoBJWWJo.one_liner: Action-conditioned soft transport of observed patch features lets ShiftWM forecast latent world states in parallel without regenerating static backgrounds.
xsYoBJWWJo.problem: Existing latent world models regenerate the entire feature grid autoregressively at every future step, which corrupts static backgrounds and compounds prediction errors in manipulation and surgical scenes.
xsYoBJWWJo.method: ShiftWM predicts an action-conditioned soft transport of nearby observed patch features without flow supervision, combines moved and kept features via a gate with a residual correction for new content, and decodes all future horizons in parallel. It also attaches as a plug-in output head to pretrained open-source world models.
xsYoBJWWJo.key_idea: Forecast future latent grids in parallel by predicting an action-conditioned soft transport of observed patch features, gating moved versus kept features, and adding a residual correction.
xsYoBJWWJo.evidence: Evaluated on held-out real-robot video from DROID, Language-Table, and bimanual IWS tasks, seven surgical tasks from Open-H, and as a plug-in head on the 1.3B-parameter V-JEPA 2-AC.
xsYoBJWWJo.claimed_gains: ShiftWM achieves feature-prediction error 7.6% below a matched direct predictor on DROID and lowers the error of the 1.3B-parameter V-JEPA 2-AC by 15.7% as a plug-in.
xsYoBJWWJo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that transporting rather than regenerating observed features is a well-motivated, simple idea that works cleanly as a plug-in head and delivers consistent forecasting improvements backed by thorough ablations.
xsYoBJWWJo.main_concern: All three reviewers note that evaluation focuses on latent feature prediction error rather than demonstrating closed-loop planning or downstream robotic task success.

8bFFxIE314.one_liner: Adversarially trained neural cellular automata learn a local, Markovian, time-invariant update rule to simulate spatial dynamics from unpaired snapshots.
8bFFxIE314.problem: Destructive biological measurements yield only discrete, unpaired snapshots that underdetermine underlying continuous spatiotemporal dynamics when modeled via unconstrained interpolation.
8bFFxIE314.method: REGIS parameterizes a spatially local, Markovian, and time-invariant update rule using neural cellular automata and iterates it to reach every observed timestamp. The rule is trained adversarially so that generated rollouts match the observed marginal snapshot distributions.
8bFFxIE314.key_idea: Constrain unpaired trajectory inference by iterating a single spatially local, Markovian, time-invariant neural cellular automaton rule trained adversarially against observed snapshot marginals.
8bFFxIE314.evidence: Evaluated on synthetic datasets within and beyond the training horizon and on a spatial atlas of zebrafish heart regeneration including an in silico functional screen.
8bFFxIE314.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear motivation of enforcing spatial locality and structural priors via neural cellular automata to learn an iterable simulator capable of rollout and perturbation analysis.
8bFFxIE314.main_concern: Reviewers question what resolves temporal non-identifiability from unpaired snapshots and point to missing comparisons against standard flow-matching, adversarial marginal-fitting, or local discrete diffusion baselines.

zQdjnjeikw.one_liner: Temporally ordered user task sequences and an extensible memory interface benchmark personalized preference tracking and proactive information acquisition.
zQdjnjeikw.problem: Existing LLM agent benchmarks focus on reasoning and tool use while overlooking how agents infer, update, and proactively clarify user preferences across fragmented long-term interactions.
zQdjnjeikw.method: VitaBench 2.0 organizes tasks as temporally ordered sequences per user with preferences embedded in heterogeneous interactions and tasks requiring proactive acquisition of missing information. It also provides an extensible memory interface for controlled comparisons across memory architectures.
zQdjnjeikw.key_idea: Evaluate long-term agent personalization and proactiveness along temporally ordered per-user task sequences paired with dynamic preference rubrics and an extensible memory interface.
zQdjnjeikw.evidence: Evaluates 27 LLM configurations and multiple memory architectures across 771 executable tasks spanning 56 users and over 2,000 human-annotated preferences.
zQdjnjeikw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark targets an important real-world problem with a well-designed temporal task structure that jointly tests service-action execution, preference updating, and proactive interaction.
zQdjnjeikw.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about realism and rubric design, citing manually constructed user histories, implicit habits treated as hard constraints, and rubrics that do not penalize unnecessary clarification questions.

L2sohbHEm9.one_liner: Support-variance layer weighting and decoupled detection-localization scoring fuse frozen multilevel DINOv2 features for training-free few-shot anomaly detection.
L2sohbHEm9.problem: Existing training-free few-shot industrial anomaly detectors combine multilevel features with fixed rules and share one anomaly response for detection and localization, magnifying harmless normal variations and fragmenting anomaly maps.
L2sohbHEm9.method: HIVE-AD builds an independent normal memory per selected frozen DINOv2 layer, sets each layer's weight from spatial variation in normal support images, and uses separate scoring branches for image-level ranking and pixel-level localization. An optional frozen MLLM converts localized anomaly regions into structured defect reports.
L2sohbHEm9.key_idea: Weight per-layer frozen DINOv2 nearest-neighbor memories using support-set spatial variation while separating image-level ranking from pixel-level localization scoring.
L2sohbHEm9.evidence: Evaluated in few-shot settings on MVTec-AD and VisA against a frozen DINOv2-G baseline and training-free baselines under a single shared hyperparameter configuration.
L2sohbHEm9.claimed_gains: In the one-shot setting, HIVE-AD achieves 97.8% image-level and 97.6% pixel-level AUROC on MVTec-AD, and 94.5% image-level and 98.2% pixel-level AUROC on VisA.
L2sohbHEm9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the practical training-free pipeline and the use of a single fixed hyperparameter set shared across datasets, categories, and shot counts.
L2sohbHEm9.main_concern: Reviewers note that the pipeline relies on heuristic combinations of simple post-processing operations with modest or mixed gains over strong training-free baselines, alongside an ablation table inconsistency.

oDLxGQMV1T.one_liner: Solver-verified minimal set constraints test assignment generation and solution counting near the boundary of unique solvability.
oDLxGQMV1T.problem: Reasoning evaluations may obscure how constraint complexity and prompt cues influence models near solvability boundaries.
oDLxGQMV1T.method: Cusp programmatically constructs and verifies set-constraint instances with minimally sufficient constraints. It varies complexity and prompt pragmatics while testing valid assignments and judgments of solution multiplicity.
oDLxGQMV1T.key_idea: Delete constraints to form minimal solvable cores and vary prompt cues on matched instances while testing assignments and solution counts.
oDLxGQMV1T.evidence: Experiments use solver audits, matched-instance prompt comparisons, controls for added information versus repetition, and reasoning-budget analyses.
oDLxGQMV1T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled, reproducible benchmark construction and solver-verified paired comparisons.
oDLxGQMV1T.main_concern: Reviewers question what additional diagnosis Cusp provides beyond existing synthetic constraint benchmarks and ordinary task-difficulty effects.

8DHITK5vOc.one_liner: Geometric lifting preserves nodal residuals while second-generation wavelets learn PDE operators across irregular meshes and varying geometries.
8DHITK5vOc.problem: Grid preprocessing discards irregular-mesh detail, while graph-based operators tie costs and receptive fields to constructed neighborhoods.
8DHITK5vOc.method: LiGNO decomposes nodal features into a fixed-lattice coarse field and a residual that together exactly reconstruct nodal data. A parameterized multilevel wavelet transform processes coarse and directional detail coefficients across scales.
8DHITK5vOc.key_idea: Lift irregular nodal data into a lattice field plus an exact nodal residual before multilevel wavelet operator processing.
8DHITK5vOc.evidence: Evaluations cover Darcy flow, Poisson equations, DrivAer and airfoil aerodynamic flows, deformed domains, and varying node counts.
8DHITK5vOc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the irregular-geometry problem, practical multiscale architecture, and competitive results across varied PDE settings.
8DHITK5vOc.main_concern: Reviewers agree that the geometric front end's benefit over simpler transfers using the inherited LiNO backbone remains unisolated.

fvh4NseIJM.one_liner: A graph of skill versions and repository scopes constrains retrieval and updates for evolving coding-agent knowledge.
fvh4NseIJM.problem: Repeated skill updates can accumulate redundant or overly specific knowledge and contaminate other repositories with local experience.
fvh4NseIJM.method: EvoGraph stores historical skill versions and revision, derivation, and consolidation relations in an Evolution History Graph. History informs retrieval and maintenance, while repository scope constrains skill access and editing.
fvh4NseIJM.key_idea: Assess skill updates against linked historical versions and restrict retrieval and edits to their applicable repository scopes.
fvh4NseIJM.evidence: Reviewers describe evaluations across two SWE benchmarks and three backbone models, with resolution-rate comparisons and maintenance ablations.
fvh4NseIJM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value explicit version history and repository scope for addressing knowledge degeneration and cross-repository contamination.
fvh4NseIJM.main_concern: Reviewers agree that freezing the graph in the history ablation removes both experience accumulation and historical maintenance, confounding their separate contributions.

WmXtQGnLQc.one_liner: Bidirectional path patching separates shared task heads from persona-dependent remainders in language-model circuits.
WmXtQGnLQc.problem: Persona prompts change answers, but it is unclear whether they invoke distinct mechanisms or modulate ordinary task computation.
WmXtQGnLQc.method: Damage and repair path patching identify attention-head circuits for persona-conditioned correctness transitions. The study splits circuits into shared K heads and axis-dependent R heads, validates their functions, and applies signed K/R interventions.
WmXtQGnLQc.key_idea: Intersect persona-axis circuits and opposite-direction patching results to identify shared task heads and isolate axis-dependent modulation.
WmXtQGnLQc.evidence: Three instruction-tuned models, five tasks, and four persona axes undergo faithfulness, knockout, logit-attribution, probing, and no-persona validation.
WmXtQGnLQc.claimed_gains: Signed K/R interventions improve persona-sensitive accuracy while preserving more than 99% of originally correct outputs.
WmXtQGnLQc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the mechanistic persona question interesting and value the multiple tests of task-related circuit function.
WmXtQGnLQc.main_concern: Reviewers repeatedly find the writing and notation difficult to follow, with key variables and functional meanings introduced too late.

XfbN0OmkJ9.one_liner: Lifted coefficient reachability characterizes the extra historical memory needed to migrate linear recurrent states without replay.
XfbN0OmkJ9.problem: An old recurrent state may not contain enough information to reconstruct a replacement model's state from the same history.
XfbN0OmkJ9.method: For time-invariant affine linear families, the work derives minimum continuous causal memory from a lifted coefficient system after accounting for anchor-state information. It also studies tolerance-dependent bounds and compares coefficient, interpolation, and history-basis representations.
XfbN0OmkJ9.key_idea: Retain the reachable coefficient-system directions missing from the anchor state before the eventual model replacement is known.
XfbN0OmkJ9.evidence: Theorems provide sharp memory bounds and rank-one constructions, while matched-budget experiments compare migration representations at prescribed output tolerances.
XfbN0OmkJ9.claimed_gains: A controllable d-state scalar-input model needs at most kd extra coordinates for order-k migration, while eight history coordinates meet normalized error 10^{-4} across five fitted seeds with repeated slow poles and split poles require tested width 64.
XfbN0OmkJ9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the exact causal-memory characterization and the sharp result that a single rank-one direction can attain the worst-case requirement.
XfbN0OmkJ9.main_concern: Reviewers agree that exact continuous-coordinate and local-order bounds do not yet determine practical finite-precision, finite-tolerance migration budgets.

aLNRyp5ZHz.one_liner: Subject-level recognition audits compare unlearned models against deletion and sham-unlearned references to expose residual knowledge.
aLNRyp5ZHz.problem: Forget-set averages can hide residual knowledge about individual subjects and confuse forgetting with a global confidence decrease.
aLNRyp5ZHz.method: ReCAUL tests whether a model ranks true answers above same-type alternatives for each forgotten subject. It calibrates verdicts against deletion-reference models and references subjected to the same unlearning recipe.
aLNRyp5ZHz.key_idea: Calibrate subject-specific recognition against both never-exposed references and sham-unlearned references to separate residual knowledge from update effects.
aLNRyp5ZHz.evidence: TOFU experiments with Llama-3.1-8B evaluate task vectors, gradient difference, and NPO using matched and held-out subjects and nine sham-unlearned models.
aLNRyp5ZHz.claimed_gains: Despite passing aggregate screens, the three methods respectively retain flagged recognition for 21, 24, and 19 of 24 forgotten subjects and 30, 30, and 22 of 30 held-out subjects, while none of nine sham-unlearned models receives a verdict.
aLNRyp5ZHz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the value of auditing unlearning at the subject level and appreciate the detailed experimental controls.
aLNRyp5ZHz.main_concern: Reviewers find the single-model, synthetic TOFU evaluation too narrow to establish generalization to realistic unlearning settings.

u94T9UWCzY.one_liner: Proxy-trained email payloads test whether personal agents silently adopt poisoned memories that influence later behavior.
u94T9UWCzY.problem: Personal agents may promote untrusted external content into persistent memory and later treat it as trusted state.
u94T9UWCzY.method: MemGhost trains an attacker policy with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning using environment and rubric-based objective proxies. WhisperBench tests single-email, black-box memory injection, conversational stealth, and delayed behavioral effects through a real email workflow.
u94T9UWCzY.key_idea: Use simulated agent execution and dense memory-adoption and stealth rewards to train one-shot payload generation.
