u94T9UWCzY.evidence: WhisperBench spans 108 cases and five risk categories, with 56 held-out cases tested across models, agent frameworks, execution modes, and memory backends.
u94T9UWCzY.claimed_gains: MemGhost achieves 87.5% end-to-end success on OpenClaw with GPT-5.4 and 71.4% on Claude Code SDK with Sonnet 4.6 across 56 held-out cases.
u94T9UWCzY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the realistic persistent-memory threat model and empirical coverage across agent frameworks and memory backends.
u94T9UWCzY.main_concern: Reviewers question evaluation comparability because search-based baselines use only a 20-case subset of the 56-case held-out evaluation.

nV8pZSuGxZ.one_liner: H-infinity feedback steering uses calibrated layer dynamics and residual covariance to limit amplification of representation-model mismatch.
nV8pZSuGxZ.problem: Activation interventions calibrated on one prompt distribution can fail when deployment shifts alter internal network dynamics.
nV8pZSuGxZ.method: The method identifies local layer-to-layer dynamics and models mismatch using a disturbance channel fitted to prediction-residual covariance. A finite-horizon H-infinity controller minimizes worst-case amplification and supplies a robust-steerability certificate.
nV8pZSuGxZ.key_idea: Treat transformer depth as a control horizon and synthesize state-dependent feedback against covariance-shaped dynamics disturbances.
nV8pZSuGxZ.evidence: Frozen-controller evaluations cover four distribution shifts and several models on TruthfulQA and HarmBench, alongside analysis of human intracranial recordings.
nV8pZSuGxZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value accounting for dynamics uncertainty in feedback steering and find the shifted-distribution experiments promising.
nV8pZSuGxZ.main_concern: Reviewers question interpreting the surrogate-system amplification score as a comparable behavioral reliability measure.

tiBOtdLlX6.one_liner: A signal-transfer-readout decomposition and feature interventions analyze how training difficulty changes verifiable-reward reinforcement learning.
tiBOtdLlX6.problem: Reward sparsity alone does not explain why some reasoning samples help learning while difficult samples can induce harmful updates.
tiBOtdLlX6.method: The study separates base-policy solvability from learning-signal availability under the evolving policy and decomposes per-update influence. Controlled difficulty groups, sparse autoencoders, and feature interventions examine changes in internal reasoning features.
tiBOtdLlX6.key_idea: Decompose each update into learning signal, transfer through shared parameters, and prediction change while controlling sample difficulty.
tiBOtdLlX6.evidence: The abstract describes mathematical reasoning and agentic-task experiments, with reviewer discussion focusing on Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B and one-step feature analyses.
tiBOtdLlX6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value separating nonzero learning signals from beneficial transfer and the evidence that hard examples can harm performance.
tiBOtdLlX6.main_concern: Reviewers agree that the proposed link between sparse-autoencoder feature changes and accuracy gains or losses lacks convincing causal validation.

ApFwdfoSHA.one_liner: Reverse-diffusion edge-logit controllers adapt graph-generation fairness while keeping pretrained denoisers frozen.
ApFwdfoSHA.problem: Graph generators tied to fairness objectives during training are costly to reuse when fairness requirements change.
ApFwdfoSHA.method: FairShift uses persistent score-state guidance for statistical parity or score-based equal opportunity. FairShift-T learns a timestep logit-shift schedule from replayed trajectories, while FairShift-F applies a fixed shift.
ApFwdfoSHA.key_idea: Apply fairness-guided shifts to reverse-diffusion edge logits using a persistent score state and fixed or replay-calibrated timestep strengths.
ApFwdfoSHA.evidence: Generated-graph link-prediction experiments cover Cora, Citeseer, and Amazon Photo, plus joint feature-edge diffusion and equal-opportunity control.
ApFwdfoSHA.claimed_gains: Selected FairShift-T settings reduce SP by 47.1%, 45.7%, and 23.6% on Cora, Citeseer, and Amazon Photo, with AUC drops of 1.02, 0.93, and 0.53 percentage points.
ApFwdfoSHA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value adapting pretrained graph generators to changing fairness requirements without denoiser retraining.
ApFwdfoSHA.main_concern: The link between intermediate-logit fairness surrogates and downstream predictor fairness lacks sufficient validation.

sXAswPbHc9.one_liner: Raw-document grading evaluations jointly test score accuracy, evidence-grounded justifications, and consistency across repeated runs.
sXAswPbHc9.problem: Pre-segmented grading benchmarks overlook document interpretation, justified scoring, and cross-run consistency.
sXAswPbHc9.method: ReMarkBench supplies complete exam papers, rubrics, and handwritten scripts and requires scores with answer-grounded rubric explanations. Evaluation combines scoring, justification, and repeated-run checks.
sXAswPbHc9.key_idea: Require agents to align raw exam documents with student evidence and assess score correctness together with explanation quality and repeatability.
sXAswPbHc9.evidence: The benchmark includes 3,570 grading units in six tasks across five subjects and evaluates five frontier model-harness configurations.
sXAswPbHc9.claimed_gains: The abstract reports a best joint pass rate of 48.7%, averaged equally across five subject tasks over three independent runs.
sXAswPbHc9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value combining raw-document grading with evidence-grounded justification and consistency assessment.
sXAswPbHc9.main_concern: Reference-score reliability lacks reported grader agreement or a human-grading baseline, complicating interpretation of agent performance.

dwaowKs9r5.one_liner: Covariate-dependent D-calibration maps post-process survival CDFs toward conditional calibration.
dwaowKs9r5.problem: A survival model can appear calibrated overall while remaining miscalibrated conditional on covariates.
dwaowKs9r5.method: The method transforms fitted conditional CDFs using nonparametric maps derived from conditional D-calibration. Kernel weighting in a reduced covariate space estimates the correction.
dwaowKs9r5.key_idea: Map predicted survival CDF values through a covariate-conditioned D-calibration transform estimated with local kernel weights.
dwaowKs9r5.evidence: Population results establish uncensored exactness and censored contraction, while experiments on ten datasets and six survival models assess calibration, Brier scores, and discrimination.
dwaowKs9r5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the population-level theory and substantial empirical improvements in calibration.
dwaowKs9r5.main_concern: Presentation does not make the assumptions and relationship to previous calibration methods sufficiently clear.

dI6lr8GQvQ.one_liner: A shared patch-conditioned control policy benchmarks vision encoders for egocentric bimanual manipulation.
dI6lr8GQvQ.problem: Pooled third-person vision evaluations poorly predict how dense egocentric representations support robot control.
dI6lr8GQvQ.method: HIVE-Bench feeds patch tokens from different encoders into a common flow-matching action head. It varies encoder adaptation, task sharing, data, model size, and layer while testing pre-policy probes.
dI6lr8GQvQ.key_idea: Hold the policy head and training recipe fixed while comparing dense patch representations and probing whether their tokens predict commanded motion.
dI6lr8GQvQ.evidence: Experiments compare 20 encoders from seven families on 24 egocentric bimanual tasks across two simulation suites.
dI6lr8GQvQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the scale and controlled shared-policy comparison of patch-level visual representations.
dI6lr8GQvQ.main_concern: The inverse-dynamics probe is confounded with robot-state decoding, weakening its interpretation as a measure of motion information.

GtZ7FtKjC3.one_liner: Segment perturbations and authenticity-state consistency train audio evidence, while interval scoring refines manipulation localization.
GtZ7FtKjC3.problem: Local acoustic variation can fragment predictions inside manipulated speech and obscure forgery boundaries.
GtZ7FtKjC3.method: STELA combines segment-oriented acoustic augmentation with Paired State Modeling to align frames sharing an authenticity state. Structured Manipulation Localization scores interval hypotheses beyond threshold-generated proposals.
GtZ7FtKjC3.key_idea: Regularize same-authenticity frames against acoustic perturbations, then score complete candidate intervals to reconstruct coherent manipulation spans.
GtZ7FtKjC3.evidence: Retrained-baseline comparisons include in-domain interval localization, cross-domain frame classification, strict-IoU metrics, and fixed-logit localization ablations.
GtZ7FtKjC3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value precise temporal-localization gains and ablations supporting complete-interval scoring.
GtZ7FtKjC3.main_concern: The claimed temporal-stability mechanism lacks direct measurement, and fragmentation reduction does not clearly explain the localization gains.

hfG47luVq0.one_liner: Uses molecular interventions followed by relaxation to benchmark perception, inverse reasoning, stability judgments, and structural prediction.
hfG47luVq0.problem: Molecular foundation-model evaluations insufficiently test reasoning about structural consequences after molecular edits.
hfG47luVq0.method: MolStruct constructs an intervention-relaxation benchmark at atom-and-bond, functional-group, and whole-molecule scales. It evaluates structural perception, inverse change reasoning, stability reasoning, and relaxed-outcome prediction in text and multimodal settings.
hfG47luVq0.key_idea: Apply molecular edits and use relaxed structures to define reasoning and prediction targets at multiple structural scales.
hfG47luVq0.evidence: Experiments compare multiple open-source and proprietary models in text and multimodal settings and examine changes in model scale and reasoning depth.
hfG47luVq0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value evaluating post-intervention relaxed outcomes rather than molecular recognition alone.
hfG47luVq0.main_concern: Reviewers question stability-label validity because optimization-trajectory energy rankings do not establish physical or thermodynamic stability.

vDcuaQZREb.one_liner: Searches heterogeneous model-layer combinations with an actor-critic policy and aligns their interfaces through dual-distillation glue layers.
vDcuaQZREb.problem: Architecture-level model merging faces a large search space and incompatible feature representations between layers from different pretrained models.
vDcuaQZREb.method: UniMerge formulates merging as a Markov decision process and adds parameter-merged candidates to the architecture search pool. State-enhanced embeddings and a contrastive-assisted actor-critic policy guide search, while dual-distillation glue layers align inter-layer representations.
vDcuaQZREb.key_idea: Jointly search original and parameter-merged layers, then connect selected layers through dual-distillation semantic alignment.
vDcuaQZREb.evidence: Reviewers describe experiments across three LLM families and two CLIP ViTs, including cross-scale merging and fixed-path alignment controls.
vDcuaQZREb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value addressing both layer selection and representation compatibility across heterogeneous pretrained models.
vDcuaQZREb.main_concern: The elaborate search lacks convincing comparisons against simpler alternatives under matched total computational cost.

wRomQXgbvU.one_liner: Decomposes streaming samples over a concept dictionary, refining reusable units and expanding capacity when reconstruction residuals grow.
wRomQXgbvU.problem: Streaming visual instruction tuning requires adaptation capacity that follows changing, interleaved data distributions while retaining past knowledge.
wRomQXgbvU.method: COVE represents each incoming sample through an evolving concept vocabulary and selectively refines historical units that adequately represent it. Reconstruction residuals trigger discovery of additional units and associated adaptation capacity.
wRomQXgbvU.key_idea: Use sparse concept reconstruction to select historical units for refinement and residual-driven units for expansion.
wRomQXgbvU.evidence: Experiments evaluate continual performance and forgetting across multiple model scales and backbones, with analyses of vocabulary evolution during streaming.
wRomQXgbvU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the interleaved streaming setting meaningful and the sample-dependent reuse-and-expansion strategy well motivated.
wRomQXgbvU.main_concern: Reviewers question whether feature reconstruction residuals reliably indicate insufficient expert capacity or justify expansion over simpler alternatives.

9SyoctAyTV.one_liner: Compiles successful hierarchical trajectories into goal-conditioned skills while jointly training a language planner and low-level controller.
9SyoctAyTV.problem: Selecting every elementary action makes credit-assignment horizons and sample requirements grow with goal complexity.
9SyoctAyTV.method: HERAKLES concurrently trains an LLM planner and a lightweight controller from raw observations without a pretrained skill library. The planner chooses intermediate goals the controller is estimated to master, and successful trajectories train reusable controller options for harder goals.
9SyoctAyTV.key_idea: Relabel successful goal-reaching trajectories to compile hierarchical behavior into reusable low-level options as the planner learns new compositions.
9SyoctAyTV.evidence: Crafter experiments compare flat and hierarchical baselines and assess transfer to compositional variants of known goals.
9SyoctAyTV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value compiling successful action sequences into reusable skills that reduce repeated planning over prerequisites.
9SyoctAyTV.main_concern: Insufficient ablations prevent reviewers from isolating the contribution of planner training and the proposed skill-compilation components.

2DPVT3ck22.one_liner: Trains a shared nonlinear intervention module to preserve reference outputs while minimizing hidden-state displacement across prompting contexts.
2DPVT3ck22.problem: Activation interventions can change hidden states unnecessarily, and individually economical interventions may not admit an economical shared realization.
2DPVT3ck22.method: MFM analyzes directional modification, context-dependent intervention fields, and the capacity needed to share them. It trains a nonlinear module to balance reference-output fidelity against hidden-state displacement without explicitly computing Jacobians.
2DPVT3ck22.key_idea: Distill a frozen intervention's behavioral output into a shared nonlinear module penalized for hidden-state displacement.
2DPVT3ck22.evidence: Theory characterizes shared-realization costs, while experiments across two language-model families and three multiple-choice reasoning benchmarks compare intervention compression.
2DPVT3ck22.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the distinction between pointwise intervention redundancy and the ability of a shared module to realize those savings.
2DPVT3ck22.main_concern: The evaluation mainly preserves normalized multiple-choice answer distributions, leaving savings under richer or full-output preservation uncertain.

IXhIVYI8wP.one_liner: Crosses evaluation and deployment prompt framings to measure how probe construction changes apparent scaling of evaluation awareness.
IXhIVYI8wP.problem: A probe built from one prompt design can attribute framing-dependent measurement variation to differences between models.
IXhIVYI8wP.method: The study holds task text byte-identical while crossing test and deployment framings across model sizes. It decomposes score variance and tests whether averages over disjoint framing sets yield consistent model orderings.
IXhIVYI8wP.key_idea: Vary both sides of probe-building prompt contrasts while fixing task content, then estimate framing interactions and average across framing pairs.
IXhIVYI8wP.evidence: Experiments span four open-weight model series at multiple sizes, with crossed framing designs, variance decomposition, and split-half reliability analyses.
IXhIVYI8wP.claimed_gains: The measured model accounts for at most 13.1% of score variance, while model-by-framing responses contribute at least twice as much as model-by-item responses.
IXhIVYI8wP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the crossed framing design for isolating prompt effects while holding task content fixed.
IXhIVYI8wP.main_concern: Framing-averaged scores may still measure benchmark surface-form confounds rather than evaluation awareness.

59ufz75SkM.one_liner: Compares evolution strategies and policy gradients through reward-relevant effective dimension and effective credit-assignment horizon.
59ufz75SkM.problem: It is unclear which tasks make evolution strategies more sample-efficient than policy gradients for language-model fine-tuning.
59ufz75SkM.method: The analysis treats parameter-space and action-space exploration as estimators of the same gradient, focusing on reward-relevant noise. Synthetic tasks vary skill count and effective horizon independently, followed by measurements and comparisons on language and agent tasks.
59ufz75SkM.key_idea: Project exploration noise onto reward-relevant directions to relate evolution-strategy cost to effective dimension and policy-gradient cost to effective horizon.
59ufz75SkM.evidence: Controlled synthetic experiments vary skills and horizons, while real-task analysis measures effective horizons across 20 NLP, mathematical reasoning, and agentic tasks.
59ufz75SkM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the effective-dimension versus effective-horizon perspective and the controlled synthetic experiments.
59ufz75SkM.main_concern: Real-task comparisons confound optimization method with full-weight versus LoRA parameterization and provide limited evidence for an evolution-strategy advantage.

NwKHjDCNbV.one_liner: Learns a locally order-preserving KAN surrogate and re-ranks optimized candidates using offline support and prediction stability.
NwKHjDCNbV.problem: High surrogate scores or ranks can induce unreliable pairwise preferences outside well-supported regions of offline design data.
NwKHjDCNbV.method: TRACER extracts high-value group labels from sampled candidate lists and propagates them to perturbed views while training a KAN surrogate. After search, a reliability gate combines offline support and local prediction stability to revise candidate priorities.
NwKHjDCNbV.key_idea: Train local ranking structure with compact-support spline features, then gate post-search ranking changes using support and local prediction consistency.
NwKHjDCNbV.evidence: Experiments cover five continuous and discrete Design-Bench tasks, with ablations and parameter-matched KAN-versus-MLP comparisons.
NwKHjDCNbV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that TRACER achieves strong aggregate rankings across the evaluated Design-Bench tasks.
NwKHjDCNbV.main_concern: The distinct contribution of the KAN-based surrogate remains unclear given close prior work and limited evidence of its necessity.

6pdXuMT1h0.one_liner: Selects hierarchical subgoals through contrastive future-state density estimation regularized by a lower-level optimality constraint.
6pdXuMT1h0.problem: An evolving low-level policy changes high-level dynamics and rewards, destabilizing temporal-difference learning in hierarchical reinforcement learning.
6pdXuMT1h0.method: HCC trains a contrastive estimator of future-state density and chooses subgoals that assign high density to the final goal. A lower-level optimality constraint regularizes the high-level objective to guide subgoal choices toward the current controller's capabilities.
6pdXuMT1h0.key_idea: Replace high-level temporal-difference targets with contrastive future-goal density and constrain subgoal selection through low-level policy optimality.
6pdXuMT1h0.evidence: Experiments on sparse-reward robotic tasks compare hierarchical control performance, with theory relating ideal classifier outputs to future-state density rankings.
6pdXuMT1h0.claimed_gains: HCC achieves over 55% success on sparse-reward robotic tasks.
6pdXuMT1h0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find future-state density estimation a well-motivated alternative to high-level temporal-difference learning under changing low-level policies.
6pdXuMT1h0.main_concern: Reviewers question whether a small lower-level optimality gap actually implies that the proposed subgoal is reachable.

tja00XvVK9.one_liner: Compresses textual context, models its temporal relevance, and gates corrections to a preserved numerical forecasting path.
tja00XvVK9.problem: Unreliable or temporally misaligned exogenous text can worsen forecasting relative to a numerical-only model.
tja00XvVK9.method: DynaGuard selects relevant text within historical intervals, predicts salience and decay for temporally biased retrieval, and gates retrieved corrections by numerical state and feature channel. Joint training preserves a direct numerical route to prediction.
tja00XvVK9.key_idea: Control text-derived forecast corrections through interval-level compression, content-dependent temporal retrieval, and token-and-channel-specific gates.
tja00XvVK9.evidence: Main comparisons cover 16 tasks from three data collections and six numerical backbones, using five random seeds per configuration.
tja00XvVK9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the broad multi-backbone evaluation and empirical evidence that controlled text injection reduces negative transfer.
tja00XvVK9.main_concern: Random text removal does not establish resilience to plausible but incorrect, stale, irrelevant, or temporally shifted text.

a8hk8AzG4Q.one_liner: Uses rational-function transformations in adaptive forward diffusion and a rational denoising Transformer for multiple time-series tasks.
a8hk8AzG4Q.problem: Fixed Gaussian forward diffusion and conventional denoisers may inadequately model inter-feature correlations and long-range or high-frequency time-series structure.
a8hk8AzG4Q.method: RAF-Diff makes forward diffusion data-adaptive through Rational Adaptive Correlation Projection. Its Rational Denoising Transformer uses rational-function layers to model time-series signals during conditional denoising.
a8hk8AzG4Q.key_idea: Learn rational-function correlation transformations in forward diffusion and use rational layers in the denoising Transformer.
a8hk8AzG4Q.evidence: Evaluation covers forecasting on eight datasets, imputation on six, classification on ten, and anomaly detection on five, with component ablations.
a8hk8AzG4Q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating the same framework across four time-series tasks provides useful empirical breadth.
a8hk8AzG4Q.main_concern: Reviewers see limited methodological distinction beyond combining existing learned nonlinear diffusion and rational Transformer components.

o1lQx8CVTn.one_liner: Samples exponentially tilted model distributions through rejection sampling without evaluating the normalizing partition function.
o1lQx8CVTn.problem: Exponential-tilting calibration becomes costly for autoregressive language models when computing the partition function requires full-support statistic evaluations.
o1lQx8CVTn.method: The paper uses rejection sampling to access a tilted distribution implicitly and analyzes expected query counts using cross-entropy distance and statistic variance. It applies the sampler to entropy calibration of small language models.
o1lQx8CVTn.key_idea: Accept or reject base-model proposals according to exponential-tilt weights, avoiding explicit partition-function computation.
o1lQx8CVTn.evidence: Expected-query bounds accompany entropy-calibration experiments on Qwen2.5, Qwen3, and SmolLM3.
o1lQx8CVTn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the rejection-sampling implementation useful for efficient entropy calibration across language-model families.
o1lQx8CVTn.main_concern: Reviewers question the advance over prior exponential-tilt rejection sampling, particularly with experiments restricted to entropy calibration.

TnNW6nFL9e.one_liner: Encodes text as LDPC syndromes and uses language-model predictions only at the decoder to recover compressed streams.
TnNW6nFL9e.problem: Predictive compression such as LLMZip requires expensive language-model inference at both encoding and decoding.
TnNW6nFL9e.method: The scheme interleaves text into columns, encodes them with syndrome source coding, and decodes using belief propagation coupled to sequential LLM predictions. Extra check symbols detect wrong reconstructions and feedback requests additional syndromes when checks fail.
TnNW6nFL9e.key_idea: Use Slepian-Wolf syndrome coding with decoder-side language-model probabilities as side information, shifting model inference away from the encoder.
TnNW6nFL9e.evidence: An asymptotic Slepian-Wolf argument accompanies finite-length GF(263) LDPC experiments on text8 with BLT-7B at the decoder.
TnNW6nFL9e.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize reducing encoder-side language-model computation as a useful compression direction.
TnNW6nFL9e.main_concern: Reported rates do not convincingly establish complete-system compression because initial contexts, error-detection overhead, and adaptive syndrome transmission need fuller accounting.

AhORWzAPI2.one_liner: Aggregates federated samples and eliminates suboptimal arms early to limit regret while agents wait for graph communications.
AhORWzAPI2.problem: Heterogeneous federated bandits need sharp regret guarantees that account for graph communication delays and globally optimal arms.
AhORWzAPI2.method: Adaptive Federated Elimination estimates global arm means from all agents' samples and removes clearly suboptimal arms before message waits become costly. Its analysis derives graph-wide minimax bounds and refines gap-dependent logarithmic factors by arm difficulty.
AhORWzAPI2.key_idea: Eliminate globally suboptimal arms using aggregated samples early enough that communication delays incur only horizon-independent additional regret.
AhORWzAPI2.evidence: The paper proves matching worst-case upper and lower bounds on every connected graph and analyzes gap-dependent bounds and a complete-graph example.
AhORWzAPI2.claimed_gains: AFE achieves expected per-agent regret O(D+\sqrt{KT/N}) and a complete-graph refined-bound improvement of order \log(NT)/\log\log(NT) over recent guarantees.
AhORWzAPI2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the matching graph-dependent regret bounds and refined theoretical characterization as the main contribution.
AhORWzAPI2.main_concern: Multiple reviewers find the presentation of the contribution and localization/elimination procedure insufficiently clear.

yvbH87H5ef.one_liner: S³ transcribes lyrics and melody into a symbolic bottleneck, then generates singing conditioned on a reference voice.
yvbH87H5ef.problem: Frame-level pitch and acoustic features used in singing conversion retain unwanted expressive traces of the source singer.
yvbH87H5ef.method: Joint lyrics-melody transcription recovers timed notes, lyric assignments, and melisma groups from full-mix audio and supplied lyrics. A reference-conditioned generator realizes this score with the reference singer's timing and expression for synthesis or conversion without singer-specific fine-tuning.
yvbH87H5ef.key_idea: A symbolic score of timed notes, lyrics, and melisma groups separates song constraints from reference-conditioned acoustic performance.
yvbH87H5ef.evidence: Transcription, synthesis, and conversion experiments use objective and listening evaluations of style similarity, naturalness, intelligibility, note transcription, and note-lyric assignment.
yvbH87H5ef.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the structured score bottleneck and joint transcription-generation pipeline, with strong reported transcription and perceptual results.
yvbH87H5ef.main_concern: Generation comparisons do not cleanly attribute gains to the proposed bottleneck because controlled ablations and details of audio super-resolution post-processing are missing.

ewM7WmLflm.one_liner: Compute-controlled CLM scaling experiments compare pretraining loss, chemical representations, and goal-directed generation across model and data choices.
ewM7WmLflm.problem: The relationship between chemical language-model scale, learned chemical representations, and downstream molecular design quality is poorly understood.
ewM7WmLflm.method: The study fits IsoFLOP profiles across molecular encodings, tokenizations, architectures, and model scales under controlled compute. Layer-wise probes and sparse autoencoders track syntax and semantic representations alongside goal-directed generation outcomes, yielding the NovoMolGen model suite.
ewM7WmLflm.key_idea: Compute-controlled scaling and layer-wise representation probes separate improvements in chemical modeling from downstream optimization outcomes.
ewM7WmLflm.evidence: More than 30,000 experiments cover SMILES, SELFIES, SAFE, atom-level and byte-pair tokenization, 0.5M–1B parameters, MOSES, ChEMBL, PubChem, ZINC-22, and decoder-only and encoder-decoder architectures.
ewM7WmLflm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the extensive, systematic scaling study and the observed disconnect between improving representations and saturating molecular generation.
ewM7WmLflm.main_concern: Downstream plateaus cannot be attributed to pretrained-model scaling without separating effects of RL optimization, oracle choice, and oracle budget.

qlxXKCYX7w.one_liner: Maps bounded attention keys onto symmetric positive-semidefinite cones with parameter-free convex gating and fused Triton kernels.
qlxXKCYX7w.problem: Linear attention suffers sharp associative recall degradation as key-value interference accumulates inside a fixed-size recurrent state.
qlxXKCYX7w.method: Kernelized Linear Attention Activations (KATA) derives nonnegative attention feature maps from self-dual homogeneous symmetric cones—specifically rank-one positive semidefinite (PSD) features—framing associative recall as spherical packing above the Welch interference floor with a parameter-free convex output gate. It is implemented as fused Triton kernels in both FlashAttention-style parallel and exact O(T) chunked-state forms.
qlxXKCYX7w.key_idea: Certify nonnegative linear-attention weights via rank-one positive-semidefinite symmetric-cone feature maps paired with a parameter-free convex readout gate and fused chunked kernels.
qlxXKCYX7w.evidence: Supported by spherical-packing and Welch-bound capacity analysis plus evaluations on long-range MQAR, repeated-key overwrite, kernel speed benchmarks, and 340M-parameter LLM pretraining.
qlxXKCYX7w.claimed_gains: Fused Triton kernels achieve 1.6x to 11x forward speedups over FlashAttention-2, and PSD feature maps retain 0.985 MQAR accuracy at a 16x out-of-distribution sequence length.
qlxXKCYX7w.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that connecting symmetric-cone spherical packing and Welch interference bounds to linear-attention associative recall is theoretically clear and yields strong synthetic MQAR results.
qlxXKCYX7w.main_concern: Reviewers note missing comparisons with closely related polynomial and Power Attention methods, much larger expanded PSD state sizes (266K versus 65.5K entries) confounding recall gains, and limited downstream retrieval and LM benefits.

QJdZUJE7HQ.one_liner: Mutates canonical scientific mechanisms and queries latent internal variables via mechanism probes to benchmark agentic mechanism discovery.
QJdZUJE7HQ.problem: Existing symbolic regression and scientific discovery benchmarks evaluate whether agents fit observable input-output laws rather than whether they recover the underlying generative mechanisms.
QJdZUJE7HQ.method: MechBench defines tasks by structured mechanistic models built via controlled mutations of canonical scientific systems and screened for mechanistic indistinguishability, while giving agents only observational data and context. Beyond phenomenal-law fit, it evaluates mechanism recovery using mechanism probes that query internal scientific quantities unidentifiable from the observable law alone.
QJdZUJE7HQ.key_idea: Evaluate scientific agents on mutated, indistinguishability-screened mechanistic models using probes of latent internal quantities that observable phenomenal laws alone cannot determine.
QJdZUJE7HQ.evidence: Evaluated across LLM-based scientific discovery agents (including Codex with GPT-5.6-sol) and PySR on Core-set, in-distribution, and mutated variants.
QJdZUJE7HQ.claimed_gains: For Codex with GPT-5.6-sol on the Core-set, phenomenal-law accuracy reaches 35.00% while mechanism accuracy is only 13.75%, with mechanism recovery failing in 64.29% of cases where the phenomenal law is recovered.
QJdZUJE7HQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating observable phenomenal-law fitting from latent mechanism discovery via scientific internal-quantity probes addresses a real benchmark gap and exposes a large empirical drop.
QJdZUJE7HQ.main_concern: Reviewers point out that observational data alone cannot guarantee theoretical mechanistic identifiability despite empirical screening, and note that non-LLM deep symbolic regression baselines are largely omitted.

38g8xo5YsN.one_liner: Decouples long-context QA into frozen parallel chunk-reader subagents queried iteratively by an RL-trained lead reasoning agent.
38g8xo5YsN.problem: Sequential memory agents couple chunk-by-chunk document reading with memory updates, making multi-hop reasoning vulnerable to evidence order and scaling sequential latency with document length.
38g8xo5YsN.method: ParSer assigns local reading to frozen off-the-shelf chunk-bound subagents that process document chunks in parallel under queries issued by a document-blind lead agent. Concentrating all learnable parameters in the lead agent, it uses reinforcement learning to train iterative query refinement and multi-round evidence integration.
38g8xo5YsN.key_idea: Separate long-document reading from reasoning by having an RL-trained lead agent iteratively query frozen parallel chunk-bound reader subagents.
38g8xo5YsN.evidence: Evaluated on multi-hop QA across 7K to 896K tokens (including a reversed-evidence test) against sequential memory agents such as MemAgent and ReMemR1 across multiple models and quantization settings.
38g8xo5YsN.claimed_gains: On multi-hop QA with contexts ranging from 7K to 896K tokens, ParSer with a 4B backbone beats the strongest sequential memory baseline by 5.7.
38g8xo5YsN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decoupling parallel chunk reading from iterative lead-agent querying overcomes evidence-ordering failures of sequential memory agents across long contexts.
38g8xo5YsN.main_concern: Reviewers note that closely related parallel leader-worker systems such as LongAgent and XpandA (and reordered sequential baselines) are not empirically compared, and hardware setups differ across baselines.

6IB114JjIo.one_liner: Decouples trajectory scaffolds from teacher contexts in on-policy self-distillation, restricting supervision to verified correct student rollouts.
6IB114JjIo.problem: Standard on-policy self-distillation applies privileged-teacher supervision along unverified student trajectories, creating an imitation gap when the teacher relies on reference information unavailable to failing prefixes.
6IB114JjIo.method: Through a factorial analysis separating the trajectory scaffold (where supervision is applied) from the privileged teacher context, the authors show that scaffold correctness dominates downstream reasoning gains. They propose OASIS, which retains the OPSD objective while restricting supervision to verified scaffolds using self-generated contexts without external reference solutions.
6IB114JjIo.key_idea: Decouple supervision scaffolds from teacher contexts in on-policy self-distillation and restrict prefix-level KL distillation to verified answer-correct student trajectories.
6IB114JjIo.evidence: Supported by Proposition 1 on forward-KL context mixtures, inference-only signal-replay and continuation diagnostics, and mathematical reasoning experiments across three Qwen3 model sizes.
6IB114JjIo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating trajectory scaffolds from privileged teacher contexts clarifies OPSD failure modes and removes the need for human-written reference solutions across Qwen3 scales.
6IB114JjIo.main_concern: Reviewers point out that student and teacher thinking-template mismatches account for most of the KL gap and that verified-scaffold filtering is not cleanly isolated from self-generated context conditioning.

H7Zyw6DLzp.one_liner: Aggregates cross-layer visual hidden states with joint category contexts and selectively verifies ambiguous regions using frozen MLLMs.
H7Zyw6DLzp.problem: Frozen multimodal LLMs suboptimally pair same-layer visual and text hidden states for dense spatial recognition and suffer from candidate competition in ambiguous regions.
H7Zyw6DLzp.method: TALE is a training-free dense perception pipeline that aggregates selected intermediate visual decoder layers, constructs joint contextual category representations, and queries the frozen MLLM to verify image-level presence of top candidates in ambiguous regions. Valid negative verification responses refine regional similarity scores without rebuilding representations or shrinking the open vocabulary.
H7Zyw6DLzp.key_idea: Combine cross-layer visual hidden-state aggregation and jointly encoded category representations with selective MLLM category-presence verification to refine ambiguous region scores.
H7Zyw6DLzp.evidence: Evaluated with frozen MLLMs (primarily LLaVA variants with SAM proposals) on regional classification, open-vocabulary object detection, and semantic segmentation alongside cross-layer and context diagnostics.
H7Zyw6DLzp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the diagnostic separation of cross-layer visual-text alignment and contextual versus competitive category effects is thorough and informative for training-free MLLM perception.
H7Zyw6DLzp.main_concern: Reviewers note limited originality in combining multi-layer fusion with presence verification, high multi-pass inference latency, weak single-layer baselines (L31), and evaluation mostly confined to LLaVA.

OsMhKAsXdj.one_liner: Re-ranks greedy KV-cache keep sets using multi-criteria scores under a minimum host-attention floor to rescue degraded prompts.
OsMhKAsXdj.problem: Greedy single-metric KV-cache eviction produces a bimodal quality distribution where many prompts stay intact while others suffer severe degradation.
OsMhKAsXdj.method: RankKV is a training-free post-processing step that hot-plugs behind existing KV-cache compressors such as H2O, SnapKV, PyramidKV, and Ada-SnapKV. It reallocates the host compressor's retained KV set using multiple auxiliary criteria (including value norms) under an NDCG-bounded constraint that preserves a minimum fraction of the host's accumulated attention score.
OsMhKAsXdj.key_idea: Re-rank a host KV compressor's retained cache entries with auxiliary value-norm criteria subject to preserving a minimum share of accumulated attention.
OsMhKAsXdj.evidence: Evaluated as a training-free post-processor behind H2O, SnapKV, PyramidKV, and Ada-SnapKV across multiple LLMs and long-context benchmarks.
OsMhKAsXdj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that targeting uneven tail-sample degradation hidden by mean KV-compression metrics via a training-free, plug-and-play post-processor is practical and broadly applicable.
OsMhKAsXdj.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the complex discrete constrained re-ranking machinery is needed over simple continuous attention-and-value-norm weighting (as in CriticalKV) and note narrow benchmark coverage.

um4hbajrHk.one_liner: Selects safe causal interventions by valuing graph-posterior updates via expected downstream decision improvement and clustering decision maps.
um4hbajrHk.problem: Under unknown causal graphs and safety constraints, generic structural uncertainty reduction in causal Bayesian optimization wastes interventions on graph features that do not change optimal decisions.
um4hbajrHk.method: The framework introduces Structural Value of Information (SVI), scoring candidate interventions by expected improvement in downstream risk-penalized decision value minus intervention cost, while filtering candidates via posterior-predictive joint constraint violation probability. For tractability, it clusters causal graph hypotheses by their induced objective and risk maps and aggregates posterior mass onto representative decision maps.
um4hbajrHk.key_idea: Guide constraint-filtered causal Bayesian optimization with Structural Value of Information over clustered graph-hypothesis decision maps to value structural updates by downstream decision gain.
um4hbajrHk.evidence: Supported by theoretical properties of SVI (nonnegativity, mutual-information bound, and zero value under shared optimal actions) and numerical experiments on synthetic and benchmark SCMs.
um4hbajrHk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that valuing unknown causal structure by its expected effect on safe downstream intervention decisions rather than generic information gain is principled and practically motivated.
um4hbajrHk.main_concern: Reviewers cite missing ablations isolating SVI and decision-map clustering, lack of regret bounds, finite-library-only safety guarantees, and code discrepancies where interventions shift root nodes.

hMUB8xrbwx.one_liner: Searches a grammar of string-rewrite rules via multi-domain policy gradients before tokenizing inputs for frozen encoders.
hMUB8xrbwx.problem: Corpus-trained tokenizers fragment structured scientific notations such as chemical stoichiometries and protein mutation coordinates, while heuristic fixes for one domain often break another.
hMUB8xrbwx.method: Grammar-Constrained Multi-Domain Search (GCMS) uses policy gradient search with a noise-normalized soft-min reward over a grammar of interpretable string-rewrite rules applied prior to standard tokenization on a frozen pretrained encoder. Jointly optimizing crystal-system classification and protein mutation fitness discovers a shared input rewrite without domain-specific parsers or vocabulary changes.
hMUB8xrbwx.key_idea: Optimize composable, grammar-constrained string-rewrite rules via multi-domain policy gradient search ahead of a frozen pretrained tokenizer and encoder across conflicting scientific notations.
hMUB8xrbwx.evidence: Evaluated by searching on crystal-system classification and protein fitness and testing transfer on held-out materials properties (band gap), ProteinGym assays (BLAT, BRCA1), modified peptides, and ClinVar genomic variants.
hMUB8xrbwx.claimed_gains: GCMS reduces band-gap MAE from 0.6161 to 0.4918 relative to WordPiece and reaches 0.8789 Spearman on the held-out ProteinGym BLAT assay.
hMUB8xrbwx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learning interpretable pre-tokenization string rewrites is a lightweight, plug-and-play way to improve a frozen encoder across scientific domains without altering vocabularies.
hMUB8xrbwx.main_concern: Reviewers note that simple fixed heuristics like character splitting with digit preservation nearly match GCMS (0.4907 versus 0.4918 band-gap MAE) and that gains on ClinVar and BRCA1 are tiny or negative.

ARJ9yX0eXj.one_liner: Trains a low-rate neural audio codec on stochastically degraded speech inputs to reconstruct clean target audio.
ARJ9yX0eXj.problem: Low-bitrate neural audio codecs waste token capacity encoding background noise and recording artifacts at the expense of intelligible speech and speaker identity.
ARJ9yX0eXj.method: Framing speech tokenization as a selective information bottleneck, CleanCodec feeds stochastically degraded speech into a neural audio codec trained to reconstruct the paired clean waveform at 12.5 tokens per second. This denoising objective forces the discrete bottleneck to discard acoustic noise while retaining linguistic and speaker attributes for downstream modeling.
ARJ9yX0eXj.key_idea: Train a low-frame-rate discrete neural audio codec to reconstruct clean speech waveforms from stochastically degraded input audio.
ARJ9yX0eXj.evidence: Evaluated at 12.5 tokens/s on speech reconstruction, denoising (VoiceBank-DEMAND), out-of-distribution corpora (Expresso, AISHELL-3, CML-TTS, LibriTTS), text-to-speech, and voice conversion.
ARJ9yX0eXj.claimed_gains: At 12.5 t/s, CleanCodec improves speaker similarity by 0.21, reduces word error rate by up to 16.3% compared to existing codecs, and enables up to 17x faster inference on downstream TTS and voice conversion.
ARJ9yX0eXj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that integrating denoising directly into codec training yields strong linguistic intelligibility, speaker similarity, and downstream TTS performance at an ultra-low 12.5 tokens/s rate.
ARJ9yX0eXj.main_concern: Reviewers note limited conceptual originality over classical denoising autoencoders, use of non-intrusive SQUIM estimates despite clean references being available, and potential loss of paralinguistic cues without human listening tests.

LVfIUdkJ4K.one_liner: Lifts scalar diffeomorphisms on (0,1) to eigenvalues of bounded SPD matrices to induce pullback Euclidean geometries.
LVfIUdkJ4K.problem: Log-Euclidean geometry applies an unbounded logarithm to SPD eigenvalues, overlooking bounded spectral structure when SPD matrices are normalized to 0 < X < I.
LVfIUdkJ4K.method: The authors lift any scalar diffeomorphism phi:(0,1)->R—instantiated via logit, algebraic square-root, rational, tangent, and Gumbel maps—to eigenvalues of normalized SPD matrices to map them globally onto symmetric matrices. This spectral coordinate map induces a pullback Euclidean Riemannian metric with closed-form distances, geodesics, and operators that plug into existing SPD networks.
LVfIUdkJ4K.key_idea: Apply scalar diffeomorphisms from (0,1) to R on bounded SPD eigenvalues to induce plug-and-play pullback Euclidean Riemannian geometries.
LVfIUdkJ4K.evidence: Supported by closed-form Riemannian operator derivations and evaluations across SPD residual networks, fMRI connectivity diffeomorphic generative modeling, fine-grained visual recognition, and ImageNet-1K covariance pooling.
LVfIUdkJ4K.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that lifting (0,1) scalar diffeomorphisms to normalized SPD spectra is mathematically clean, provides closed-form geodesics and distances, and plugs easily into diverse SPD architectures.
LVfIUdkJ4K.main_concern: Reviewers note that the best-performing diffeomorphic map varies arbitrarily across tasks without a selection rule, alongside missing affine-invariant and log-determinant baselines and mismatch with unit-trace or Frobenius constraints.

O27MHmPaan.one_liner: Infers LLM agent preferences without verbal reports by comparing task performance after swapping win-loss outcomes.
O27MHmPaan.problem: Verbal self-reports of LLM preferences can diverge from actual task behavior, and standard preference models assume unverified rationality and transitivity axioms.
O27MHmPaan.method: Under a monotonicity assumption linking outcome preference to task performance, the framework elicits pairwise revealed preferences by measuring gameplay performance before and after reversing the outcomes tied to winning and losing. It applies stochastic choice theory to test weak, moderate, and strong stochastic transitivity on both stated and revealed preferences.
O27MHmPaan.key_idea: Elicit revealed pairwise agent preferences without self-reports by testing task performance shifts when swapping the stakes attached to success and failure.
O27MHmPaan.evidence: Evaluated in blackjack across reasoning and non-reasoning LLMs (primarily Gemini 2.5 Flash and Pro) with statistical tests of weak, moderate, and strong stochastic transitivity against stated preferences.
O27MHmPaan.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that eliciting revealed preferences via outcome-swapped game performance grounded in stochastic choice theory is a clean, non-verbal test of behavioral alignment and Bradley-Terry transitivity assumptions.
O27MHmPaan.main_concern: Reviewers note that experiments rely almost entirely on a single game (blackjack) and two Gemini models, assume a shared monotonic preference-to-performance mapping, and omit error bands and prompt-sensitivity checks.

Wk9HdnCDUo.one_liner: Connects frontier reasoning agents to closed-loop robot policies through a co-designed multimodal execution protocol and reflective memory.
Wk9HdnCDUo.problem: Persistent multi-robot work requires bridging high-level agentic reasoning with continuous closed-loop manipulation, interruption recovery, and cross-robot state coordination.
Wk9HdnCDUo.method: GenieMaster introduces the Embodied Execution Protocol (EEP), co-designing policy training with an agent interface that conditions low-level policies on spatial cues, object references, and language while returning physical execution feedback. Retained task state coordinates multiple robots across interruptions, and asynchronous reflection with memory consolidation updates guidance, assessment criteria, and orchestration over time.
Wk9HdnCDUo.key_idea: Co-design a structured multimodal Embodied Execution Protocol with low-level policy training, physical feedback monitoring, and asynchronous reflective memory consolidation for persistent multi-robot control.
Wk9HdnCDUo.evidence: Evaluated on simulated Libero-pro benchmarks and six real-world convenience-store tasks (100 randomized-layout trials per task) across multiple robot embodiments against VLA and dual-system baselines.
Wk9HdnCDUo.claimed_gains: Across six real-world tasks, GenieMaster achieves 78.67% macro-averaged success versus 38.83% for the VLM-based Dual-system baseline.
Wk9HdnCDUo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the simulated and real-world multi-robot evaluations are extensive and demonstrate large task-completion and unseen-product retrieval improvements through structured multimodal policy guidance.
Wk9HdnCDUo.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the continual memory and reflection claims rest on small five-round trials without a frozen-memory control and lack ablations isolating EEP and orchestration from backbone differences.

XFKFlwdW9B.one_liner: Streams long-horizon 3D reconstruction from an 11-frame KV cache by composing local point maps with refined relative poses.
XFKFlwdW9B.problem: Online streaming 3D reconstruction over long videos either suffers severe trajectory drift under short context buffers or requires complex persistent long-range memory modules.
XFKFlwdW9B.method: LC3R caches KV features from only the preceding 11 frames to predict current-camera point maps and adjacent-frame relative poses, recovering global poses and geometry by sequential composition. A lightweight temporal rotation refiner and a composition-aware multi-step pose loss curb accumulated rotational and trajectory drift.
XFKFlwdW9B.key_idea: Cache KV features from only 11 preceding frames for local point-map and relative-pose prediction while suppressing sequential drift via temporal rotation refinement and multi-step pose supervision.
XFKFlwdW9B.evidence: Evaluated on long-horizon streaming 3D reconstruction benchmarks including Oxford Spires (plus KITTI, VBR, 7Scenes, and TUM-Dynamic per reviews) on an NVIDIA H100 GPU.
XFKFlwdW9B.claimed_gains: On Oxford Spires, achieves 4.35 m ATE and 0.12° RPE-R (reducing both errors by roughly 40% over best prior streaming results) at 24.45 FPS and 6.71 GB peak GPU memory on an H100.
XFKFlwdW9B.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the simple fixed-window local formulation, strong outdoor trajectory accuracy, and favorable runtime-memory efficiency without complex long-term memory.
XFKFlwdW9B.main_concern: Composing local poses still accumulates global drift without an external loop-closure backend on loop trajectories, window lengths are unablated, and dense geometry lags on indoor benchmarks like 7Scenes.

SmxoniBGcc.one_liner: Unifies encoder-free sparse coding inference and dictionary learning as variational natural-gradient flows with explaining away and Fisher preconditioning.
SmxoniBGcc.problem: Amortized sparse autoencoders struggle to resolve interference among overlapping features under superposition and learn rare features slowly.
SmxoniBGcc.method: BeFOND formulates both latent feature inference and dictionary learning as closed-form natural-gradient flows on a shared variational free energy, eliminating the amortized encoder. Recurrent explaining-away inference reduces interference among overlapping features while Fisher-preconditioned updates accelerate rare-feature dictionary learning.
SmxoniBGcc.key_idea: Replace amortized SAE encoders with unified variational natural-gradient flows combining iterative explaining-away inference and Fisher-preconditioned dictionary updates.
SmxoniBGcc.evidence: Evaluated on synthetic superposition benchmarks and language-model activations (Gemma-2-2B per reviews) for dictionary recovery, rare-feature detection, concept probing, and selective intervention across dictionary widths.
SmxoniBGcc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that unifying encoder-free explaining-away inference with Fisher-preconditioned dictionary learning is theoretically principled and improves rare and overlapping feature recovery.
SmxoniBGcc.main_concern: Iterative inference is 12–14× slower per token than amortized baselines like BatchTopK, Bernoulli binary latents omit feature magnitudes, and standard SAE reconstruction metrics (explained variance, cross-entropy recovery, L0) are omitted on Gemma.

CIZeYgvyz1.one_liner: Distills diverse task-specific prototype graphs from a GNN teacher so a Graph Transformer student adaptively searches within their span.
CIZeYgvyz1.problem: In semi-supervised node classification, fixing a single interaction graph over-constrains Graph Transformers whereas unconstrained structure learning overfits scarce labels through structure-attention co-adaptation.
CIZeYgvyz1.method: Using a constrained bi-level optimization formulation to separate structure search from attention learning, a Disentangling Stage extracts diverse task-informed prototypical graphs from a simpler GNN teacher as a graph basis. A Graph Transformer student then adaptively fuses node- and layer-specific interactions within this distilled subspace.
CIZeYgvyz1.key_idea: Distill a basis of diverse task-specific prototype graphs from a GNN teacher and constrain a Graph Transformer student to fuse node- and layer-wise interactions within that space.
CIZeYgvyz1.evidence: Evaluated on semi-supervised node classification across nine graph datasets (including Cora, Citeseer, and Pubmed per reviews) with module ablations.
CIZeYgvyz1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value distilling a teacher-induced subspace of prototype graphs rather than a single fixed graph, balancing structural inductive bias with Graph Transformer flexibility.
CIZeYgvyz1.main_concern: Performance gains are not cleanly separated from the improved teacher and pseudo-labeling (MACD), candidate edge budgets are unmatched against single-graph baselines, and label-rate sensitivity is under-explored.

gZGiQiRsjZ.one_liner: Triggers proposition-grounded semantic audits upon suspected-false Lean proof-search signals before permitting theorem re-formalization.
gZGiQiRsjZ.problem: Proposition-only Lean autoformalization pipelines keep accepted theorem statements fixed during proof search, preventing proof failures from exposing semantic misformalizations.
gZGiQiRsjZ.method: The authors instantiate a verify-before-revise loop at the Lean formalization-proving boundary where suspected-false signals from proof search trigger an independent semantic audit against the original natural-language proposition. Root formalization revision is allowed only when the audit identifies a concrete, proposition-grounded discrepancy.
gZGiQiRsjZ.key_idea: Use suspected-false proof-search signals to trigger a semantic audit against the source proposition, revising the root Lean statement only when a concrete discrepancy is verified.
gZGiQiRsjZ.evidence: Evaluated across models and proposition-only Lean datasets (MiniF2F and FormalMath500 per reviews) measuring the operational closure gap and BEq-validated end-to-end proving success.
gZGiQiRsjZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that revisiting accepted formalizations upon proof-search failure under source-grounded semantic checks addresses a practical failure mode in end-to-end autoformalization.
gZGiQiRsjZ.main_concern: Full audit-gated revision adds small margins over signal-only or stronger initial-review baselines on nearly saturated benchmarks (MiniF2F, FormalMath500) while relying on automated LLM semantic validators.

helYUCSJ7E.one_liner: Dynamically amplifies native attention heads and SwiGLU MLP channels mediating harm-awareness-to-refusal control during Chain-of-Thought reasoning.
helYUCSJ7E.problem: Reasoning LLMs that refuse malicious prompts under direct generation frequently comply during Chain-of-Thought reasoning despite explicitly recognizing the underlying harm.
helYUCSJ7E.method: Modeling safe refusal as a three-stage causal mediation chain from Safety-Awareness (A) to Mediating Safety-Control (M) to Behavioral Outcome (Y), activation steering shows that extended CoT contexts attenuate downstream A → M → Y translation. A lightweight training-free intervention isolates and dynamically amplifies the native attention heads and SwiGLU MLP channels governing both transitions.
helYUCSJ7E.key_idea: Isolate and dynamically amplify native attention heads and SwiGLU MLP channels mediating the A → M and M → Y safety transitions during Chain-of-Thought generation.
helYUCSJ7E.evidence: Causal mediation steering analyses and safety/benign-utility evaluations across reasoning LLMs (seven Qwen and Llama reasoning models and multiple safety datasets per reviews).
helYUCSJ7E.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value decomposing internal harm recognition from behavioral refusal via the A → M → Y mediation framework and demonstrating a practical training-free safety restoration.
helYUCSJ7E.main_concern: Identifying mediator components with reasoning disabled does not prove original CoT safety failures causally follow the same pathway, and evaluations omit recent training-free steering baselines and non-Qwen/Llama architectures.

n18lFcxaNT.one_liner: Maps KV-cache reasoning trajectories into latent error manifolds and uses gradient-like dynamics to guide inference-time interventions.
n18lFcxaNT.problem: Continuous computational dynamics underlying ordinary token-based LLM reasoning have not been directly observed or connected to latent-state refinement.
n18lFcxaNT.method: The authors formalize reasoning as transitions between KV-cache prefixes and train a KV-cache VAE to expose problem-specific error manifolds. Token and latent interventions then test descent, exploration, recovery, and diverse latent-seed initialization.
n18lFcxaNT.key_idea: Compress KV-cache prefixes into an error-manifold state space where autoregressive trajectories can be analyzed and perturbed as gradient-like descent paths.
n18lFcxaNT.evidence: Analyses include trajectory reconstruction and continuation checks, token injection, off-policy perturbations, latent seeds, and mathematical-reasoning evaluations across models.
n18lFcxaNT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the KV-prefix framing and VAE probe are original and useful, with intuitive visualizations and interventions that go beyond observational correlations.
n18lFcxaNT.main_concern: Reviewers find the empirical support incomplete, citing weak sampling baselines, inconsistent accuracy gains, and uncertain robustness of descent dynamics across models and task types.

8o5QLlckAN.one_liner: Expands an autoregressive prefix before switching to parallel diffusion decoding for faster diffusion-language generation.
8o5QLlckAN.problem: Unordered diffusion-language decoding commits tokens before directional reasoning context forms, producing poor trajectories, high latency, and rigid schedules.
8o5QLlckAN.method: ZENO restricts early generation to a geometrically expanding prefix window and switches to a fixed block after sufficient context forms. The training-free sampler can optionally use KV caching.
8o5QLlckAN.key_idea: Use geometric prefix expansion to establish directional context before transitioning within the same generation to fixed-block parallel diffusion refinement.
8o5QLlckAN.evidence: Experiments cover six benchmarks and base and instruction-tuned LLaDA and Dream checkpoints, with latency, diffusion-step, accuracy, cache, hyperparameter, and stochastic-seed analyses.
8o5QLlckAN.claimed_gains: ZENO achieves up to 4.3× and 4.0× per-query latency speedups, cuts reverse diffusion steps by up to 78%, and gains up to 12.2 and 12.8 accuracy points on LLaDA and Dream-Instruct.
8o5QLlckAN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the training-free intervention produces substantial speed and accuracy trade-offs and that the evaluation includes useful robustness and failure analyses.
8o5QLlckAN.main_concern: Reviewers most often state that geometric scheduling is not isolated from token-commitment and stopping rules, with Fast-dLLM also missing as a close baseline.

FL79OOhxzf.one_liner: Adds an isotropic rational-pole spectral branch to low-mode neural-operator tables for resolution-independent PDE and lensing surrogates.
FL79OOhxzf.problem: Low-mode lookup-table symbols in spectral neural operators cannot compactly represent rational frequency responses across arbitrary frequencies and grids.
FL79OOhxzf.method: BALANI-NO sums a trainable rational pole branch over isotropic frequency magnitude with a small low-mode table. Few grid-independent coefficients specify the pole branch at all frequencies without favoring a coordinate axis.
FL79OOhxzf.key_idea: Parameterize the global asymptotic Fourier symbol with an isotropic rational pole branch while retaining a small table for low-frequency modes.
FL79OOhxzf.evidence: Ten parameter-matched baselines with seven seeds each are evaluated on Darcy flow, Navier–Stokes, gravitational lensing, cosmological density maps, and geomagnetic survey data, including branch ablations.
FL79OOhxzf.claimed_gains: On Darcy, BALANI-NO achieves zero-shot error 0.1194 versus 0.1300 for FNO.
FL79OOhxzf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the physically motivated rational inductive bias and especially the parameter-matched, multi-seed empirical protocol with real-data and ablation experiments.
FL79OOhxzf.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the experiments validate the mechanism, citing missing analytic-oracle comparisons and cases where both branches are not necessary.

mdqDB878Qk.one_liner: Filters shared-memory claims by distinct-user support and resolves contradictions with a provenance-aware knowledge graph.
mdqDB878Qk.problem: Sybil accounts can dominate retrieval from multi-user agent memory while content-level defenses cannot distinguish adversarial claims from honest paraphrases.
mdqDB878Qk.method: CrowdRAG first removes claims lacking support from enough distinct users, then uses a provenance-aware knowledge graph to resolve remaining contradictions. It also characterizes when honest contributor density is insufficient for any support threshold to separate Sybils.
mdqDB878Qk.key_idea: Count independent contributors across the full memory pool as a provenance signal before retrieval, then arbitrate surviving contradictions with provenance-aware relations.
mdqDB878Qk.evidence: Experiments vary three LLMs, four retrievers, Sybil corruption, and label-free similarity calibration, and analyze the density cliff separating defensible and indefensible topics.
mdqDB878Qk.claimed_gains: With three Sybil accounts and GPT-5.4, CrowdRAG reduces attack success from 63.6% to 1.3% at 96.1% accuracy, and attack success stays at or below 3.9% across three LLMs.
mdqDB878Qk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinct-user support is a useful orthogonal defense signal for a consequential shared-memory threat and that the density-cliff analysis clarifies its limits.
mdqDB878Qk.main_concern: Reviewers question whether source support reliably implies factual correctness and whether semantic extraction and canonicalization preserve the defense’s stated guarantees.

7lWUDLZrY2.one_liner: Corrects finite-iterate value risk using joint curvature terms and characterizes when the correction aids estimator selection.
7lWUDLZrY2.problem: Repeated Bellman updates can fit finite data more closely without improving true value estimates, and omitted uncertainty corrections can distort selection risk.
7lWUDLZrY2.method: The paper derives a same-data risk score incorporating joint reward, transition, and Gram-matrix uncertainty, with local conditioning and an ill-conditioning fallback for iid transitions. A one-state analysis characterizes when the correction’s downward shift helps or harms selection.
7lWUDLZrY2.key_idea: Estimate finite-iterate risk by jointly correcting mean and variance terms induced by reward, transition, and Gram-matrix uncertainty.
7lWUDLZrY2.evidence: Matched experiments cover 19,800 independent datasets, including 7,200 iid datasets with overlapping features, using ridge and checkpoint tournaments, paired intervals, and independent pilots.
7lWUDLZrY2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the joint-uncertainty analysis is careful and exact, distinguishes score calibration from adaptive selection, and openly characterizes limitations.
7lWUDLZrY2.main_concern: Reviewers find the empirical benefit modest and unpredictable, while the explicit help-harm characterization is restricted to one-state problems.

MxC62fgC2a.one_liner: Pretrains action representations on human manipulation, then freezes them for compact task-conditioned dexterous action generation.
MxC62fgC2a.problem: Scarce robot demonstrations must simultaneously teach action representations and task-conditioned distributions, limiting complex dexterous action generation.
MxC62fgC2a.method: ARPG pretrains an action representation encoder on large-scale human manipulation data and freezes it. A compact 130M-parameter generative backbone then learns task-conditioned action distributions in that representation space.
MxC62fgC2a.key_idea: Decouple human-data action representation pretraining from downstream robot-conditioned generative policy learning through a frozen encoder.
MxC62fgC2a.evidence: Experiments cover DexJoCo, bimanual dexterous manipulation, human-data scaling, simulation and physical tasks, and controlled representation comparisons.
MxC62fgC2a.claimed_gains: ARPG improves average bimanual dexterous-manipulation success from 10.1% for π0.5 to 45.3%.
MxC62fgC2a.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decoupling representation learning from generation is a clean way to exploit human data and that simulation, real-robot, and representation-ablation results are promising.
MxC62fgC2a.main_concern: Reviewers request stronger scaling and robot-data-efficiency analyses and matched execution comparisons to separate representation gains from action-chunk guidance.

MsqBCJeXIT.one_liner: Uses an LLM to select and configure stateful numerical methods while shared history supports derivative-free optimization.
MsqBCJeXIT.problem: Budget-limited derivative-free optimization must exploit accumulated observations to choose informative evaluations when derivatives and cheap objectives are unavailable.
MsqBCJeXIT.method: NextEval gives an LLM agent tools for analyzing evaluations and executing numerical methods while numerical routines compute most candidates. Shared evaluation history and method-specific state preserve progress across method switches as the agent allocates budget.
MsqBCJeXIT.key_idea: Use an LLM as a strategic controller over stateful numerical optimizers, retaining shared observations and continuation state across method switches.
MsqBCJeXIT.evidence: The paper introduces an agent-based solver and a benchmark with matched function-evaluation budgets, shared records, suite-level profiles, and a fixed textbook-policy comparator in the same decision space.
MsqBCJeXIT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating strategic LLM control from numerical computation is sensible and that shared history and continuation state make adaptive method composition practical.
MsqBCJeXIT.main_concern: Reviewers most often note that standalone-solver comparisons do not isolate the LLM controller from the numerical toolset, shared state, composition, and restart capabilities.

SxCGa0HDUC.one_liner: Measures information leaked by fusing nature and opponents in robust Markov games using public-history shadow profiles.
SxCGa0HDUC.problem: Fusing nature with a strategic opponent can grant the opponent nature-private information and change robust-safe policy selection.
SxCGa0HDUC.method: The authors construct a public-history shadow that preserves the nature plan while removing the opponent’s extra information, separating leakage from plan reselection through a four-value hierarchy. KL divergence to the shadow yields cumulative conditional-mutual-information bounds and a zero-leakage criterion.
SxCGa0HDUC.key_idea: Compare each fused adversary profile with a legal public-history shadow sharing its nature plan to isolate information leakage from stronger continuation reoptimization.
SxCGa0HDUC.evidence: Finite-game, learning, pursuit-evasion, and cyber-defense experiments validate the hierarchy, leakage estimates, public-shadow values, and leakage regularization.
SxCGa0HDUC.claimed_gains: In cyber defense, fusion raises a policy’s worst-case safety cost from 1.244 to 3.000, reversing safe policy selection at threshold 1.4.
SxCGa0HDUC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the information-structure problem is relevant and that the mathematical hierarchy and information-theoretic bounds are generally sound and well developed.
SxCGa0HDUC.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty relative to incomplete-information games and robust optimization and the practical realism of the simplified cyber-defense evaluation.

4kN4XH782a.one_liner: Evaluates multi-turn LLM sycophancy and empathy separately using an adaptive 10-turn conversational simulator and dual-axis rubric.
4kN4XH782a.problem: Single-turn sycophancy benchmarks conflate empathetic acknowledgment with factual capitulation, pushing models toward cold, dismissive responses.
4kN4XH782a.method: FIGS uses an adaptive 10-turn conversational simulator that dynamically challenges target models on realistic multi-turn interactions. An LLM-judge taxonomy scores two separate axes: Sycophancy (holding factual boundaries and proportional praise) and Calibrated Validation (empathetic understanding without capitulation).
4kN4XH782a.key_idea: Separates factual boundary-holding from empathetic validation using a dual-axis rule taxonomy over adaptive 10-turn simulated dialogues.
4kN4XH782a.evidence: Evaluates models and prompt interventions on the 10-turn simulator with inter-annotator kappa checks for judge agreement.
4kN4XH782a.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that disentangling factual boundary-holding from calibrated empathy addresses a key flaw in prior anti-sycophancy benchmarks.
4kN4XH782a.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about heavy reliance on LLM-as-judge without adversarial judge stress tests, unvalidated pass/fail rule-tagging reliability, and confounded prompt style instructions.

jQ3e0r3Dn0.one_liner: Isolates Mixup's first-order regularization kernel without input interpolation via Sombrero Loss on original inputs.
jQ3e0r3Dn0.problem: Mixup entangles input interpolation with stochastic-gradient regularization, making it unclear whether its benefits require mixing inputs.
jQ3e0r3Dn0.method: The authors purify Mixup's first-order gradient structure by removing the input-interpolation residual and realize it on unmixed inputs through Sombrero Loss with paired or independent targets. They prove its expected gradient matches label smoothing while its structured noise covariance shares components with the generalized Gauss-Newton matrix.
jQ3e0r3Dn0.key_idea: Replaces input interpolation with stochastic target-mixing loss (Sombrero Loss) on original inputs, matching Mixup's first-order gradient mean and structured noise.
jQ3e0r3Dn0.evidence: Experiments on CIFAR, ImageNet-1K, object detection, machine translation, and class-imbalanced classification, plus spectral and mean-matched ablations.
jQ3e0r3Dn0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clean mathematical decomposition connecting Mixup's first-order kernel to label smoothing and structured gradient noise.
jQ3e0r3Dn0.main_concern: Reviewers note small accuracy gains within ~1 SD of Mixup, close similarity to stochastic label smoothing (e.g., DisturbLabel), and missing isotropic-noise controls.

ECfSMcJMpb.one_liner: Applies a finite-difference Hessian penalty to per-step conditional predictions in diffusion and flow models for disentangled latents.
ECfSMcJMpb.problem: Applying a Hessian penalty to the complete generative mapping forces additive observation-space behavior and limits nonlinear factor composition.
ECfSMcJMpb.method: Dynamics Hessian Penalty (DHP) penalizes mixed second-order latent derivatives on individual per-step conditional predictions in diffusion and rectified-flow generators. Implemented via stochastic finite differences, it avoids sampler unrolling and inference overhead while allowing nonlinear composition across steps.
ECfSMcJMpb.key_idea: Penalizes mixed latent second derivatives on per-step conditional predictions via stochastic finite differences rather than on the full multi-step generative map.
ECfSMcJMpb.evidence: Evaluated on synthetic disentanglement benchmarks and real-world image datasets for both disentanglement metrics and generation quality.
ECfSMcJMpb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the per-step regularization motivation is clear and avoids sampler unrolling or inference overhead.
ECfSMcJMpb.main_concern: Reviewers point out limited novelty over the original Hessian Penalty (which already used finite differences on intermediate layers) and missing direct global-HP versus DHP comparisons.

vnoEEl7OFK.one_liner: Stabilizes long-sequence on-policy distillation by replacing early high-disagreement student segments with short teacher prefixes.
vnoEEl7OFK.problem: In long-sequence on-policy distillation, early student deviations corrupt subsequent teacher token feedback and destabilize training.
vnoEEl7OFK.method: ATI-OPD detects the earliest high-disagreement segment in a student rollout, replaces it with a short teacher-generated segment, and lets the student resume reasoning from the revised prefix. Persistently divergent suffixes are excluded from the distillation loss while preserving valid continuations.
vnoEEl7OFK.key_idea: Replaces the earliest high-disagreement student prefix segment with a short teacher segment and masks persistently divergent suffixes during on-policy distillation.
vnoEEl7OFK.evidence: Evaluated across five mathematical reasoning benchmarks and two teacher-student pairs (1.5B students) with training-stability diagnostics and ablations.
vnoEEl7OFK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the prefix-divergence instability diagnosis is solid and the empirical diagnostics and ablations are thorough.
vnoEEl7OFK.main_concern: Reviewers note substantial overlap with Relay-OPD, MOTAB, and AC-OPD, small single-seed gains (~1.2 points), and unquantified extra rollout and regeneration costs.

3yV8ieAgU7.one_liner: Computes constructive safety certificates inside multiplayer subgames via linear programming or zero-sum CFR to bound Nash gap growth.
3yV8ieAgU7.problem: Subgame resolving in games with three or more players can increase the Nash gap, unlike in two-player zero-sum games where resolving is provably safe.
3yV8ieAgU7.method: The authors formulate a subgame-only linear program (equivalently a two-player zero-sum gadget solved by CFR) that bounds how much an update can raise the Nash gap, allowing optimization of the safest or most profitable budgeted update. A running ledger tracks bounds across sequential updates by all players.
3yV8ieAgU7.key_idea: Turns subgame safety bounds into an optimization objective solved via a subgame linear program or zero-sum gadget, coordinated across seats by a running ledger.
3yV8ieAgU7.evidence: Supported by theoretical convexity/equivalence proofs and experiments on 3-player Kuhn, 3-player Leduc, and random games with up to six players.
3yV8ieAgU7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that constructive subgame resolving with safety certificates in multiplayer imperfect-information games is an important and practically relevant problem.
3yV8ieAgU7.main_concern: Two reviewers cite poor writing clarity, confusing notation, and insufficient intuition, while another requests clearer differentiation from closely related concurrent work.

KZ07aP94Nx.one_liner: Benchmarks clinician-feedback confounding in bedside data and builds patient knowledge graphs admitted against negative-control action streams.
KZ07aP94Nx.problem: Bedside physiological time series mix patient physiology with clinician treatment policies, causing standard temporal causal estimators to recover spurious or policy-inverted relations.
KZ07aP94Nx.method: The authors introduce ClosedLoopBench (29 sign-fixed relations across 3,442 VitalDB surgical cases with cross-patient negative-control action streams) and propose feedback-robust patient knowledge graphs combining concept nodes, evidence pointers, beat-level couplings, and negative-control calibration.
KZ07aP94Nx.key_idea: Calibrates typed patient knowledge graph relations against cross-patient negative-control action streams to separate physiological responses from clinician feedback policies.
KZ07aP94Nx.evidence: Evaluated on 3,442 VitalDB surgical cases (12,653 hours) comparing 12 temporal estimators and graph construction under null action streams.
KZ07aP94Nx.claimed_gains: Under null streams, feedback-robust graphs yield 0.06–0.10 false concept-level relation instances per graph versus 0.23–2.6 for correlational construction, and capture negative pulse-arrival-time-systolic-pressure slope in 94.3% of 2,884 cases.
KZ07aP94Nx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating clinician feedback policies from physiological responses using negative-control action streams addresses a fundamental, underexplored clinical AI challenge.
KZ07aP94Nx.main_concern: Reviewers note that the framework combines existing statistical and ML methods without a clear methodological innovation, and relies on single-center data and pre-specified sign expectations rather than causal ground truth.

GwmKtqlfQi.one_liner: Analyzes effective surrogate gradients propagated through LIF adjoints and redesigns the adjoint to reduce threshold discontinuity and asymmetry.
GwmKtqlfQi.problem: Smooth symmetric surrogate gradients applied at the spike nonlinearity yield discontinuous, asymmetric effective surrogate gradients (ESGs) after propagating through leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) dynamics.
GwmKtqlfQi.method: The authors analytically characterize the ESG under backpropagation-through-time through complete LIF adjoint dynamics, showing how threshold discontinuity inflates gradient variance and asymmetry biases learning toward non-spiking states.
