They redesign the LIF adjoint directly so the effective gradient has reduced threshold discontinuity and balanced credit assignment.
GwmKtqlfQi.key_idea: Redesigning the LIF adjoint directly shapes the effective surrogate gradient propagated through time rather than modifying only the local spike surrogate function.
GwmKtqlfQi.evidence: Analytical characterization of ESG dynamics and empirical SNN training experiments comparing the redesigned adjoint against conventional adjoints.
GwmKtqlfQi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that shifting focus from local surrogate functions to the effective surrogate gradient propagated through temporal backpropagation is a useful perspective.
GwmKtqlfQi.main_concern: Reviewers note insufficient component ablations for the proposed adjoint design and unclear causal evidence linking synthetic ESG properties to actual training degradation.

f4BHiyrds1.one_liner: Measures SSM recall range under input-dependent timestep gating to predict when added attention layers begin improving recall.
f4BHiyrds1.problem: In hybrid state-space and attention language models, it is unclear which SSM properties determine the query-key distances at which attention becomes necessary for associative recall.
f4BHiyrds1.method: The authors isolate autonomous SSM recall by replacing attention outputs with constants and define the recall range g50. They intervene on input-dependent timestep gating (decay vs. write) in synthetic associative recall and staged hybrids, and test token-aligned gating disruption in jointly pretrained hybrids.
f4BHiyrds1.key_idea: Isolates input-dependent timestep gating's suppression of filler-induced decay to measure autonomous SSM recall range g50, which predicts the onset distance where attention helps.
f4BHiyrds1.evidence: Evaluated on controlled two-key associative recall tasks, staged Mamba-attention hybrids, and pretrained Granite-4.0-h-tiny and Nemotron-H-8B models.
f4BHiyrds1.claimed_gains: Input-dependent timestep gating extends the recall range g50 2.4-fold on a controlled two-key associative task.
f4BHiyrds1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the careful controlled interventions separating decay and write channels of timestep selectivity in SSMs.
f4BHiyrds1.main_concern: Reviewers note that the attention-onset relationship partly follows from its threshold definition and question whether synthetic staged-hybrid findings translate to jointly trained hybrid LLMs.

uHvnva1GJW.one_liner: Trains video autoencoders with temporal predictive objectives and past-conditioned decoding to produce predictable latents for generative world models.
uHvnva1GJW.problem: Standard reconstruction-trained video autoencoders yield latents hard to predict over long horizons, whereas planning-only latents sacrifice pixel reconstruction quality.
uHvnva1GJW.method: The authors pair temporal predictive representation objectives during autoencoder training with a past-conditioned decoder architecture. This produces compact latent spaces where future dynamics are easier to model without sacrificing visual reconstruction fidelity.
uHvnva1GJW.key_idea: Adds temporal predictive objectives to autoencoder training alongside a past-conditioned decoder to balance pixel reconstruction quality with latent dynamics predictability.
uHvnva1GJW.evidence: Controlled study on the Bridge V2 robotics dataset evaluating visual quality, out-of-distribution/long-horizon error, training/inference speed, and VLM-judged policy correlation.
uHvnva1GJW.claimed_gains: Achieves up to 6x lower inference latency, up to 8x faster world-model training at matched perceptual quality, and 15-24% lower OOD and long-horizon pixel/perceptual errors.
uHvnva1GJW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled comparisons at matched reconstruction quality clearly show substantial world-model training and inference speedups.
uHvnva1GJW.main_concern: Reviewers note evaluation is limited to a single robotics dataset (Bridge V2) and framewise image encoders without testing temporally compressed video VAEs.

TdowtEYAl1.one_liner: Combines per-class logits and normalized feature Gaussian fits with classifier-shrunk class references for OOD detection.
TdowtEYAl1.problem: Post-hoc out-of-distribution detectors can invert ID/OOD feature orderings across pretrained models and suffer from unreliable class-relative references under small calibration budgets.
TdowtEYAl1.method: ONE combines raw logits and Gaussian-form feature fits within matching classes before pooling, and estimates class centers by shrinking empirical means toward classifier-weight priors with sample-aware covariance regularization.
TdowtEYAl1.key_idea: Fuses logits and normalized feature Gaussian fits per class before pooling while shrinking empirical class centers toward classifier priors.
TdowtEYAl1.evidence: Evaluated across nine benchmark settings, 30 public ImageNet checkpoints, eight ResNet-50 training recipes, and low-budget calibration settings.
TdowtEYAl1.claimed_gains: Achieves 86.3 mean AUROC across nine benchmark settings with full calibration, and 85.1 mean AUROC with a 6.8-point maximum gap to the best score across 30 ImageNet checkpoints.
TdowtEYAl1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper addresses an important robustness issue across pretrained models and provides a comprehensive empirical evaluation.
TdowtEYAl1.main_concern: Reviewers view the methodological novelty and performance gains as incremental, noting untested large vision-language models and missing FPR discussion where baselines outperform ONE.

BIkr2Yfreg.one_liner: Audits MoE expert-caching replay against live execution to separate inaccurate trace labels from suboptimal caching decisions.
BIkr2Yfreg.problem: Offline behavior traces in Mixture-of-Experts serving can mispredict live expert-cache savings when substitutions alter downstream routing and cache states.
BIkr2Yfreg.method: The paper pairs fixed-token trace replay with live execution under controlled FP32 routers and cache-state swaps, and introduces the Trace-to-Action Audit Protocol (TAP) to verify winning policies and bound decision regret.
BIkr2Yfreg.key_idea: Compares trace replay against matched live MoE execution under controlled routers to distinguish label error from actual caching-policy regret.
BIkr2Yfreg.evidence: Audited Qwen3-MoE, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, and GPT-OSS-20B across fixed-route and cache-substitution runs.
BIkr2Yfreg.claimed_gains: In FP32 Qwen runs, replay and execution select different layer windows on 9 of 40 requests; correcting costs where routes differ leaves 3 of 32 choices suboptimal within 1% of native loads.
BIkr2Yfreg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the importance of validating offline trace replay against live execution in MoE serving.
BIkr2Yfreg.main_concern: Dense jargon makes the paper very difficult to follow, while methodological novelty over prior router-mismatch work and practical regret impact are modest.

bJyyykt27o.one_liner: Replaces sequential backpropagation in deep GNNs with learned Kronecker-aligned feature-feedback matrices to fix vanishing gradients.
bJyyykt27o.problem: Deep message-passing GNNs suffer from vanishing backward gradients that stall parameter updates even when forward hidden states remain informative.
bJyyykt27o.method: KAFT exploits the Kronecker structure of graph-convolution Jacobians to send graph-aware feedback directly to hidden layers using a capped forward-graph operator and learned feature-feedback matrices aligned to downstream probe targets, leaving forward inference unchanged.
bJyyykt27o.key_idea: Delivers direct layerwise supervision in deep GNNs via Kronecker-structured graph-convolution feedback aligned to propagated probe targets.
bJyyykt27o.evidence: Supported by PSD alignment and convergence theory plus experiments across four node-classification datasets, four backbones, two depths, and three learning settings.
bJyyykt27o.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the focus on backward credit assignment and the Kronecker-structured feedback alignment formulation.
bJyyykt27o.main_concern: Vanishing gradients in deep GNNs are already well studied, diagnostic tables have missing entries, and evaluations omit long-range benchmarks and focus on shallow depths like L=6.

10qVsNBQWC.one_liner: Measuring native phone execution, energy, latency, and API cost reveals how agent harnesses shape hybrid mobile GUI performance.
10qVsNBQWC.problem: Cloud-only mobile agents raise privacy and API-cost concerns, while existing evaluations miss how device-cloud control policies affect realized capability and deployment cost.
10qVsNBQWC.method: Edge Symphony evaluates physical-smartphone agents with native on-device inference and joint Smartness and Cost measurements. It supplies 280 tasks, automated task curation, the local PocketAct harness, and the hybrid RelayAct harness.
10qVsNBQWC.key_idea: The agent harness becomes an explicit evaluation variable controlling model placement, exchanged information, and handoffs alongside task success and deployment cost.
10qVsNBQWC.evidence: The benchmark contains 280 reproducible tasks across 23 applications and six capability categories, with native physical-phone execution and reference local and hybrid harnesses.
10qVsNBQWC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that real on-device execution and measured energy, latency, and API expenditure make the benchmark a useful deployment-oriented resource.
10qVsNBQWC.main_concern: Reviewers most often cite limited evaluation diversity, including small task categories, one phone model, one edge model, and a single remote-model vendor.

wEJDZvEAYr.one_liner: Reading conclusion-specific attention rows preserves token identity and predicts deductive validity better than permutation-invariant graph spectra.
wEJDZvEAYr.problem: Label-free attention-graph summaries discard token identity under joint relabeling, limiting their ability to represent whether a conclusion follows from premises.
wEJDZvEAYr.method: A logistic readout uses a few conclusion-row attention values per head, such as attention directed to premises, without residual-stream access. The paper contrasts this readout with spectral summaries and states a permutation-blindness lemma.
wEJDZvEAYr.key_idea: Identity-preserving conclusion-row features retain which token attends to which, unlike attention Laplacian spectra that remain unchanged under joint token relabeling.
wEJDZvEAYr.evidence: Evaluation covers 13 models up to 27 billion parameters, ProofWriter and other benchmarks, spectral detectors, feature decompositions, and negation-artifact controls.
wEJDZvEAYr.claimed_gains: The readout reaches at least 89% of the hidden-state probe's ProofWriter AUC in every one of the thirteen models and beats LapEigvals on every tested Qwen3-1.7B benchmark.
wEJDZvEAYr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that attention-only validity prediction is interesting and that cross-model comparisons and artifact audits provide useful evidence.
wEJDZvEAYr.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the readout offers a practical advantage over hidden-state probes and whether the experiments isolate permutation blindness as the cause of spectral failure.

RpdKHNrEWZ.one_liner: Joint clip encoding improves gait recognition under domain shift and persistent occlusion by stabilizing features with temporal context.
RpdKHNrEWZ.problem: Frame-wise gait encoders defer temporal modeling to downstream heads, leaving unclear when video-native clip representations help recognition.
RpdKHNrEWZ.method: The study compares frame-wise and clip-wise encoding within one video LVM using an identical gait head. It analyzes in-domain and unseen-domain recognition, evolving occlusion patterns, and temporal feature changes before pooling.
RpdKHNrEWZ.key_idea: Clip-wise encoding uses neighboring frames to stabilize visible features and sharpen identity cues before the gait head pools representations.
RpdKHNrEWZ.evidence: Matched experiments examine domain shifts, clothing and lighting changes, partial and persistent body occlusion, and coherent versus randomly fluctuating visibility.
RpdKHNrEWZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the matched analysis addresses an underexplored question and gives useful measurements of when temporal context helps or hurts.
RpdKHNrEWZ.main_concern: Reviewers most often find the evidence narrow because it relies mainly on V-JEPA, with one checkpoint, one gait head, and few benchmarks in the central comparison.

MRsNqeLHtK.one_liner: Rule-grounded wargame campaigns evaluate long-horizon LLM planning through traceable strategy, allocation, execution, and outcome measurements.
MRsNqeLHtK.problem: Strategic-agent evaluation needs complete campaigns that combine delayed outcomes, resource coordination, opponent adaptation, and explicit rules.
MRsNqeLHtK.method: AlameinBench provides three turn-based hex-grid scenarios evaluated from two roles with validated actions and trace-based metrics. Its SAE reference agent links strategic objectives to unit assignments and executable actions through a modular neuro-symbolic design.
MRsNqeLHtK.key_idea: A shared rule-grounded campaign interface connects actions, game-state changes, scenario progress, and terminal outcomes for traceable strategic evaluation.
MRsNqeLHtK.evidence: Fixed-seed evaluation covers six scenario-role conditions, six LLM profiles, four LLM-free heuristic policies, and a rule-based self-play reference.
MRsNqeLHtK.claimed_gains: A deterministic domain-informed heuristic matches or exceeds the best SAE profile in four of six conditions.
MRsNqeLHtK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the wargame tasks are relevant and that linking campaign traces to states and goals helps diagnose planning failures.
MRsNqeLHtK.main_concern: Reviewers most often question whether the benchmark adds validated measures of strategic capability beyond existing wargame benchmarks.

WbuFF4OKRV.one_liner: Uses matched controls and graph constructions to separate regularization reweighting, complementary directions, and coupling in quadratic spectral-feature classification.
WbuFF4OKRV.problem: Agreement of classifier predictions after removing quadratic spectral features is often misread as feature redundancy, ignoring confounding regularization and coefficient-coupling effects.
WbuFF4OKRV.method: The authors design matched controls (Base, Parallel, Decoupled, Full), construct connected graphs where removing complementary quadratic directions leaves full-model predictions unchanged yet decoupling yields perfect classification, and derive signed margin bounds certifying prediction invariance along the coupling path.
WbuFF4OKRV.key_idea: Isolates anisotropic reweighting, complementary quadratic spectral directions, and coefficient coupling via matched controls and signed margin-invariance bounds.
WbuFF4OKRV.evidence: Theoretical impossibility and margin-invariance theorems plus matched experiments on image, citation, and neuronal graphs.
WbuFF4OKRV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers highlight the strong graph counterexample proving identical ablated predictions can hide useful complementary features and the carefully matched experimental controls.
WbuFF4OKRV.main_concern: Exposition is dense, practical gains after independent model selection on real graphs are tiny and mixed, and the theory does not predict when harmful coupling occurs on natural data.

AXuZHJQV9s.one_liner: TTT-SCL improves out-of-distribution supervised causal discovery by generating test-aligned training datasets via score-based graph search at test time.
AXuZHJQV9s.problem: Supervised causal learning models degrade sharply under distribution shifts, real-world data, and unseen combinations of causal mechanisms.
AXuZHJQV9s.method: Test-Time Training for Supervised Causal Learning (TTT-SCL) runs a score-based candidate graph search on each test dataset, fits mechanisms via Structural Intervention Modeling to synthesize aligned training data, and trains a fresh supervised causal learner from scratch.
AXuZHJQV9s.key_idea: Runs score-based graph search and mechanism fitting on each test dataset to synthesize test-aligned training sets for training a fresh supervised causal learner.
AXuZHJQV9s.evidence: Empirical analysis of SCL failure modes plus experiments on synthetic, pseudo-real, and real-world causal discovery datasets.
AXuZHJQV9s.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the paper clearly describes a test-time search-to-learning framework motivated by concrete OOD failures of supervised causal learning.
AXuZHJQV9s.main_concern: Comparisons do not isolate the supervised learner's gain from score-based candidate graph search (voting baselines use different candidate pools), and per-dataset retraining incurs high computational cost.

N6mQXu2qCU.one_liner: Injects Hamiltonian-derived physical side information into fermionic neural wavefunctions via zero-initialized trainable readers without altering the backbone.
N6mQXu2qCU.problem: Prior neural wavefunction methods bake physical knowledge into bespoke architectures, preventing clean separation of physical information value from architectural changes.
N6mQXu2qCU.method: The authors propose a modular side-information interface that computes fixed Hamiltonian-derived physical quantities and injects them into particle features, pair communication, or orbitals of a general fermionic backbone via zero-initialized trainable readers preserving antisymmetry.
N6mQXu2qCU.key_idea: Decouples fixed Hamiltonian-derived physical computations from zero-initialized trainable readers and injection sites while preserving fermionic backbone antisymmetry.
N6mQXu2qCU.evidence: Antisymmetry proofs plus variational Monte Carlo experiments on a 3D unitary attractive Fermi gas and a 2D moire electron system at 10,000 updates.
N6mQXu2qCU.claimed_gains: Lowers 3D Fermi gas backbone energy by 1.82 hbar^2 k_F^2 / m and 2D moire energy by 0.12 to 0.19 E_h* at 10,000 updates.
N6mQXu2qCU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clean modular separation of physical computation, trainable reader, and injection site with exact antisymmetry and neutral initialization.
N6mQXu2qCU.main_concern: Comparisons match update counts rather than wall-clock compute (despite expensive per-proposal physics derivatives), statistical support lacks multi-seed runs, and physics jargon hinders general AI readability.

S4Mqb68xnv.one_liner: StructScope benchmarks LLM structural scope maintenance over long LaTeX documents, testing scope-constrained selection and attribution under nested structures.
S4Mqb68xnv.problem: Existing long-context benchmarks treat document structure as static background rather than testing whether models enforce query-specified structural scope constraints.
S4Mqb68xnv.method: StructScope constructs deterministic, automatically scored tasks from real LaTeX scientific documents across compact parse trees and 12K–90K long-context settings to evaluate scope-constrained selection and nested exclusion.
S4Mqb68xnv.key_idea: Evaluates whether LLMs enforce query-specified structural scope boundaries across compact parse trees versus long-context LaTeX documents using deterministic scoring.
S4Mqb68xnv.evidence: Automated evaluations across multiple LLMs comparing compact parse-only inputs against Skeleton-12K, Skeleton-32K, Skeleton-90K, and full-document settings.
S4Mqb68xnv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize structural scope maintenance as a distinct long-context capability and appreciate the deterministic, LLM-judge-free evaluation pipeline.
S4Mqb68xnv.main_concern: The LaTeX document-structure QA tasks feel artificial and impractical without code/search tools, and nested-scope errors may reflect exhaustive retrieval failures rather than scope reasoning.

KJQOfdoqqI.one_liner: Audits physiological foundation models across four axes—Recover, Stress, Intervene, Verify—to separate provenance decodability from shortcut reliance.
KJQOfdoqqI.problem: Standard OOD transfer tests and provenance probes do not determine whether a fixed physiological classifier actually relies on recording-condition shortcuts or whether removing them preserves utility.
KJQOfdoqqI.method: PhysioTRACE audits frozen physiological encoders through four steps: Recover measures provenance decodability, Stress reverses the provenance-target association on held-out records, Intervene removes a train-localized linear component, and Verify certifies removal only when it outperforms matched random controls within a declared task-utility margin.
KJQOfdoqqI.key_idea: Separates provenance decodability from task-head reliance via association-reversing stress tests and certifies linear erasure only when it beats rank-matched random controls within a utility margin.
KJQOfdoqqI.evidence: Evaluated on paired EEG datasets (with custom and pretrained encoders CBraMod, BIOT, LaBraM) and observational ECG datasets (ECGFounder and CLEF-Small, including LEACE).
KJQOfdoqqI.claimed_gains: Certifies a remedy lowering ECGFounder's excess vulnerability from 0.023 to 0.002 AUROC on observational ECG data.
KJQOfdoqqI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinguishing provenance accessibility from actual downstream reliance is well motivated and backed by careful statistical controls.
KJQOfdoqqI.main_concern: Reviewers note limited methodological novelty since the underlying probing, stress-testing, and linear-erasure components are established, alongside limited pretrained foundation model coverage and unclear presentation.

RPnuhyTcR4.one_liner: Represents uncertain Text-to-SQL intent as explicit SQL decisions and grounded program worlds to validate and clarify result-changing ambiguities.
RPnuhyTcR4.problem: Tool-augmented interactive Text-to-SQL agents rely on free-form reasoning for clarification, leading to redundant questions, low-value database exploration, and silent unsupported SQL assumptions.
RPnuhyTcR4.method: DB-COPE projects uncertain user intent onto explicit SQL decision components and instantiates grounded alternatives as complete SQL program worlds. Structural AST validation checks whether interpretive differences actually change the SQL, triggering user clarification for unresolved result-changing choices and storing confirmed Phase 1 answers in a canonical state for SQL generation.
RPnuhyTcR4.key_idea: Instantiates grounded candidate SQL program worlds and uses AST structural validation to ask clarifications only for unresolved intent choices that alter the query.
RPnuhyTcR4.evidence: Evaluated on the 600-task BIRD-INTERACT Full set with DeepSeek v4-Flash and GPT-5.6 Terra and on PRACTIQ nine-way classification, with ablations and significance tests.
RPnuhyTcR4.claimed_gains: On BIRD-INTERACT Full, raises DeepSeek v4-Flash Phase 1 success from 20.50% to 27.17% and Phase 2 success from 10.67% to 16.67%, increases GPT-5.6 Terra weighted success by 8.93 and 8.83 percentage points, and reaches 87.83% accuracy on PRACTIQ.
RPnuhyTcR4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that grounding ambiguity resolution in explicit SQL decision components and AST-validated candidate worlds is sensible and improves over ReAct across two LLMs.
RPnuhyTcR4.main_concern: Reviewers note missing comparisons against prior interactive/disambiguation Text-to-SQL baselines (only ReAct is compared), weak component ablations, and lack of deterministic verification of final SQL against clarified constraints.

3Hw3MjMyHM.one_liner: Adds a lightweight decoupled module that corrects stale asynchronous VLA action chunks using relative robot and optical-flow environment changes.
3Hw3MjMyHM.problem: Asynchronous execution of action-chunking VLA policies avoids robot pauses but executes chunks conditioned on stale observations without accounting for robot-environment changes during inference.
3Hw3MjMyHM.method: Relative Temporal Alignment (RTA) keeps the base VLA policy frozen and runs a lightweight correction network once per chunk using relative robot-state changes and optical-flow environment changes measured across the inference window. The predicted action residual is applied to align the pending action chunk with the state at inference completion.
3Hw3MjMyHM.key_idea: Predicts per-chunk action residuals from relative robot-state and optical-flow changes during asynchronous VLA inference to align stale chunks with current state.
3Hw3MjMyHM.evidence: Evaluated across two base VLA models in static simulation (LIBERO), dynamic simulation (DOMINO), and real-robot platforms under varying inference delays, reporting 1.16 ms P95 latency.
3Hw3MjMyHM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the decoupled correction module is simple, lightweight (1.16 ms latency, 1.94 MB), and shows clear gains on dynamic simulation tasks.
3Hw3MjMyHM.main_concern: Reviewers question how the correction mechanism works without seeing the original actions or task instructions, note mismatches between training on demonstrations and deployment execution, and warn of fragility to optical-flow noise and nonlinear target motion.

B88R0U1KQP.one_liner: Models normal multivariate time-series windows as the common zero-level set of learned implicit constraints and flags anomalies via constraint violations.
B88R0U1KQP.problem: Reconstruction, forecasting, and prototype-based multivariate time-series anomaly detectors characterize normality indirectly, entangling true anomalies with ordinary modeling uncertainty.
B88R0U1KQP.method: ZERO-AD learns a set of implicit constraint functions F_theta(Z) driven toward zero on normal windows, regularized for complementary Jacobian directions, temporal consistency, and finite-step sensitivity off the zero set. At inference, constraint violations are calibrated on held-out normal data and aggregated via reliability weighting, temporal persistence, and dense-sparse combination without anomalous training samples.
B88R0U1KQP.key_idea: Learns regularized implicit constraint functions whose common zero-level set represents normal time-series windows and scores anomalies directly by calibrated constraint violations.
B88R0U1KQP.evidence: Evaluated on the TSB-AD-M multivariate time-series anomaly detection benchmark with ablations, sensitivity studies, and failure-case analyses.
B88R0U1KQP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that formulating normality as an implicit constraint zero-level set is intuitive and achieves competitive empirical performance on TSB-AD-M.
B88R0U1KQP.main_concern: Reviewers cite high method complexity with five loss terms and unclear hyperparameter selection, mathematical ambiguities in the derivations, and evaluation restricted to TSB-AD-M without univariate datasets.

yXeTUSCljr.one_liner: Applies standard unlearning objectives during language model pretraining to suppress unwanted capabilities and improve resistance to adversarial fine-tuning.
yXeTUSCljr.problem: Post-hoc unlearning of pretrained open-weights LLMs is easily reversed by adversarial fine-tuning, while pretraining data filtering suffers diminishing returns once obvious harmful documents are removed.
yXeTUSCljr.method: The authors integrate standard unlearning algorithms directly into the LLM pretraining loop on retained harmful-proxy data rather than discarding it or applying unlearning after pretraining. They compare pretrain-time unlearning against post-hoc unlearning and further data filtering under token-matched budgets and adversarial fine-tuning attacks.
yXeTUSCljr.key_idea: Executes existing unlearning objectives during pretraining on flagged data to prevent unwanted capabilities from forming rather than removing them post hoc.
yXeTUSCljr.evidence: Empirical token-matched comparisons across model scales and unlearning strengths using Wikipedia Biology articles as the target domain under adversarial fine-tuning.
yXeTUSCljr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that studying unlearning during pretraining for open-weights tamper resistance is timely, clearly written, and supported by controlled budget-matched experiments.
yXeTUSCljr.main_concern: Reviewers point out a mismatch between the safety motivation and using Wikipedia Biology as a proxy for harmful capabilities, missing comparisons to post-training tamper-resistance defenses (TAR, Booster, CTRAP), and limited mechanistic analysis.

USa4hbQ5lF.one_liner: Benchmarks LLM moral consistency across 2,000 matched scenarios elicited as third-person judgments, role-played statements, and tool actions.
USa4hbQ5lF.problem: Aligned LLMs can articulate moral principles in text, yet it is unclear whether their stated ethical judgments remain consistent when executing tool actions in agentic settings.
USa4hbQ5lF.method: The authors construct Should-Say-Do, a benchmark of 2,000 matched scenarios spanning 30 domains covering both moral temptations and ethical dilemmas. Each scenario holds the situation and two alternatives fixed across three independently elicited conditions: third-person judgment (Should), role-assigned stated choice (Say), and tool execution (Do).
USa4hbQ5lF.key_idea: Elicit decisions on identical ethical-conflict scenarios across third-person judgment, first-person text choice, and tool-call execution to measure moral judgment-to-action gaps.
USa4hbQ5lF.evidence: Evaluations of 14 open-weight and commercial LLMs across 2,000 matched scenarios, plus interface, presentation-order, and instruction controls.
USa4hbQ5lF.claimed_gains: Across 14 LLMs, Should-Do differences in reference agreement reach 22.3 percentage points, with the larger gap typically occurring between Say and Do.
USa4hbQ5lF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that testing consistency between stated moral judgments and agentic tool actions is an important alignment question backed by a broad 14-model benchmark.
USa4hbQ5lF.main_concern: Reviewers note that Should, Say, and Do confound moral inconsistency with differences in perspective, information access (tool retrieval vs. direct facts), and response format, and criticize the synthetic binary-choice setup.

WkJDewAAZ8.one_liner: Augments LLMs with a parallel environment-conditioned action encoder that scores typed candidate actions against internal LLM states.
WkJDewAAZ8.problem: Standard LLM agents generate actions as free-form text, making typed decision-making inefficient and non-modular as action spaces grow or change across environments.
WkJDewAAZ8.method: The authors introduce Dyad, which pairs a pretrained LLM with a separate transformer action encoder that embeds candidate action descriptions in parallel and scores them against the LLM's internal state to produce a distribution over typed actions. They evaluate both frozen-LLM modular RL (training only the action encoder) and joint RL post-training.
WkJDewAAZ8.key_idea: Factorize agentic decision-making by embedding candidate action descriptions with a parallel action encoder and scoring them against the LLM's evolving internal state.
WkJDewAAZ8.evidence: In-domain and cross-environment RL evaluations across ALFWorld, WebShop, tau^2-bench, and SWE-bench Verified using multiple model sizes, families, and RL algorithms (GRPO and GiGPO).
WkJDewAAZ8.claimed_gains: Joint optimization achieves a 3.80% average absolute gain on ALFWorld with a 9B model over conventional RL post-training while improving general knowledge, reasoning, and coding.
WkJDewAAZ8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the state-action factorization clean and practically appealing for reusing action embeddings, supported by broad multi-benchmark and transfer evaluations.
WkJDewAAZ8.main_concern: Reviewers note that comparisons do not isolate the factorization from extra pretrained encoder capacity, teacher alignment, and constrained admissible-action selection (lacking a masked fixed-head or constrained-decoding baseline).

BonCTbj9xX.one_liner: Maps genus-0 surfaces via conformal spherical parametrization to apply closed-form rotation-bank polar spline manifold convolutions.
BonCTbj9xX.problem: Manifold convolution methods on curved surfaces either impose restrictive symmetry assumptions for exact equivariance or require expensive local gauge-equivariant differential-geometric computations.
BonCTbj9xX.method: The authors map 2D manifolds onto the unit sphere via a one-time conformal spherical parametrization to leverage closed-form spherical connections, exponential maps, and geodesics. Convolutions apply polar spline kernels across discrete rotational orientation banks, with an error analysis bounding approximate equivariance via conformal distortion and quadrature error.
BonCTbj9xX.key_idea: Use a conformal spherical parametrization with closed-form spherical geometry and discrete rotation-bank polar spline kernels to define approximately equivariant surface convolutions.
BonCTbj9xX.evidence: Theoretical approximate-equivariance error bounds and synthetic surface-deformation experiments.
BonCTbj9xX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simplicity of using closed-form spherical geometry after a one-time parametrization, the explicit distortion error analysis, and robustness under strong synthetic deformation.
BonCTbj9xX.main_concern: Reviewers point to an inconsistency between the theoretical operator definition (tangent-space pullback) and the implementation (spherical exponential map), strict restriction to low-distortion genus-0 surfaces, and synthetic-only experiments without runtime comparisons.

q1rFpEeUjt.one_liner: Derives sharp recovery thresholds for pairwise self-rewarded softmax updates, proving failure at K>=4 actions despite correct rankings.
q1rFpEeUjt.problem: A policy-dependent evaluator can rank the optimal action first at every interior policy, yet sampled pairwise softmax updates can still converge to a suboptimal action.
q1rFpEeUjt.method: The authors analyze finite softmax policies updated from two independently sampled actions using policy-dependent evaluator score differences under bounded bias standard deviation epsilon and L-Lipschitz bias contrasts. They derive a sharp worst-case recovery threshold Psi_L(Delta), prove almost-sure recovery below it, construct boundary failures for four or more actions, and study balanced-query updates.
q1rFpEeUjt.key_idea: Characterize the sharp worst-case bias threshold Psi_L(Delta) separating almost-sure recovery from suboptimal convergence in pairwise self-rewarded softmax updates, revealing a phase transition at K=4 actions.
q1rFpEeUjt.evidence: Martingale and stochastic-approximation convergence proofs, counterexample constructions, and synthetic parameter-sweep simulations.
q1rFpEeUjt.claimed_gains: Proves almost-sure recovery below Psi_L(Delta) and at the boundary for 2 or 3 actions, while showing sampled pairwise updates can fail at the boundary for 4 or more actions even under everywhere-correct rankings.
q1rFpEeUjt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard the sharp recovery threshold, martingale proof techniques, and complete characterization of the three-versus-four action boundary transition as theoretically interesting.
q1rFpEeUjt.main_concern: Reviewers criticize poor paper organization with excessive emphasis on the boundary corner case, simulations restricted to a single synthetic evaluator family, and lack of empirical comparison with balanced-query updates or realistic models.

kEwT6cNzon.one_liner: Diagnoses next-step continuation failures in multi-step LLM reasoning and mitigates them by explicitly identifying the next computation.
kEwT6cNzon.problem: When a multi-step reasoning chain fails after verified correct intermediate steps, standard evaluations do not separate choosing the wrong next operation from misexecuting the right one.
kEwT6cNzon.method: The authors construct controlled serial reasoning tasks with a unique correct next step to test whether models holding a correct intermediate result resume from the wrong step (repeating, skipping, or branching). They test explicit next-step or remaining-computation pointers alongside training and internal-state interventions across multiple model families.
kEwT6cNzon.key_idea: Isolate continuation-selection errors from step-execution errors on verified partial reasoning traces and test whether explicit next-operation pointers close the gap.
kEwT6cNzon.evidence: Controlled serial arithmetic and conditional-program continuation experiments, prompt interventions, and matched training and hidden-state probes across multiple LLM families.
kEwT6cNzon.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the carefully controlled experimental tasks that separate next-step selection from execution ability across multiple model families.
kEwT6cNzon.main_concern: Reviewers question practical relevance to real-world reasoning (arithmetic gaps vanish to 99-100% once written continuation is allowed, and tasks are simple on older/smaller models) and find the manuscript dense and difficult to read.

oKgrcqvFqW.one_liner: Builds a web agent around deterministic DOM-to-PageMem summaries, offline site-crawl memory, and multi-step workflow actions.
oKgrcqvFqW.problem: Generalist web agents typically require expensive proprietary reasoning models because existing agent architectures lack selective page observation, persistent site memory, and procedural workflows.
oKgrcqvFqW.method: The authors introduce WebChallenger, built on PageMem—a deterministic hierarchical semantic summary of a page's DOM. Over PageMem, they implement a selective observation pipeline reading only task-relevant sections, an offline-crawled persistent website memory, and reusable multi-step workflow actions that run with off-the-shelf open-weight LLMs without fine-tuning.
oKgrcqvFqW.key_idea: Construct a deterministic hierarchical DOM summary (PageMem) that unifies selective section observation, offline-crawled site memory, and multi-step workflow actions for frozen open-weight LLMs.
oKgrcqvFqW.evidence: Evaluations using off-the-shelf open-weight and proprietary models on WebArena, VisualWebArena, Online-Mind2Web, and WorkArena, with targeted component ablations.
oKgrcqvFqW.claimed_gains: Using off-the-shelf open-weight models without fine-tuning, achieves 56.3% on WebArena, 48.7% on VisualWebArena, 51.0% on Online-Mind2Web, and 70.9% on WorkArena.
oKgrcqvFqW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the unified PageMem interface, strong practical scores across simulated, live, and enterprise web benchmarks, and detailed component ablations.
oKgrcqvFqW.main_concern: Reviewers question fairness of harness comparisons due to mismatched step/table/inference budgets across baselines and doubt how one-time offline whole-site crawling scales to dynamic real-world websites.

NtvUJZrh6o.one_liner: Trains LLM agents with progressive, partial-rollout user and tool noise injection to improve robustness to imperfect environments.
NtvUJZrh6o.problem: LLM agents trained in idealized, deterministic benchmarks degrade sharply in real-world deployments with ambiguous user interactions and failing or anomalous tools.
NtvUJZrh6o.method: The authors propose NoisyAgent, an agentic RL framework that injects simulated user noise (interaction ambiguity and variability) and tool noise (execution failures and anomalies) into a subset of training rollouts. Noise difficulty is progressively scheduled as the policy adapts, keeping clean and noisy rollouts balanced during optimization.
NtvUJZrh6o.key_idea: Inject progressively harder simulated user and tool perturbations into a controlled fraction of agentic RL rollouts while retaining clean rollouts for training stability.
NtvUJZrh6o.evidence: Multi-domain, multi-scale agentic RL experiments comparing NoisyAgent against clean-training baselines and ablations on noisy and clean benchmarks.
NtvUJZrh6o.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that training agents explicitly under imperfect user and tool interactions is practically motivated, simple, and yields consistent gains across tested domains and scales.
NtvUJZrh6o.main_concern: Reviewers flag underspecified noise-severity definitions and curriculum scheduling rules, weak single-run statistical evidence for ~1-point gains, and close overlap between injected training noise and test-benchmark noise categories.

7Eg59Tnzr0.one_liner: Tracks intermediate transformer residual states against an empirical bank of final states to characterize non-linear convergence geometry.
7Eg59Tnzr0.problem: How intermediate residual states in transformer language models progressively distinguish their eventual final state from competing alternatives across layers is not well characterized.
7Eg59Tnzr0.method: The authors compare intermediate residual states against their own final state and a bank of final states from other contexts across six pretrained LLMs, tracking shrinking competitor sets, directional alignment, and Euclidean distance. They introduce a high-dimensional geometric model separating norm, alignment, and endpoint geometry, and prove that straight-line convergence cannot admit new competitors under Euclidean or cosine distance.
7Eg59Tnzr0.key_idea: Measure the competitor set of alternative final states closer to each intermediate residual state and use a straight-path nestedness theorem to prove non-straight-line convergence in residual streams.
7Eg59Tnzr0.evidence: Geometric measurements across six pretrained language models, a high-dimensional analytical model, and the straight-path nestedness proof.
7Eg59Tnzr0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the methodology sound, the writing clear without overclaiming, and the straight-line-convergence nestedness proposition a clean analytical tool.
7Eg59Tnzr0.main_concern: Reviewers view the central hypothesis as descriptive or near-tautological (competitor sets shrink to size 1 by construction) and note the lack of causal or interventional experiments showing functional impact on predictions.

dPWpXPLvQS.one_liner: Decomposes likelihood-based zero-shot text detector scores into entropy and KL terms to show decoding truncation outweighs model identity.
dPWpXPLvQS.problem: Likelihood-based zero-shot machine-text detectors conflate who generated a text with how it was sampled, causing severe failures when decoding strategies change.
dPWpXPLvQS.method: The authors measure how top-k/top-p truncation and six other decoding settings shift liketropy and four other zero-shot detectors across six evaluator LLMs (up to 32B) and eight domains. They derive an expected-score decomposition for log-likelihood detectors into an entropy-based configuration term and a KL-divergence identity term.
dPWpXPLvQS.key_idea: Decompose expected log-likelihood detector scores into a sampling-sensitive entropy term and a generator-evaluator KL term to explain why decoding truncation dominates zero-shot attribution.
dPWpXPLvQS.evidence: Controlled decoding-sweep experiments across six evaluator LLMs up to 32B parameters, eight text domains, five zero-shot detectors, and a supervised classifier comparison.
dPWpXPLvQS.claimed_gains: Applying top-k/top-p truncation moves an evaluator's liketropy score ~2x farther than switching LLMs and >10x farther than switching to a human; calibrated at 95% acceptance on raw samples, liketropy rejects 78% of its own truncated text while accepting 88% of human text; switching to full-vocabulary sampling drops detector AUROCs from up to 0.99 to chance or below.
dPWpXPLvQS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the decoding-sensitivity robustness issue is practical and systematically demonstrated across multiple models, domains, and truncation settings.
dPWpXPLvQS.main_concern: Reviewers argue the entropy-versus-KL decomposition does not truly disentangle decoding from model identity (e.g., instruction tuning alters entropy), view the contribution as incremental over prior decoding-sensitivity and entropy-KL work, and note raw full-vocabulary sampling is atypical in deployment.

JW0CDqPnCy.one_liner: Introduces a multi-user smart-home benchmark and aligns LLM agents via observation-bounded resident judges weighted by global need.
JW0CDqPnCy.problem: Smart-home LLM agents operate in shared spaces with conflicting resident preferences, permissions, and partial observations, which single-user benchmarks and alignment methods fail to address.
JW0CDqPnCy.method: The authors build MUSE-Home, an executable benchmark of 6,790 training and 721 audited OOD test instances covering multi-user conflict, socially conditioned proactivity, cross-resident forensics, and avoiding unnecessary coordination. They also propose MUSE-Align, which combines observation-bounded resident judgments with full-context global need weights to select SFT/RL tasks and supply soft GRPO rewards.
JW0CDqPnCy.key_idea: Aggregate observation-bounded per-resident judge scores using full-context global need weights to filter training tasks and provide soft GRPO rewards for multi-user smart-home agents.
JW0CDqPnCy.evidence: Audited OOD benchmark evaluations across multiple LLMs, memory/history ablations, and SFT and GRPO fine-tuning experiments on Qwen3-4B.
JW0CDqPnCy.claimed_gains: The best evaluated model achieves 45.35% task success on MUSE-Home; MUSE-Align improves Qwen3-4B from 26.63% to 31.35% under SFT and from 20.39% to 38.56% under GRPO.
JW0CDqPnCy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the reframing to multi-user shared-environment decisions, the disciplined dual-annotator test audit, and evidence that removing resident memory/history drops performance by 24.13 points.
JW0CDqPnCy.main_concern: Reviewers note the lack of scaling analysis over household size or context volume to distinguish multi-user reasoning from generic context removal, and criticize rigid predefined target states that mark reasonable alternative compromises wrong.

Ud46lixxF9.one_liner: Proves how higher-order time-series cumulants enter fitted echo-state network readouts order by order as a function of input scaling.
Ud46lixxF9.problem: Representing time series by the weights of a fitted forecasting model is widely used in model-space learning, yet what distributional statistics such readouts retain and their sampling cost are poorly understood.
Ud46lixxF9.method: The authors analyze ridge readouts of fixed random echo-state networks fitted to scalar time series, proving that linear terms capture autocovariance while higher-order moments of order 2k+2 enter at order lambda^(2k+1) in input scale lambda via joint cumulants. For bounded moving averages, they establish a local Gaussian limit at scale lambda^(4k) L and a classifier error lower bound attained by population LDA.
Ud46lixxF9.key_idea: Characterize the graded order-by-order entry of higher-order cumulants into fitted echo-state network ridge readouts as powers of input scale lambda and derive the resulting lambda^(4k) L trajectory-length scaling.
Ud46lixxF9.evidence: Asymptotic population-readout and local-Gaussian-limit proofs, classifier error lower bounds, and synthetic time-series validation experiments.
Ud46lixxF9.claimed_gains: Proves that once lower-order moments match, differences of order 2k+2 enter at order lambda^(2k+1) in input scale and require trajectory length governed by lambda^(4k) L to detect.
Ud46lixxF9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard the theoretical characterization of what fitted ESN readouts represent and their higher-order sampling complexity as an original, mathematically sound analysis.
Ud46lixxF9.main_concern: Reviewers cite poor exposition clarity, restrictive assumptions (small input scaling and univariate linear processes that mismatch practical regimes), and unclear distinction from general fixed nonlinear feature regression.

GLl9HBBORy.one_liner: Organizes tools into a capability hierarchy for on-demand discovery and recursive task decomposition in long-horizon agents.
GLl9HBBORy.problem: Single-chain reasoning agents fail on long-horizon tasks as growing histories obscure dependencies, while injecting large flat tool libraries overwhelms context and impairs retrieval.
GLl9HBBORy.method: TaReD organizes tools by functional relationships into a hierarchy of capabilities. During execution, the agent discovers tools on demand and uses this hierarchy to recursively decompose tasks into a subtask tree aligned with stage-specific capabilities.
GLl9HBBORy.key_idea: Organizes tools into a functional capability hierarchy so the agent discovers tools on demand and recursively aligns subtask tree levels with available capabilities.
GLl9HBBORy.evidence: Evaluated on complex real-world tasks with ablation studies comparing hierarchical discovery against fixed subsets, full tool injection, and expandable flat subsets.
GLl9HBBORy.claimed_gains: Improves end-to-end task success rate by up to 40 percentage points over compared baselines.
GLl9HBBORy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that connecting on-demand hierarchical tool discovery to task decomposition is a coherent, practically relevant design for large API catalogs, supported by useful ablations.
GLl9HBBORy.main_concern: Reviewers note that the benefit over related hierarchical systems like CUGA is not established, the static taxonomy may misguide decomposition, and ablations do not isolate recursion from curated node summaries.
